$schema_note: RetroForge ticket board. Fields: id, title, phase (roadmap phase), crate (primary write scope), write_scope (globs the executor may touch), depends_on (ticket ids), acceptance (ALL must pass before status=done), points (fibonacci), status (todo|in_progress|done|blocked), notes (OPTIONAL array of strings, append-only: HANDOFF:/BLOCKED: entries). ALWAYS-WRITABLE SET (in addition to write_scope, for every ticket): this file's own-ticket status+notes fields; docs/STATUS.md (append one line per merged ticket); Cargo.lock; docs/TECH_STACK.md section-2 rows (new-dependency decision record). Claim rule: a ticket is claimable when all depends_on are done. Executors: work ONE ticket per session, run `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace && scripts/validate-arch.sh` plus ticket acceptance before marking done. Never widen write_scope beyond the always-writable set without a HANDOFF note in the ticket's notes array.

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-03 (conductor). All four acceptance criteria verified INDEPENDENTLY (RF-L-08): full seven-command gate re-run by the conductor, all exit 0, 213 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored with vectors absent. THE SEAM HELD — verified structurally, not on the agent's word: `master_cycle` is mutated only inside crates/rf-nes/src/system/mod.rs (CpuBus::read, CpuBus::write, run_oam_dma), and `grep -rn 'stall|dma' crates/rf-nes/src/cpu/` returns NOTHING, so the CPU has no knowledge of DMA at all. W1-02 was therefore an addition, not the rewrite the risk note feared. OAM DMA cycle counts re-derived by the conductor against nesdev: 1 dummy + (0 or 1) alignment + 256 get/put pairs (512) = 513/514, and the tests assert master_cycle parity as an explicit PRECONDITION before triggering, so neither branch can silently be exercised twice.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): the DMC/OAM-DMA seam flagged in HANDOFF resolves in favour of the current design, and EMULATION_CORES.md section 1 is the authority: 'CPU is the master clock. Each chip keeps its own cycle counter; when the CPU touches a register another chip owns, that chip runs catch_up(to_master_cycle) first.' So the master cycle counter must live in the SYSTEM BUS and be advanced inside CpuBus::read/write (one tick per bus op), NEVER by summing Cpu::step's u32 return afterwards. Only then do bus-inserted stall cycles (OAM DMA's 513/514, later DMC) land in the master clock for free, and the $2007/$4016 RDY double-read glitch becomes expressible as the bus performing the read twice internally and returning the second value. If the executor finds itself needing to add DMA cycles to step()'s return value, that is the signal the seam did NOT hold — stop and escalate rather than papering over it.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): rf-nes has NO dependency on rf-cart today and must add one (path dep; permitted — validate-arch.sh rule 1 forbids only upper-layer crates and rf-cart is a peer core crate, rule 3 exempts rf-nes). Note rf-cart exposes cartridge METADATA only: `Cartridge::load(&[u8]) -> Result<Cartridge, CartError>` yielding `Cartridge::Nes { header: NesHeader, identity: RomIdentity }`, where NesHeader carries format/mapper/submapper/prg_rom_size/chr_rom_size/prg_ram_size/mirroring/battery/trainer — but NOT the PRG/CHR bytes. rf-nes must slice those out of the raw image itself (16-byte header + optional 512-byte trainer offset). rf-cart is outside this ticket's write scope, so do not 'fix' it there.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): crates/rf-nes/Cargo.toml's description and src/lib.rs's module doc both claim rf-nes 'consumes rf-core-api only'. That is already inaccurate (there is no rf-core-api dependency either) and adding rf-cart makes it more so — update both in this ticket (they are in scope) rather than leaving an R-15 stale-comment.

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-03 (conductor). Both acceptance criteria verified INDEPENDENTLY (RF-L-08): full seven-command gate re-run, all exit 0, 238 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. Result is FULL-LINE byte-exact 8991/8991 — the disassembly column (FR-DBG-003) as well as PC/A/X/Y/P/SP/CYC (FR-CORE-021), not the register-columns-only fallback the brief permitted. ANTI-TAMPER PROOF (the check that matters, since a comparison that passes vacuously looks identical to one that works): the conductor corrupted the A: register on line 5001 of a copy of the golden log and re-ran — the suite reported exactly '8990 matched, 1 mismatched, first divergence at line 5001' and FAILED. The diff is real and byte-exact, not a loosened comparison. Evidence now covers 2 Tier-A-local suites (nes6502 2,560,000 cases + nestest 8991 lines).

SCRUTINIZED 2026-08-03 (conductor): the agent's one semantic judgment call — hardcoding $FF in NesBus::peek for the APU stub range so the disassembly annotation matches — was checked against the real log rather than accepted. It holds: all five golden lines ($4004-$4007, $4015) show '= FF' while the accumulator on those same lines holds 02/3F/9A/FF/00, so an open-bus latch cannot explain a constant FF. The fix is also correctly scoped — `peek` is side-effect-free and used ONLY for the trace annotation; `read_untimed`, the real emulation path, keeps its true open-bus latch and is unchanged. Not a fudge to force a match.

FLAKE FIXED 2026-08-03 (conductor): the agent honestly reported two one-off non-reproducible test flakes. They were a real race, not noise: three copies of a `tempdir()` helper (fetch.rs, nes6502_evidence.rs, nestest_evidence.rs) keyed the directory on `process::id() + SystemTime nanos`, but libtest runs a binary's tests in PARALLEL THREADS sharing one pid, so two threads in the same clock tick get the same path and one test's cleanup deletes the other's working directory. Added an AtomicU64 sequence to all three; 3 consecutive rf-harness runs green (82 passed each). Left in place because an intermittently-red gate corrodes the entire independent-verification discipline this project runs on.

SCOPE-ADD 2026-08-03 (conductor): nestest's ROM and golden log are fetched, gitignored artifacts (NFR-006), so like the nes6502 vectors this suite CANNOT run in CI and `cargo test --workspace` must pass when they are absent. That makes it the second Tier-A-local suite and exactly what W0-07's evidence gate exists for — without an evidence row, a passing nestest is invisible to CI and unverifiable. Added the four exact paths needed to register it (scripts/local-gate.sh, scripts/validate-evidence.mjs, docs/evidence/local-gate.json, docs/TESTING.md) rather than widening to scripts/** or docs/**. CI still never fetches anything (HP-4: Brad is GitHub-Actions-constrained).

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor, verified against the real fetched log): nestest.log is 8991 lines and CRLF-terminated — strip the trailing \r or every single line diff fails. The register block begins at byte offset 48; the disassembly field is columns 0..47, space-padded. First line is `C000  4C F5 C5  JMP $C5F5` with A:00 X:00 Y:00 P:24 SP:FD PPU:  0, 21 CYC:7 — i.e. the trace starts AFTER a 7-cycle reset, which is why this ticket must build the reset sequence W1-02 deferred. PPU column format is `PPU:%3d,%3d` (space-padded, e.g. 'PPU:  0, 21' and 'PPU:233,209').

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): THE PPU COLUMN NEEDS NO PPU. Verified arithmetically over all 8991 lines with ZERO mismatches: scanline == (CYC*3)//341 and dot == (CYC*3)%341, exactly. So the trace logger can emit a byte-exact PPU column from the CPU cycle count alone. Do NOT build or stub a PPU to satisfy it — the PPU is W1-04a, and this holds only because nestest's automated mode leaves rendering disabled (no odd-frame skipped dot).

HANDOFF 2026-08-03 (conductor, from W1-02): W1-02 deliberately did NOT build a reset sequence — `NesBus::new` starts `master_cycle` at 0 and W1-02's tests set `cpu.pc` directly. Two consequences this ticket must absorb, both already documented in crates/rf-nes/src/system/mod.rs's `run_oam_dma` doc: (1) nestest's $C000 entry needs a real reset/power-on sequence (reset vector fetch, correct initial SP/P, and the 7-cycle reset timing) or the CYC column will be offset from the golden log from the first line; (2) until that sequence anchors the master-clock PHASE to hardware, OAM DMA's get/put parity is an internal bookkeeping convention rather than a hardware-true absolute — so a real ROM's DMA cost can differ from the model by exactly one cycle. Scoping the reset sequence into this ticket is the intended fix. Both are honest documented deferrals, not defects.

CONDUCTOR RE-DERIVED THE FIX INDEPENDENTLY from nesdev's second-write bit layout (t: FGH..AB CDE..... <- d: ABCDEFGH => keep only coarse X bits 0-4 and nametable bits 10-11): 0x8C1F, matching the agent's fix exactly, and confirmed 0x8FFF provably leaves bits 5-9 set.

THE GOLDEN IS ANALYTIC, NOT RECORDED — expected_pixel(x,y) is a closed-form formula (tile_index = row*37 + col*7 + 11 mod 256; conductor verified gcd(37,256)=gcd(7,256)=1 so no row or column aliases) and the file contains ZERO 64-hex-char hash constants. Original wording demanded all 6 and 10/10; that bundling was a spec error discovered by the work, not a target that was missed.

nes6502 vectors still 2,560,000/2,560,000 and nestest still 8991/8991 byte-exact — these are the guardrails on a change to when CountingBus samples nmi_line() relative to NesBus::tick_master's 3-dot batching, and a regression in either is a stop, not a re-baseline
the OAM DMA master-clock seam still holds: master_cycle mutated only inside crates/rf-nes/src/system, and no DMA/stall reference appears in crates/rf-nes/src/cpu
crate::ppu's module doc section 'A sub-CPU-cycle timing ceiling this module does NOT reach' is deleted or rewritten to describe what was actually achieved
notes: ORIGIN 2026-08-03 (Brad's ruling, raised by the conductor at W1-05b's close): W1-05b delivered sprite_hit 11/11 but ppu_vbl_nmi only 4/10. The cause is architectural, diagnosed against the real fetched ROMs rather than guessed: cpu::exec::CountingBus samples nmi_line() ONCE per whole bus op, and NesBus ticks the PPU's 3 dots strictly after a register read completes, so the sub-CPU-cycle race nesdev's 'VBL Flag Timing' table describes (reading $2002 on the very PPU clock the flag is set) is unreachable. The one-clock-EARLY case is reachable and already implemented; the same-clock case is not. Five of the six failures show one identical signature — a suppression boundary exactly one CPU cycle / 3 PPU dots early — cross-checked against a matching independently-reported symptom at forums.nesdev.org/viewtopic.php?t=17682, which is strong evidence of one shared root cause rather than six bugs. 10-even_odd_timing fails separately at a $2001-write-timing sub-test and was deliberately NOT claimed to share that root cause.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN TICKET, not a W1-05b fix: the change is CPU-crate-adjacent and lands on the exact seam W1-02 established and W1-04a improved (master clock in the bus, single tick_master mutation site, zero PPU/DMA awareness in cpu/). Its blast radius is the 2,560,000-case nes6502 vector suite and the byte-exact 8991-line nestest trace. It needs to be scoped and gated deliberately with those two suites as guardrails — not attempted as an unscoped widening at the end of another ticket.

MECHANICAL NOTE: the six waivers in crates/rf-harness/waivers.toml name THIS ticket and rf_harness::accuracy::build_report refuses to build a report whose waiver names a non-open ticket — verified empirically 2026-08-03 by temporarily closing W1-05b, which made scripts/local-gate.sh fail with 'waiver for ppu_vbl_nmi/02-vbl_set_time names ticket W1-05b, which is not open'. So this ticket cannot be closed by waiving harder: closing it REQUIRES deleting those waivers, which requires the ROMs actually passing. Waiver expiry is 2026-11-01 — if this ticket is still open then, the gate goes red on its own.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor) — THE TWO HEADLINE GUARDRAILS ARE STRUCTURALLY IMMUNE TO THIS CHANGE, which is the single most useful fact established about this ticket and materially lowers its risk from how notes [1] and the HANDOFF describe it. (a) nestest's byte-exactness does NOT depend on the real PPU at all: crates/rf-nes/src/trace.rs's ppu_columns() derives the PPU:SSS,DDD columns arithmetically as (master_cycle*3/341, master_cycle*3%341) — its module doc says so outright ('The PPU column needs no PPU', ticket W1-03 pre-flight). (b) the 2,560,000-case nes6502 vector suite runs against RecordingBus, its own mock CpuBus in cpu/tests/vectors.rs — there is no NesBus and no PPU anywhere in it. THEREFORE: re-sequencing register access relative to tick_master's 3-dot batch cannot perturb either suite, PROVIDED master_cycle still advances exactly once per bus op. That proviso is the load-bearing invariant — split only the dot loop, never make master_cycle sub-cycle. This is an argument, not a measurement: run both suites anyway and treat a regression as a stop.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor) — THE RISK MOVED, IT DID NOT VANISH. The real blast radius is the in-crate PPU suite, whose expectations were all written under the current access-before-dots ordering: ppu/tests/read_buffer.rs ($2007 delayed-read buffer), scroll_registers.rs ($2005/$2006 write ordering), frame_timing.rs, sink_emission.rs, nmi.rs, fetch_pipeline.rs, plus golden_frame_bg/golden_frame_sprites (W1-04b's analytic golden frame drives the real PPU through real register writes) and sprite_hit_tests 11/11 (dot-sensitive). The predictable failure mode is a re-baseline wearing a different hat: flip the ordering, watch a dozen PPU tests go red, edit their expected values until green. Every failing test must be triaged INDIVIDUALLY against the nesdev source its own doc comment cites, and any changed expectation must gain a sentence saying why hardware says the new value. An expectation that changes with no such justification means the change is wrong, not the test.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor) — THREE RANKED ROOT-CAUSE CANDIDATES, not one (global rule: never ship the first plausible theory). (1) MOST LIKELY: register access is sequenced BEFORE the cycle's 3 dots — NesBus::read is `read_untimed(addr); tick_master(1)`, so a read observes PPU state as of the END of the previous cycle, while real hardware latches at φ2, within the cycle. This predicts exactly the measured signature: suppression one CPU cycle early. (2) The NMI SAMPLE INSTANT: cpu::exec::CountingBus::sample() runs after the whole bus op completes, i.e. after all 3 dots; hardware samples during φ2. Fixing (1) may leave this still wrong. Prefer fixing it bus-side (latch the NMI level at the right dot inside tick_master and have nmi_line() return that) over restructuring cpu/. (3) read_status's SUPPRESSION MODEL itself: scroll.rs keys on `scanline == VBLANK_START_SCANLINE && dot == 0`, which models exactly ONE row of nesdev's VBL Flag Timing table; that table has several rows (one clock before / same clock / one clock after) with different read-value and suppression combinations. NOTE (1) and (3) ARE TWO HALVES OF ONE MODEL: read_status's dot==0 check only makes sense given access-before-dots, so changing the ordering without reworking the suppression check in lockstep produces partial progress that isn't. THE DISCRIMINATOR: fix and run 02-vbl_set_time FIRST, alone — it measures which CPU cycle the flag reads set, with no NMI involved. 02 passing confirms (1) and exonerates (2); 02 passing while 05/06/07/08 still fail isolates a second cause in the edge-detection path.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor) — 10-even_odd_timing's SYMPTOM POINTS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION and probably does NOT share the root cause; W1-05b already declined to claim it did. The five read-side waivers say suppression fires one cycle EARLY, so the fix moves register access LATER relative to PPU state. But 10 fails at 'Clock is skipped too late, relative to enabling BG' — for that to fire EARLIER, the $2001 write would have to take effect earlier, and it already happens before the cycle's dots. One uniform 'move access after the ticks' shift moves both symptoms the same direction, so it cannot fix both. Check this against the real ROM output EARLY (it is cheap) — it either confirms 10 is a separate cause or refutes the reasoning. If separate, the realistic outcome is 9/10, not 10/10.

IMPLEMENTATION 2026-08-05 (agent): 9/10 achieved -- 02/05/06/07/08 all now pass; 10-even_odd_timing confirmed separate, exactly as predicted. DISCRIMINATOR RESULT: running 02-vbl_set_time alone with ONLY a uniform CpuBus::read ordering swap (hypothesis 1, full tick-then-access) left 02's table byte-identical to baseline -- proven self-canceling empirically, because 02 is a self-referential measurement (sync_vbl's own convergence reads are shifted identically to the deliberate test read, so the reference point and the measurement move together). master_cycle is still mutated only inside crates/rf-nes/src/system and advances exactly once per bus op, and no DMA/stall reference appears in crates/rf-nes/src/cpu
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W1-05c 2026-08-05 (Brad's option-B ruling; see W1-05c's notes for the full history). W1-05c took ppu_vbl_nmi from 4/10 to 9/10 and PROVED this ROM is a separate defect rather than the sixth instance of the one it fixed. ROOT CAUSE: 10-even_odd_timing needs a $2001 mask write to take effect EARLIER relative to the pre-render line's dot-339/340 odd-frame skip decision, while every mechanism W1-05c introduced moves effects LATER -- so no single uniform re-sequencing can satisfy both, which is exactly why one ticket could not close both. DO NOT RETRY BY GLOBALLY RE-SEQUENCING REGISTER ACCESS: measured, not assumed -- both CpuBus::read orderings and every read_status model that fixed the other five leave this ROM failing identically ('Clock is skipped too late, relative to enabling BG', sub-test 3 of 4; 2 and 4 pass). WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED: a model of when a $2001 write lands relative to the odd-frame skip decision -- a write-side timing question, untouched by W1-05c's read-side work. Useful starting points already in the tree: NesBus::write's write_untimed-then-tick_master ordering, and Ppu::process_dot's PRERENDER_SCANLINE arm.

PRE-FLIGHT ALREADY PAID by W1-05c, do not rediscover: (1) the two headline guardrails are STRUCTURALLY immune to sub-cycle re-sequencing -- nestest's PPU columns come from trace.rs's ppu_columns(), an arithmetic function of master_cycle, and the 2.56M vector suite runs on RecordingBus with no PPU -- PROVIDED master_cycle still advances exactly once per bus op. (2) The real blast radius is the in-crate PPU suite (read_buffer, scroll_registers, frame_timing, sink_emission, nmi, fetch_pipeline, both golden frames, sprite_hit_tests), whose expectations encode the current ordering; triage every failure against the nesdev source its doc comment cites and never edit an expectation without a hardware justification. (3) Evidence regeneration is MANDATORY here -- validate-evidence.mjs's coveredPaths include crates/rf-nes/src/{cpu,ppu,system}; commit code first, regenerate via scripts/local-gate.sh on a clean tree, commit evidence second.

CLOSED 2026-08-16. ROOT CAUSE was neither ticket's prediction. The skip decision read PPUMASK with ZERO propagation delay; nesdev.org/wiki/PPU_registers's PPUMASK section says verbatim "Toggling rendering takes effect approximately 3-4 dots after the write. This delay is required by Battletoads to avoid a crash." So nothing needed to land EARLIER (W1-05c's framing, inherited from W1-05b) -- `write_untimed` already runs before its own cycle's dots and was never the problem. The two-dot latch `Ppu::render_enable_pipe` is the whole fix; `crate::ppu`'s module doc corrects the old diagnosis in place rather than leaving it to rot.

MEASURED, NOT SEARCHED (the trap W1-05c fell into was searching over orderings). Fetched blargg's own source (christopherpow/nes-test-roms ppu_vbl_nmi/source/10-even_odd_timing.s + common/sync_vbl.s, scratchpad only, nothing written into the repo): sub-tests 2 and 3 are the SAME test run with sync_vbl_delay A=4 vs A=5, i.e. the BG enable one PPU dot apart, and BOTH expect X=8 -- so hardware skips for the earlier write and not the later one. Instrumented the engine (temporary eprintln on the $2001 write and on the pre-render skip decision, removed before commit): those two writes land at pre-render dots 337 and 338, decision runs after dot 339. Depth 2 is therefore the ONLY value that accepts 337 and rejects 338 -- arithmetic, not tuning.

CORROBORATION that it is a model and not a fitted constant, which matters because a one-parameter fix to a threshold test is exactly the shape of a fudge: (1) sub-tests 4 and 5 -- the DISABLING-BG pair, never reached before because the ROM aborts at first failure, and never consulted while choosing the depth -- pass untouched; (2) the ROM prints `08 08 09 07`, byte-identical to the expected output in its own source header; (3) rf-harness's independent evidence runner (a separate implementation of the $6000 protocol) also reports 10/10.

ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE, seven-command gate all exit 0 (fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, test --workspace, validate-arch.sh, validate-plan.mjs, validate-traceability.mjs, validate-evidence.mjs). workspace: 826 passing / 0 failed / 7 ignored (was 825 at W4-06b close; +1 = the new `enabling_bg_one_dot_too_late_does_not_skip` guard, and the temporary measurement test was deleted, not left behind). Six canaries all unregressed, from the regenerated docs/evidence/local-gate.json: nes6502 2,560,000/2,560,000, nestest 8991/8991 byte-exact, sprite_hit_tests 11/11, ppu_vbl_nmi 10/10 (01-09 unregressed, 10 now passing), golden_frame_bg + golden_frame_sprites green. Accuracy table raw 23/23 pass and effective 23/23 -- the two agree for the first time, because there are now no waived rows at all. Criterion 3 re-checked mechanically: no `master_cycle` mutation outside crates/rf-nes/src/system (grep), and crates/rf-nes/src/cpu's only dma/stall matches are the same four doc-comment mentions W1-05c left.

ONE IN-CRATE TEST CHANGED, and its SETUP was the thing that was wrong -- not its expectation. `frame_timing::odd_frame_with_rendering_enabled_skips_dot_340` poked (261, 339) and enabled rendering in the same breath, which is precisely the case hardware does NOT skip for; it now ticks in from dot 337. The rest of the blast radius W1-05c predicted (read_buffer, scroll_registers, sink_emission, nmi, fetch_pipeline, both golden frames, sprite_hit_tests) did not materialize, because the latch is scoped to the skip decision and does not touch `rendering_enabled` generally.

OPEN REFINEMENT, deliberately not taken: nesdev's 3-4 dot delay applies to rendering toggles generally, not just this decision. Applying it globally is a real accuracy improvement but changes fetch-pipeline behavior that sprite_hit_tests 09/11 and both golden frames currently encode -- no test in this tree measures it there, so it is left as a documented narrowing on `Ppu::render_enable_pipe` rather than guessed at. Anyone widening it must re-verify those, not re-baseline them.

tickets.title: Keyboard input + InputFrame + input log
acceptance: deterministic per-frame latch (FR-FE-003)
replay log records/plays back per docs/design/SAVE_STATES.md §3 (FR-STATE-006)
determinism CI: two runs same input log => identical state hashes (FR-CORE-002, FR-CORE-003)
notes: HANDOFF 2026-08-05 (conductor): write_scope widened by TWO EXACT PATHS, never a glob (Brad's W1-01a ruling). (1) docs/design/SAVE_STATES.md — §3 is a four-line sketch, not a wire spec, exactly as §2 was before W0-05 made it normative; this ticket ships the first .rfreplay writer/reader, so under NFR-008 its field choices become public commitments and must land in the doc in the same commit. Same precedent and same marker style as W0-05's 'normative as of W0-05' table. (2) docs/TESTING.md — §6's 'Double-run' and 'Replay determinism' rows attribute the suite to rf-harness, but this ticket's write_scope is rf-input + retroforge and rf-harness cannot depend on rf-input under scripts/validate-arch.sh reasoning; leaving those rows pointing at the wrong crate is doc drift. Precedent for exact doc paths in a write_scope: W1-05c already carries docs/TESTING.md and docs/evidence/local-gate.json.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor) — ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3 WOULD HAVE PASSED VACUOUSLY. The obvious fixture is stepper.rs's synthetic_nrom (all-zero PRG => reset vector $0000 => BRK forever in zeroed RAM). That ROM NEVER READS $4016, so 'two runs, same input log => identical state hashes' is byte-identically true with the input wiring absent, the keymap broken, or the latch never called — the same shape as the three vacuous tests found in W1-04a/W1-05a. The fixture MUST be a hand-assembled NROM that strobes $4016 (write 1, write 0), reads it 8 times, and stores the assembled byte into WRAM every frame. Criterion 3 needs the anti-vacuity half too: two DIFFERENT logs must produce DIFFERENT hash sequences, plus one positive assertion that a known button byte lands at a known WRAM address. Same discipline as corrupting one line of nestest.log to prove the diff is real.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor): the state hash reachable from this ticket's write_scope is NOT a full-machine hash and must not be named one. rf-nes does not implement rf_core_api::EmulatorCore at all (no save_state/state_view — grep confirms), and serializing NES state is W2-04's job (write_scope rf-nes + rf-state + retroforge, depends_on W0-05 + W2-01b). Reachable today from retroforge: Cpu{a,x,y,s,pc,p,jammed} (public fields), NesBus::oam(), prg_ram(), master_cycle(), frame_count(), and peek() for $0000-$07FF WRAM. PPU internals (VRAM, palette RAM, loopy regs) and APU are NOT reachable. Hash those explicit regions — enumerated, never a 64KB peek sweep, which would drag in constant PRG ROM for nothing — and carry the framebuffer digest as a SEPARATELY NAMED component, because it is output, not state: it proves double-run reproducibility but cannot catch PPU-internal divergence that happens to render identically. Upgrading to a true full-state hash is owed to W2-04.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor): NesBus::set_controller_buttons(index, buttons) already exists (W1-02) — the host-side latch hook this ticket needs is present and rf-nes needs no change. Note the two DIFFERENT latches: the host latch (set_controller_buttons, once per frame, FR-FE-003's 'deterministic per-frame latch') versus the controller's own 1->0 strobe latch (done by the running game, crates/rf-nes/src/system/controller.rs, correct and out of scope). Under scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 3, rf-input MUST NOT depend on rf-nes; it depends on rf-core-api only (for InputFrame) and stays host-agnostic, with the egui::Key -> rf_input::Key table living in crates/retroforge.

FORMAT DECISION 2026-08-05 (conductor), not a new choice — read off three existing commitments: docs/design/CONTRACTS.md §3 'Replays are BK2-shaped (header + per-frame inputs + periodic hashes)', docs/SCOPE.md 'BK2-style input-log replay (.rfreplay)', and docs/research/accuracy-and-testing.md §5, which describes BK2 as UTF-8 with one |-delimited line per frame and a first-line log key and calls it 'excellent model for our input-log format'. So .rfreplay is a SINGLE UTF-8 TEXT FILE (header key=value block + log-key line + per-frame lines + periodic hash lines), NOT a binary TLV like .rfstate and NOT a literal BizHawk zip. Text keeps it diffable, hand-editable for TAS/bug repro, dependency-free, and makes the R-A3/P9 'BizHawk header import (v1)' commitment cheap.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-05 (conductor): scripts/validate-evidence.mjs's coveredPaths table is rf-nes-only (crates/rf-nes/src/{cpu,ppu,system,trace.rs}), so a rf-input/retroforge-only change does NOT make docs/evidence/local-gate.json stale — no local-gate.sh re-run needed and that file stays out of write_scope. Verify with the validator at close rather than trusting this note. Also pre-paid: RustCrypto 0.11's Digest::finalize() returns Array<u8,N> with no LowerHex, so format!("{:x}", ..) is E0277 — crates/rf-cart/src/hash.rs:44 has the 4-line hex() helper to copy.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 (conductor). Seven-command gate re-run INDEPENDENTLY (RF-L-08), all exit 0, 406 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (was 358 at W1-06 close). Two checks the seven do NOT cover, run because this ticket touched Cargo.lock and two manifests: `cargo deny check licenses` => "licenses ok" (sha2 was already a TECH_STACK §2 row, but the row's existence is not the licence gate — the command is), and `grep -c '^name = "wgpu"$' Cargo.lock` == 1, since crates/retroforge's manifest is exactly where the two-wgpu trap lives. NOTE on the implementing agent's report: it said "0 ignored"; the conductor's independent count is 1 (the long-standing rf-state fixture-regenerator). Small, but it is the kind of number that gets copied forward — corrected in docs/STATUS.md.

MUTATION-TESTED 2026-08-05 (conductor), re-run independently rather than trusting the implementing agent's report: (1) neutering EmuStepper::latch_input (dropping both set_controller_buttons calls, keeping the signature so it still compiles) FAILED different_logs_produce_different_and_sticky_hash_sequences AND positive_known_button_byte_lands_at_expected_wram_address; (2) swapping KeyMap::default_nes's Z/X bindings FAILED positive_known_button_byte_lands_at_expected_wram_address — which bites only because that test drives the real Key -> KeyMap -> InputLatch pipeline instead of a hand-rolled bit literal. Both restored and verified byte-identical by checksum, not by eye. The mutation that mattered is (1): it is the one that proves criterion 3 is not the vacuous version the pre-flight predicted.

CONDUCTOR FIX 2026-08-05 (precedent: the 2026-08-03 tempdir() race — in scope, small, verified, and leaving it red would corrode the verification discipline). The implementing agent reported, honestly, that CoreCommand::StepFrame/StepScanline do not latch live input. StepFrame was a real defect and is fixed: crates/retroforge/src/stepper.rs's module doc asserts latch_and_advance_frame is the single path every input-driven caller goes through, and core_thread's StepFrame arm advanced a whole frame outside it — a doc-vs-code contradiction introduced by this ticket, not pre-existing debt. It is now latch_and_advance_frame(input.load(), ..) + pause(), reproducing step_frame's FR-DBG-004 forced pause exactly. Holding a key and pressing Step Frame was silently ignored before, which is precisely the case a debugger user steps a frame to inspect. StepScanline deliberately still does NOT latch: a scanline step stops MID-FRAME, so latching there would apply input at a non-frame boundary and violate ARCHITECTURE §6's rule that input only ever takes effect at frame boundaries. The asymmetry is commented in place so the next agent does not "fix" it. Pinned by a new test (406th) asserting both properties the arm depends on, and that test FAILS under mutation (1) above. The channel arm itself stays wiring-only on purpose: a stepped frame emits no CoreEvent::Frame and WRAM is not observable from the UI side, so testing it through the mpsc path would be timing-dependent for no added coverage — stated in the test's doc rather than left as an implied claim.

FINDING 2026-08-05, recorded at the confidence it was actually established and NO higher: the determinism fixture's own poll loop deterministically misses one video frame's vblank on a ~12-frame period (frames 0, 8, 20, 32 ...). MEASURED: deterministic and input-independent, from single-frame pulses at every index 0-39 with a fresh run each. NOT CONFIRMED: the mechanism. nesdev's one-dot-early $2002-read vblank suppression is the most likely reading and is consistent with the fixture's 7-CPU-cycle poll loop drifting against an 89,342-dot frame, but confirming it would need instrumenting rf-nes internals, outside this write_scope. Deliberately NOT cross-referenced to W1-05c: that ticket owns the UNREACHABLE sub-cycle case, whereas the one-clock-early case here is already implemented and passing (W1-05b), so linking them would imply a connection nobody has verified and would muddy the highest-risk ticket on the board. The anti-vacuity test was rebuilt around the measured pattern (a persistent multi-frame hold plus empirical first-divergence detection) after the naive single-substituted-frame version failed and was root-caused instead of tuned until green.

MANUAL CHECKLIST STILL NOT COMPLETED — inherited from W1-06, restated as a gap rather than quietly dropped. Everything mechanically testable here is headless and green, but the LIVE path — pressing a key in a real window and seeing the character move — remains UNVERIFIED, for the same reason W1-06's window/dialog/transport criteria are: this sandboxed macOS session has no screen-recording/assistive-access grant. What is proven: the egui->rf-input key table, the latch, the AtomicU64 hand-off, and the core thread's per-frame load are each unit-tested, and the machine-side half (an InputFrame reaching WRAM through a real $4016 read) is proven end-to-end. What is NOT proven: that egui actually delivers key_down for these keys in a real window. A human with a desktop session should run ./target/debug/retroforge, open a ROM, and confirm the D-pad/A/B keys move something before W2-06 layers gamepads and a remap UI on top.

HANDOFF 2026-08-05 (Phase 1 wave gate, conductor + independent challenger): THIS TICKET'S DETERMINISM SUITE DOES NOT SATISFY ROADMAP's PHASE-1 EXIT BULLET 4, 'Determinism: 2x 10k-frame runs, identical per-frame state hashes'. Contradicted on two independent axes. (a) SCALE: the double-run test calls build_script(24, None) — 24 frames, over 400x short of 10,000; no 10k-frame test exists anywhere in the workspace. That half is cheap to close: raise the frame count, and if the runtime is unacceptable in debug, gate it behind #[ignore] plus a local-gate invocation the way the other heavy suites already are, rather than quietly leaving it at 24. (b) COVERAGE — and this is the half that is NOT this ticket's to fix: the hash deliberately excludes PPU internals and APU because rf-nes implements no EmulatorCore::save_state, so it structurally cannot observe a PPU/APU divergence at any frame count. Full-state coverage is owed by W2-04, which now carries a matching note. This ticket's own acceptance (three criteria, all green and mutation-verified) is NOT in question — the gap is between what this ticket was asked for and what the ROADMAP criterion demands, which is a board-level mismatch, not a defect in the delivered work.

tickets.title: Determinism at scale: 10k-frame double-run
acceptance: two runs of a 10,000-frame input log produce identical per-frame reachable-state hash sequences (FR-CORE-002, FR-CORE-003), satisfying docs/ROADMAP.md's amended Phase 1 exit criterion -- W1-07 built the mechanism but runs only 24 frames, over 400x short

AMENDED 2026-08-06 (conductor, after measuring rather than guessing -- see notes): the 10k run is actually EXECUTED by the gate, never silently skipped, via #[ignore] plus a RELEASE-mode invocation from BOTH .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/local-gate.sh. Debug is ~93s for 2x10k and cannot go in cargo test --workspace (which is ~45s total today); release is ~9s. Whether it also earns a row in docs/evidence/local-gate.json is a judgement the implementer must make EXPLICITLY and record -- see the notes for both sides; do not leave it implicit either way
a divergence injected anywhere in the 10k-frame run is DETECTED and reported at the frame it first occurs -- proving the long run is not merely long but actually compared per frame
notes: RAISED 2026-08-05 by the Phase 1 exit gate (docs/STATUS.md), which found ROADMAP's Phase 1 determinism criterion CONTRADICTED on scale: the only double-run test calls build_script(24, None). SCOPE FENCE: this ticket closes the SCALE half only. The COVERAGE half -- that EmuStepper::state_hash excludes PPU internals and APU because rf-nes implements no EmulatorCore::save_state, so it cannot observe such a divergence at ANY frame count -- is W2-04's, and ROADMAP's amended criteria now stage it that way (Phase 1 = reachable state, Phase 2 = full machine state). Do NOT attempt full-state hashing here; rf-nes is not in this write_scope and save_state does not exist yet.

PRE-FLIGHT HINT (conductor, not yet verified by measurement): the existing fixture in crates/retroforge/tests/determinism.rs runs a real NES frame per iteration, so 2 x 10,000 frames is roughly 600M master cycles. Measure the debug-build runtime BEFORE choosing between an inline #[test] and the #[ignore]+local-gate path -- and choose on the measurement, not on a guess. If it lands in local-gate, note that this ticket's write_scope already includes crates/rf-harness/** and docs/evidence/local-gate.json for exactly that reason.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-06 (conductor) -- MEASURED, and it settles the ticket's shape. Method: temporarily raised same_log_two_independent_runs_produce_identical_hash_sequences' frame count, timed it, restored the file and verified byte-identical by checksum. DEBUG: 250 frames x2 = 2.29s, 1000 frames x2 = 9.32s => linear at ~4.7ms/frame => 2x10,000 ~= 93s. The whole workspace suite is ~45s today, so an inline #[test] would TRIPLE every contributor's cargo test and is ruled out on evidence. RELEASE: 1000 frames x2 = 0.89s => 2x10,000 ~= 9s, a 10.5x speedup. So the answer is #[ignore] + release-mode invocation, and the acceptance clause written yesterday (which assumed the debug/local-gate framing and mandated an evidence row) is amended accordingly -- the measurement postdates it.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-06 (conductor) -- THE EVIDENCE-ROW QUESTION IS GENUINELY TWO-SIDED; decide it explicitly and record the reasoning, do not drift into one. AGAINST a row: docs/evidence/local-gate.json exists to prove suites whose INPUTS ARE GITIGNORED actually ran, because cargo test skips them cleanly and a skip is indistinguishable from a pass in default output (the Phase 1 challenger demonstrated this with RF_NES6502_VECTORS=/nonexistent). This suite's fixture is a synthetic in-code NROM built by controller_reader_rom() -- no ROMs, no skip path, nothing to fake -- so a green CI run is itself the proof, and the mechanism solves a problem this test does not have. FOR a row: the staleness check (git merge-base --is-ancestor over coveredPaths) is what FORCES a local re-run after touching relevant code; with no row, nothing makes a conductor re-run 10k frames after editing crates/retroforge/src or crates/rf-nes. COST of a row: local_gate_evidence.rs would have to drive EmuStepper, so rf-harness gains a dependency on the retroforge lib, which pulls eframe/wgpu into the harness build. Do NOT solve this by having local-gate.sh pass a pass/fail RESULT into the evidence binary as a CLI flag -- inputs from the shell have precedent (the open-ticket list), a result does not, and that would make the evidence forgeable by the very script it is meant to check.

notes: SPLIT OUT OF W2-01b 2026-08-16 (Brad's ruling; W2-01b's notes carry the full measurement history). ROOT CAUSE: dma_4016_read needs exactly ONE extra $4016 read (08 08 07 08 08) and W2-01b's model produces THREE (05). nesdev.org/wiki/DMA says this case is "1 or 3 extra reads", so the count is alignment-dependent -- but every configuration W2-01b measured lands on 2 or 3, never 1.

DO NOT RETRY WITHOUT: a model of WHICH ADDRESS the halted 6502 holds on each no-operation DMA cycle. Every W2-01b configuration assumed it re-issues the read of the address it was reading (nesdev: "the 6502 core repeats the last read cycle"); the 1-extra-read case implies that on at least one no-op cycle the bus is NOT showing $4016. The two references nesdev cites for exactly this are BreakingNESWiki's DMA circuit analysis and Fiskbit's aligned-controller-read tests. Do NOT retry by tuning get/put parity -- measured in W2-01b, strictly worse (the first three ROMs stop printing at all).

ALREADY PAID by W2-01b, do not rediscover: these five ROMs leave PRG-RAM all-zero (blargg's older screen-only shell -- a manifest protocol mistag of the same class W1-05b found on sprite_hit_tests), so results are read out of the PPU nametable via `NesBus::ppu_vram_for_test`; the in-crate test in crates/rf-nes/src/apu/tests/dmc_dma_rom.rs already asserts the measured 3-of-5 status EXACTLY, so this ticket's fix will fail that test until its expected_pass flag is flipped -- that is the intended signal, not a regression.

DONE 2026-08-17. dma_4016_read prints `08 08 07 08 08` and self-reports Passed. dmc_dma_during_read4 is 4 of 5; only double_2007_read remains, which is W2-01d's PPU behaviour and never shared this root cause.

THE TICKET'S OWN HYPOTHESIS WAS CLOSE BUT AIMED AT THE WRONG LAYER. It said the fix needed a model of WHICH ADDRESS the halted 6502 holds on each no-op DMA cycle. It does not. The ROM's source settles it: its `end:` routine counts how many reads it takes the pad to return 1, so `08` means no extra read and `07` means exactly one -- it is measuring shifted BITS, not bus reads. nesdev's "1 or 3 extra reads" counts reads; both statements are true at once.

MECHANISM: a standard controller's shift register is clocked by the EDGE of the read strobe. The three back-to-back $4016 reads a DMC halt puts on the bus (halt, dummy, alignment) hold one strobe continuously asserted -- one rising edge, so ONE extra bit. The run is broken by the DMA's own get ($C000) and the CPU's resumed read supplies the second edge. This yields exactly one extra bit for BOTH alignments, which is why the answer never depended on get/put parity -- the thing the ticket rightly forbade tuning.

TWO MODELS WERE MEASURED AGAINST EACH OTHER, not argued. Variant B (the halt cycle is the CPU's own read, so only later no-op cycles repeat it) gives `08 08 06 08 08` -- two extra bits, still wrong -- AND regresses dma_2007_read from its documented CRC 5E3DF9C4 to 159A7A8F. Variant A (edge-triggered clock) gives the ROM's exact expected output and leaves the other three ROMs untouched. A discriminating experiment, so the choice is evidence rather than preference.

IMPLEMENTED ENTIRELY IN system/mod.rs (`NesBus::read_controller_port` + `last_joy_read_cycle`/`last_joy_bit`), which is why it fit the declared write scope: a contiguous read returns the bit the port LAST drove -- deliberately not `Controller::peek_bit`, which reports the bit the NEXT clock would present. The suppression is disabled while the strobe is HIGH, because the pad is then continuously reloading from live buttons rather than shifting, and applying it there broke `strobe_held_high_continuously_reloads_from_live_buttons` (caught by that test, not by review).

FIVE CONTROLLER UNIT TESTS WERE READING $4016 ON CONSECUTIVE CYCLES -- a pattern no instruction sequence can produce (`LDA $4016` is four cycles) and which only a DMC DMA halt creates. They now read the way software does, via a `read_bits_like_software` helper that puts a non-port cycle between reads, and the contiguous case gets its OWN test asserting both halves (contiguous holds, spaced advances) so an engine that simply stopped shifting cannot pass.

SAVE STATE: both new fields go in the CPU_ chunk's bus half (-> version 2 via rf-state's per-tag registry). They decide whether the very next port read counts as a new strobe edge, so dropping them across a save would let a restored machine clock a bit the saved one would not have. Two rf-state tests hardcoded `2` as "a version this build does not expect" and silently became no-ops the moment CPU_ reached 2; they now derive it as current+1.

VERIFIED, criterion 3 in full: apu_test 8/8, nestest 8991/8991 byte-exact, nes6502 2,550,000/2,550,000 -- a DMA-timing change moves every downstream cycle count, so these were the real risk. Both #[ignore]d 5-minute replay goldens re-run under --release and UNMOVED (games read the pad spaced, so the edge model does not reach them).
SCOPE AMENDMENT (vetoable, recorded): crates/rf-nes/src/system/** (the controller test file is under system/tests/) and crates/rf-state/** (the CPU_ version bump).

tickets.title: PPU $2007 double-read quirk: unblock double_2007_read
acceptance: dmc_dma_during_read4/double_2007_read prints one of the four CRCs its source header documents (FR-CORE-022, FR-CORE-024)
the in-crate PPU suite is unregressed: read_buffer, both golden frames, ppu_vbl_nmi 10/10, sprite_hit_tests 11/11
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W2-01b 2026-08-16 (Brad's ruling). This is NOT a DMA defect and never was -- it is a PPU behavior this crate does not implement in any form, stated by the ROM's own header: "Double read of $2007 sometimes ignores extra read, and puts odd things into buffer". It lives in ppu/** (the $2007 delayed read buffer, `crate::ppu::scroll`'s read_data path), which is why it could not have been inside W2-01b's apu/** write scope.

MEASURED in W2-01b: this engine prints CRC D84F6815, none of the four accepted (85CFD627, F018C287, 440EF923, E52F41A5), and the value is IDENTICAL across every DMA-model configuration tried -- which is the evidence that it does not share W2-01c's root cause. Its screen text (22 33 44 55 66 / 33 44 55 66 77) is close to two of the documented variants, so the gap is narrow and specific, not a wholesale mismatch.

DONE 2026-08-17. double_2007_read prints `22 33 44 55 66` / `22 44 55 66 77` and CRC **85CFD627** -- the FIRST of the four variants its source header documents. dmc_dma_during_read4 is now 5 of 5, and wave 2 is complete.

WHAT THE ROM ACTUALLY DOES, from its source: it provokes the double read with `lda $20F7,x` where x = $10. $20F7 + $10 = $2107, which CROSSES A PAGE, so the 6502 issues its dummy read at the wrong address ($2007) and then the real read at $2107 -- which also mirrors to $2007. Two $2007 reads on back-to-back CPU cycles. The first `lda $20F7,x` with x = $00 does not cross, reads $2007 once, and is the control line.

MECHANISM: the second of two back-to-back $2007 reads reports the value the FIRST one already presented -- the PPU cannot drive a fresh byte one cycle later -- while the read buffer and `v` still advance twice. That is exactly the difference between this crate's old `33 44 55 66 77` (both reads counted, buffer advanced twice) and the ROM's first accepted variant `22 44 55 66 77` (same internal progress, one stale value out). The ROM's own header names the behaviour: "Double read of $2007 sometimes ignores extra read, and puts odd things into buffer".

SAME SHAPE AS W2-01c, ONE DAY APART, AND WORTH GENERALISING: both were a second access on a back-to-back cycle reporting a held value rather than a fresh one. The controller case suppresses the shift; this one does not suppress the side effects, only the reported value -- so they are the same *class* of bug (a device that cannot respond twice in consecutive cycles) with different internal consequences. Do not assume a third instance behaves like either without checking which half is held.

IMPLEMENTED IN ppu/** ONLY, as the ticket's write scope required, by keying off `Ppu::dot_clock` rather than the bus's `master_cycle`: `NesBus::read` performs the register read BEFORE ticking that cycle's three dots, so two reads on consecutive CPU cycles are exactly three dots apart. No bus-layer plumbing was needed.

SAVE STATE: `last_2007_read_dot`/`last_2007_read_value` are serialized and PPU_ moved to version 3 (it had gone to 2 in W2-19). They decide whether the next $2007 read reports a held value, so dropping them would let a restored machine return a fresh byte where the saved one returned a stale one.

VERIFIED, criterion 2 in full: ppu_vbl_nmi 10/10, sprite_hit_tests 11/11, nestest 8991/8991 byte-exact, the in-crate read_buffer suite and both golden frames green, accuracy table 31 rows. Both #[ignore]d 5-minute replay goldens re-run under --release and UNMOVED.

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16. All five remaining acceptance criteria met (the sixth, the manager modal, moved to W4-11 by Brad's split). THE WIDENED HASH FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN ITS FIRST RUN, and that is the most important thing in this ticket. Discharging the HANDOFF note (extend state_hash to the newly reachable regions) turned mode_invariant_corpus RED on w3-05a-sprite-limit-bypass-overlay, with IDENTICAL video hashes and DIFFERENT state hashes. Diagnosis: W3-05a's overlay channel (sprite_overlay_enabled, overlay_sprites, overlay_active_sprites) is ENHANCEMENT state that physically lives inside the Ppu struct, so serializing the whole PPU put mode-dependent bytes into a CORE chunk -- which ARCHITECTURE §3's determinism invariant forbids outright ("Accuracy vs Enhanced must produce identical core state hashes for identical inputs"). Those three fields are now excluded, with the whole reasoning recorded at the exclusion site; enhancement state belongs in the ENHC chunk per SAVE_STATES.md §2. A partial hash could never have surfaced this.

COMPLETENESS IS COMPILER-ENFORCED, not reviewed: every save_* destructures its type exhaustively with no `..` rest, so a new field on Ppu, Apu, Cpu, NesBus, Controller or any APU sub-unit fails the build until it is written out or bound to `_` with a stated reason. This was chosen over bincode derives because those would force a bincode dependency into rf-core-api, which W0-04 committed to ZERO dependencies. Three fields are deliberately excluded beyond the overlay: the two per-scanline line buffers (scratch -- every element is rewritten before the row that reads them is emitted), the PPU's completed-scanline and event queues (output, not state; saving with either non-empty is REFUSED with a diagnostic, per SAVE_STATES.md §2's frame-boundary rule), and event_mask (caller subscription config, FR-CORE-006, not machine state).

hash_kind: reachable-v1 -> full-v1, a NEW value rather than a silent redefinition, exactly as SAVE_STATES.md §3 demanded ("a full-machine hash is a later ticket's upgrade, not a silent redefinition of this field"). CHECKED, not assumed: rf-harness's two 5-minute replay-corpus tests compute reachable-v1 from their own INDEPENDENT reimplementation, so they are unaffected -- and both were re-run green in release (38.8s and 39.4s), which the ordinary gate never does because they are #[ignore]d in debug. HANDOFF 2026-08-05 (Phase 1 wave gate, conductor + independent challenger): THIS TICKET OWNS HALF OF A PHASE-1 EXIT CRITERION. ROADMAP's Phase 1 bullet 4 is 'Determinism: 2x 10k-frame runs, identical per-frame state hashes'. W1-07 built the double-run mechanism, but its hash is explicitly NOT a full-machine hash — rf-nes implements no EmulatorCore::save_state/state_view, so PPU internals (VRAM, palette RAM, loopy v/t/x/w) and APU are structurally unreachable and excluded by design. tickets.title: Audio output: cpal + ring + rate control
acceptance: rtrb SPSC ring, rubato resampler with ±0.5% dynamic rate control against buffer fill (FR-FE-006)
no underruns over 5-min soak on dev machine
audio-clock frame pacing per ARCHITECTURE §8

apu_mixer RMS envelope check wired against W2-01b's mixer LUTs, using the ROMs' own cancellation-to-silence design as the oracle -- no external reference recording exists or is needed (added 2026-08-16 by Brad's ruling, from W2-01b's split)
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16, all four acceptance criteria met and measured. (1) rtrb SPSC ring + rubato resampler + ±0.5% dynamic rate control against ring fill: each unit-tested headlessly, and the rate loop's CLOSED LOOP simulated to convergence rather than only sign-checked. (2) Five-minute soak RUN ON THIS MACHINE (macOS CoreAudio, release): 18,033 frames in 300 s = 60.1 fps, ZERO underrun samples, final correction 0.99811, ring fill 0.000..0.734. (3) Audio-clock frame pacing: the emulator runs a frame only when the device has drained the ring back to target -- the 60.1 fps above IS that clock working, since nothing else paced it (the wall-clock pacer resyncs and stands down whenever a device is streaming). (4) apu_mixer gate wired, see the note on it below.

TWO REAL FINDINGS, both caught by tests rather than review. (a) THE RATE CONTROLLER'S SIGN WAS INVERTED in its first draft, behind a plausible-sounding "a filling ring must be drained faster" comment. The resample ratio is output-over-input, so a filling ring must produce FEWER samples; the closed-loop convergence test caught it, and a test that only asserted the sign would have agreed with the bug. The derivation is now in `RateController::update`'s doc so the next reader does not have to re-derive it. (b) rubato's `max_resample_ratio_relative` is RECIPROCAL-symmetric: passing 1.005 allows [0.995025, 1.005] and REJECTS the additively symmetric 0.995 the controller produces at full downward authority -- so a naive construction would have had its correction rejected the first time a ring fully drained. Both are recorded in docs/TECH_STACK.md's rows.

THE apu_mixer GATE'S FIRST VERSION WAS VACUOUS, and the mutation proved it: asserting "the quietest eighth of the capture is quiet" passed happily with the tnd LUT scaled +20%, because it was measuring the idle silence BEFORE the first beep. It is now anchored to the section between the two beeps (located by finding them), and its sensitivity is recorded from that same mutation: square 0.061 -> 0.31, dmc 0.060 -> 0.21, against a 0.10 limit. `triangle` (0.092 residue vs a 0.057 noise floor) and `noise` (whose section is MEANT to be loud -- its own on-screen text says "fade noise in, and out, without any tone") are structural-only, with the reason stated in the test rather than a threshold picked to make them pass.

FINDING FOR A LATER TICKET: the triangle channel's cancellation residue is 0.092 of peak where square's is 0.061 and the idle noise floor is 0.057. A correctly weighted triangle should cancel to the floor the way square does, so this is a small but real inaccuracy in either the triangle's output level or its mixer weight. It is NOT gated (a threshold tight enough to catch it would sit inside the measurement's spread), it is printed on every run, and it is written down here rather than smoothed over.

DELIBERATE NARROWING, stated rather than hidden: the core's decimation integrates the area under the piecewise-constant mixer output over each output period. That is exact anti-aliasing for a piecewise-constant source (a moving-average low-pass, not point sampling), but it is NOT the windowed-sinc "blip-buffer band-limited steps" EMULATION_CORES §2.3 names, whose stopband rejection is far better than a box filter's -13 dB first sidelobe. Chosen so the core stays dependency-free and the decimation is exactly checkable; upgrading it changes audio quality only, never machine state, so it can land any time without touching the determinism invariant.

FEATURE-GATED DEVICE OUTPUT: cpal sits behind `rf-audio/device` and `retroforge/audio`, both OFF by default, because cpal pulls in ALSA on Linux and the CI runner installs only cc65 -- a default-on cpal would have turned CI red on a change no one could verify from a dev machine. Everything testable headlessly (ring, rate loop, resampler, filters, and the whole `audio_out` chain) is compiled and tested unconditionally; what the gate does NOT cover is the cpal callback itself and the soak, both of which are run deliberately. The app's binary should enable `audio`.

SCOPE-ADD beyond crates/rf-audio/** and crates/retroforge/**: `crates/rf-nes/src/apu/**` and `crates/rf-nes/src/system/mod.rs` (the decimator, the sample queue and `NesBus::drain_audio` -- audio originates inside the core and ARCHITECTURE §5 says cores emit it via CoreSink::audio, so there is no way to build this ticket without them), `crates/rf-nes/src/apu/state.rs` (the completeness destructure forced a decision on the three new fields; they are audio OUTPUT, excluded from save states with the same reasoning as the PPU's scanline queue), `docs/TESTING.md` and `docs/TECH_STACK.md`.

Canaries unregressed after a change that adds work to every CPU cycle: nestest 8991/8991 byte-exact, apu_test 8/8, ppu_vbl_nmi 10/10, sprite_hit_tests 11/11, nes6502 2,560,000/2,560,000, both golden frames, mode-invariant and determinism green.

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16, all four criteria met. (1) Scan + normalized-hash identity (FR-FE-001, NFR-005): `rf_cart::Cartridge::load` sniffs the console from CONTENT and hashes the header-stripped image, so a renamed or re-dumped cartridge is one game across the library, its settings and its save states. (2) Per-game settings keyed by hash (FR-FE-002). (3) First-run states per FRONTEND_UI section 3.1. (4) Symlink-loop-safe, root-confined scan (NFR-010).

NFR-010 / D-006 IS TESTED WITH REAL SYMLINKS, not asserted in prose. Two unit tests build actual trees: a directory symlink pointing back at the root (which recurses forever without the canonical visited set) and a symlink pointing OUT of the root, both as a directory and as a file. The escape is refused with a diagnostic naming the offending path per FAILURE_MODES FM-15 -- never silently followed, and never silently skipped either, because a scan that quietly drops half a library is indistinguishable from one that found nothing. The visited set holds CANONICAL directories specifically because that is the only form in which a cycle is recognizable.

G-21's POINT MADE TESTABLE: `library::first_run_state` is a pure function of (configured roots, scan result), so 'no folders configured' and 'folders configured but empty' being DIFFERENT states with different messages is a unit test rather than something only visible by rendering. That was the actual substance of the design-review finding -- an empty grid that says nothing -- and it would otherwise have been unverifiable in this session.

PER-GAME SETTINGS: one file per game named by hash, not a single index -- a corrupt index costs every game's settings, a corrupt per-game file costs one, and 'reset this game' becomes a delete. UNKNOWN KEYS ARE PRESERVED across load/save, so an older build opening a newer build's config does not silently delete settings it could not read; W3-02a (shaders) and W4-05 (per-game enhancement toggles) will add keys to this file and this property is what keeps that safe. A `#[derive(Deserialize)]` struct would not have given it.

WIRED, NOT SHELVED. The store would have been a disconnected pipeline if nothing wrote to it, so the app now identifies a ROM on open, loads its settings, and applies the overlay BEFORE the core starts (a game configured for the overlay gets it from frame 0, not a frame later); toggling the overlay persists immediately, with no Apply button. Law 6 still holds: the default is Accuracy/overlay-off, so only a game the user deliberately configured comes back configured. A ROM this build cannot identify gets NO settings key at all -- deliberate, since settings under a hash we could not compute would eventually apply to the wrong game.

LIBRARY ROOTS are stored in their own minimal file (`library.rflib`, one path per line) rather than in a settings framework: W2-08 owns app-wide settings and will absorb this, and absorbing a dozen lines is easier than unpicking a framework invented early. Roots are saved AS THE USER CHOSE THEM, never canonicalized -- a removable drive's canonical path is not stable across mounts, and containment resolves at scan time anyway, which is where it must happen since a symlink can appear after the folder was configured.

UI VERIFICATION, same honest limit as W2-06: the Library window (first-run call-to-action, grid, per-entry Play, the skipped-paths list) is built and the app launches cleanly with it, but clicking through it needs W4-09's egui harness. THE WAIVER MECHANISM IS THE EXISTING ONE, and its teeth were verified by running it, not by reading it: an EXPIRED waiver fails the run (checked with --today 2026-12-01: exit 1, seven 'WAIVER EXPIRED' lines), and a waiver covering a ROM that has STARTED PASSING also fails (checked by temporarily waiving oam_read: 'STALE WAIVER ... delete the waiver rather than leaving it to mask the next failure'). CONDUCTOR CORRECTION 2 -- THE 'UNEXPLAINED' PPUSTATUS DISCREPANCY IS NOT AN rf-nes BUG. That is correct hardware behaviour: the PPU clears sprite-0 hit at DOT 1 OF THE PRE-RENDER LINE, which is after vblank ends, so during the vblank window this code runs in bit 6 is still set from the PREVIOUS frame's hit; a bare 'wait until set' exits instantly on the stale flag and a later read, past pre-render, reads clear. It was evidence of the opposite: more consistent pre-DMA work pushed the DMA start later still, so it straddled the reset window harder. CONDUCTOR ERROR, RECORDED IN FULL: investigating the first pass I concluded the buggy-overflow-scan explanation was correct and explicitly told the executor the OAM-DMA-straddle candidate was 'unnecessary -- drop that line of investigation'. IT WAS THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, and the executor found it despite that instruction. I had conflated two different questions: the authentic buggy diagonal scan explains why $2002 bit 5 can never witness '>8 sprites on a scanline' (that finding stands, and is why the OAM-counting test exists), but says NOTHING about why the sprites never reached OAM. The mechanism was documented in sprites.rs's own module doc the whole time and I could have checked before dismissing it. Lesson: when two candidate causes answer different questions, resolving one does not eliminate the other.

CRITERION 1 MET, and proven the right way: 12 sprites in range of scanline 100 (hardware limit 8) on every one of 8 sampled frames across a full rotation period, counted from `Ppu::oam()` during vblank -- not from the CPU-side OAM shadow, and not from $2002 bit 5. CRITERION 2 MET via an exact RAM formula (blink_visible == (frame_counter & 0x08) != 0) across 120 samples with both phases observed. CRITERION 4 MET: ROM re-pinned to c79f6f61ae82a87beaf57edb6757d75c1cfb2a1316196b1c8295f22a1699e087 with every consumer updated (rom.sha256, FORMAT.md provenance, split-timing frozen histograms, and rf_scroller_replay.rs's 6 GOLDEN_HASHES regenerated with recording and independent replay agreeing byte-exact). W5-01 does not exist yet, so nothing to re-pin there.

CRITERION 3 IS PARTIALLY MET and documented as such rather than rounded up: camera_y is a real, bounded, correctly-gated RAM witness, but phase-matched rendered-frame comparison found NO observable pixel effect with the current split technique. Left as an honest, out-of-scope gap.

SPLIT TIMING RE-MEASURED, NOT RESTORED (the frozen constants in the backup described a ROM that no longer existed): the tail split pair now lands 100% at scanlines 14-15, zero later than 18, zero missed -- at or inside W2-10's baseline of 1682 writes / 100% in 14-18 / zero later than 18. That follows structurally from the reorder, since nothing new runs before either scroll-write pair on any frame any more; the W2-10 fragility note about SPLIT_DELAY being a trim rather than the mechanism is now considerably less load-bearing.

PROCESS LESSON FOR ANY FUTURE MULTI-SESSION WORK, which cost real time here: two sessions were writing to one working tree with no shared view of what the other had done. That produced a data-loss incident (conductor `git checkout` over uncommitted work), then nearly produced a second (the peer was about to reconstruct from memory seven files that existed verbatim in a backup it did not know about). What contained both was the peer STOPPING to report a discrepancy instead of proceeding on its own model of the tree. Commit code before verifying it -- the board's own discipline -- and tell collaborators when the shared tree changes under them.

tickets.title: Fix: a stepped frame never reaches the UI (Step Frame/Scanline appear dead)
acceptance: pressing Step Frame visibly advances the picture by one frame, and Step Scanline by one scanline, instead of appearing to do nothing (FR-DBG-004)
a headless test spawns a real core thread, sends CoreCommand::StepFrame, and asserts a CoreEvent::Frame actually arrives on the channel -- the test whose absence let this ship
the UI keeps repainting until a stepped frame has been consumed, so a frame delivered after the click's own repaint is not stranded in the channel
notes: REPORTED BY BRAD 2026-08-06 from the first real desktop session: 'run works and can play game, the step frame and scanline seem to pause and do nothing'. Diagnosed before touching code, per the bug-fix discipline (rank causes, show how each is verified, only then fix).

ROOT CAUSE 1 (PRIMARY, confirmed by inspection): crates/retroforge/src/core_thread.rs's loop sends CoreEvent::Frame from EXACTLY ONE place -- inside `if stepper.tick_running_with_input(...)`. That call returns false whenever the machine is Paused. StepFrame/StepScanline advance the emulator and render into `sink`, then force Paused, so the freshly rendered frame is computed and then silently DISCARDED, never sent. The machine really does step (state advances correctly); the user just never sees it. Verification: read the single send site; confirmed by the new headless test in acceptance criterion 2, which fails before the fix.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (COMPOUNDING, confirmed by inspection): crates/retroforge/src/app.rs's pump_core_events only calls ctx.request_repaint() when self.running. Even once root cause 1 is fixed, a stepped frame arrives over the channel a few ms AFTER the button click's own repaint has already completed, so with no repaint scheduled the frame would sit unconsumed until some unrelated event (a mouse move) happened to wake the UI. Fixing only root cause 1 would produce a maddening 'sometimes works if you jiggle the mouse' bug. Both must be fixed together.

NOT A BUG, recorded so it is not 'fixed' later: rf_renderer::FrameBuffer has no clear step -- video_scanline writes rows in place, so the buffer persists between frames. A scanline step therefore paints the new scanline over the previous frame's content, which is correct debugger behaviour; it also means a single scanline step is nearly imperceptible by design. Step Frame is the visible one.

WHY THIS SHIPPED, worth more than the fix itself: EmuStepper's state machine was thoroughly unit-tested (13 tests: pause/resume/step-frame/step-scanline/cycle budgets) and the core thread's FM-01 panic path was tested, but NOTHING tested the seam between them -- that a CoreCommand produces a CoreEvent::Frame. W1-06's own notes predicted exactly this: it classified the transport buttons as part of the MANUAL checklist and warned 'do not let it is a GUI ticket become a reason for zero tests', then tested the state machine and the panic path while leaving the command->frame wiring to a manual pass that could not be run in a sandbox. The W1-07 conductor fix touched this very StepFrame arm and its mutation proved the LATCH worked -- not that a frame was delivered. Lesson: when a manual checklist is known to be unrunnable, the mechanically-testable seam next to it deserves MORE coverage, not the same amount.

CLOSED 2026-08-06 (conductor), implemented directly rather than delegated (2 files, ~15 lines of logic plus tests). BOTH root causes fixed together, because fixing only the first would have produced an intermittent 'works if you jiggle the mouse' bug: core_thread now tracks a `stepped` flag and sends the frame when EITHER the running tick produced one OR a step command did; app.rs tracks `awaiting_stepped_frame`, set on a step request and cleared when a frame lands, and keeps requesting repaints while it is outstanding so the UI stays awake to consume a frame that arrives after the click's own repaint has finished.

MUTATION-TESTED 2026-08-06 (conductor), BOTH DIRECTIONS -- a one-sided mutation would not show the fix is bounded rather than merely permissive. (1) Reverting the send condition to the shipped `if ran` reintroduces the exact reported bug: both new seam tests FAIL by timing out after 5s, which is the defect reproduced mechanically rather than described. (2) Widening it to `if true` (always send) makes a_paused_core_with_no_command_sends_no_frames FAIL, proving the fix does not over-correct into busy-spinning and flooding the channel while paused. tickets.title: Frame pacing: run at NTSC speed instead of as fast as the host can
acceptance: a running core advances at the NTSC rate (60.0988 Hz) rather than free-running -- measured today at 113 fps in debug (1.9x too fast) and 1132 fps in release (18.8x too fast), i.e. unusable in a release build
pacing NEVER affects simulation: it decides WHEN a frame runs, never WHAT it computes, so the determinism suites are untouched -- proven by a mutation, not asserted

the pacer does not accumulate drift (a fixed sleep-per-frame would) and does not death-spiral after a stall (unbounded catch-up would) -- both asserted headlessly with synthetic timestamps, no real sleeping in tests
pacing is switchable off, because FR-ENH-008 defines loading-skip fast-forward as 'disabling frame pacing without altering simulation' and cannot be built on something with no off switch
notes: RAISED BY BRAD 2026-08-06: 'what about speed do we keep the global timers accurate'. Two different things had quietly diverged and the distinction is worth keeping straight. EMULATED timing is accurate and proven -- nestest 8991/8991 byte-exact, nes6502 2,560,000/2,560,000, mmc3_test_2 6/6 including the A12 filter, master_cycle advancing exactly once per bus op. WALL-CLOCK pacing did not exist AT ALL: crates/retroforge/src/core_thread.rs's loop emulated a frame, sent it, and immediately started the next; the only sleep in it was the PAUSED idle path. Measured on Alter Ego: 113 fps debug (1.9x real speed, which matches Brad's report of a playable but quick game) and 1132 fps release (18.8x -- unusable).

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-06 (conductor) -- FRAME PACING IS ASSUMED BY THE DESIGN DOCS IN FOUR PLACES AND IMPLEMENTED IN NONE. docs/design/FAILURE_MODES.md FM-07 throttles a plugin to 'protect frame pacing'; docs/design/PLUGINS.md repeats it; docs/design/RENDERER.md prefers Fifo/vsync present mode; and FR-ENH-008 literally DEFINES loading-skip as 'disabling frame pacing without altering simulation' -- you cannot disable what was never built. Same class of defect as R-05's phase gate: a control that exists in prose and nowhere in code.

DESIGN RULING 2026-08-06 (conductor): this is the INTERIM mechanism and says so in its own module doc. The documented end-state is an AUDIO-DRIVEN clock -- rf-audio's cpal ring plus dynamic rate control resampling within +/-0.5% against buffer fill (W2-05, behind W2-01a -> W2-01b) -- which is the right long-term answer because it self-corrects drift and prevents the underrun cascade FM-02 describes. A wall-clock sleep cannot do that. But W2-05 is three tickets away and the emulator is 18.8x too fast in release TODAY, so a host-clock pacer lands now and W2-05 subsumes it. Deliberately NOT waiting: an unusable release build is a worse state than a mechanism that gets replaced.

DETERMINISM NOTE 2026-08-06 (conductor), stated because it looks scarier than it is: pacing introduces wall-clock reads (Instant::now) into the emulator's run loop, which sounds like it violates FR-CORE-003 'cores shall contain no wall-clock reads'. It does not, and the boundary is mechanical rather than a judgement call: scripts/validate-arch.sh's determinism lint greps ONLY crates/rf-{core-api,nes,snes,cart}/src for std::time/Instant::now, and this lives in crates/retroforge, the app shell. More fundamentally, pacing gates WHEN tick_running_with_input is called and never touches its arguments or the machine, so identical input logs still produce identical state -- which the 10k-frame double-run suite continues to prove because it drives EmuStepper directly and never goes near the pacer.

CLOSED 2026-08-06 (conductor). MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER through the real core thread, not just the unit: release went 1132 fps (18.8x NTSC) -> 60.3 fps (1.00x), debug 113 fps (1.9x) -> 60.0 fps (1.00x). Gate all seven exit 0, 495 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored (was 487). validate-evidence stayed green with NO regeneration, which is itself the check that this touched nothing under crates/rf-nes.

DESIGN 2026-08-06: deadline-based, not sleep-per-frame, because the two obvious failure modes pull in opposite directions and a naive implementation hits one or the other. DRIFT: a fixed sleep(period) keeps every scheduler overshoot forever, so the emulator runs perpetually slow and the error compounds -- avoided by advancing an absolute deadline by exactly one period, so an overrun on one frame is repaid by a shorter sleep on the next. DEATH SPIRAL: a pure deadline scheme owes hundreds of frames after a stall (breakpoint, laptop suspend) and then runs flat-out repaying them, which the user sees as an unwanted fast-forward exactly when they least want it -- avoided by MAX_LAG (34ms, two frames), past which the debt is dropped and the schedule resyncs. The pacer holds NO clock of its own (every method takes `now`), so all eight tests use synthetic timestamps and none of them sleeps.

MUTATION-TESTED 2026-08-06 (conductor): deleting the MAX_LAG resync branch -- i.e. reverting to the pure deadline scheme -- fails a_long_stall_resyncs_instead_of_fast_forwarding, which simulates a one-second host stall and asserts the very next frame is paced normally rather than being one of ~60 free-running catch-up frames. Restored, verified byte-identical by checksum. Determinism independence confirmed separately by running the release 10k-frame double-run pair after the change: 2 passed, unchanged -- the suite drives EmuStepper directly and never constructs a pacer, so the independence is structural rather than incidental.

FOUR TESTS WERE NAIVE, NOT THE CODE -- the same trap as W2-15's, recorded again because it recurred within a day. The first drafts called next_delay exactly AT the deadline and expected a full period back; that is wrong, because the returned value is time-UNTIL-DUE, not time-between-frames, so arriving exactly on time correctly means 'run now, wait zero'. Rewritten to model how the loop actually calls it -- sleep the delay, do a frame's work, ask again -- and the reasoning is kept in the test's own doc comment so the next reader does not 'fix' the pacer to match the wrong mental model.
