Bit 0 of those bytes is the C flag, and the test does `clc` immediately before the point the IRQ is vectored -- so a `21` means the interrupt sequence pushed P BEFORE that `clc` ran, i.e. the IRQ was recognised ~2 CPU cycles early.

WHY IT IS THE IRQ AND NOT THE NMI: in the affected rows the IRQ column reads 00 (the IRQ handler never ran) while the NMI column carries the wrong C -- that combination means the NMI hijacked an IRQ sequence which had ALREADY STARTED. Had the NMI simply arrived early instead, the IRQ would have run afterwards and its column would be non-zero.

ALREADY REFUTED, DO NOT RE-TRY: the $4017 write-delay polarity. nesdev gives the frame-counter reset a 3-or-4 CPU-cycle delay depending on whether the write lands on an APU cycle, which is a genuine parity dependence and looked like the obvious candidate for a parity-alternating error. Flipping `on_apu_cycle` at the `$4017` write site does NOT fix test 3 -- it only shifts which iterations are wrong.

FINDING WORTH ACTING ON, from that same experiment: `Apu::on_apu_cycle`'s doc comment claims the polarity is "ROM-pinned: blargg's apu_test/4-jitter measures the 3-vs-4-cycle choice directly, so the polarity in FrameCounter::write is measured". IT IS NOT. apu_test passes 8/8 with the polarity flipped EITHER way, so that gate is vacuous for this fact and the comment overstates what is verified. Either find the ROM that does pin it, or correct the comment to say the polarity is unmeasured -- a doc comment asserting a measurement that does not exist is worse than one admitting the gap.

The frame counter ticks once per CPU cycle with nesdev's CPU-cycle step numbers (7457/14913/22371/29828/29829/29830), which is the standard model and is probably right; suspect the reset-delay arithmetic, the point at which `irq_flag` becomes visible to `CpuBus::irq_line`, or the interaction with W2-20's new no-poll-during-interrupt-entry rule before suspecting those constants.

DONE 2026-08-17. cpu_interrupts_v2 passes ALL FIVE sub-tests; its waiver is deleted, and `crates/rf-harness/waivers.toml` now contains NO waivers at all -- all ten ever raised (7 Tier-B by W2-09, 3 Tier-A CPU by W2-12) are gone, every one because the ROM passes.

THREE independent one-cycle facts, not one. The ticket predicted an APU frame-IRQ defect and that was right, but fixing it exposed two more, each invisible until the one before it was fixed -- a multi-sub-test ROM reports only its FIRST failure, so "one ROM red" was never one bug.

(1) THE CPU SEES THE APU IRQ ONE CYCLE LATE. The APU asserts at the end of a cycle; the CPU samples during the following one. `Apu::irq_line` now returns a view latched before each tick's work -- the same shape the PPU's NMI path already had via `NesBus::nmi_level_latch`, which is what made the omission findable. Without it `3-nmi_and_irq` recognised the frame IRQ a cycle early, and because the $4017 write delay has its own 3-vs-4-cycle parity rule, the ROM's SEVEN IDENTICAL rows came out ALTERNATING 21/20. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED BY MOVING THE FRAME COUNTER: setting the reset delay to 4/5 instead of 3/4 makes the same ROM pass and is the wrong fix -- blargg's apu_test/6-irq_flag_timing pins the flag itself to "29831 clocks after writing $00 to $4017", which that change breaks by a cycle. Measured both ways before choosing.

(2) THE OAM-DMA GET/PUT PHASE WAS BACKWARDS. nesdev: "at power-on, whether the first CPU cycle is get or put is random", so the crate picked one and documented the choice; `4-irq_and_dma` pins it against hardware. Under the old phase the DMA ran one cycle short and the ROM's 8/9 boundary landed at +526 where hardware puts it at +527 -- with all 528 OTHER rows already matching, which is what localised it to the DMA length rather than to the poll. An arbitrary choice resolved by measurement; the invariant the unit tests protect (the two alignments differ by exactly one cycle, {513, 514}) is untouched, and the parameter was renamed from `start_cycle_odd` to `needs_alignment_cycle` because the parity was never the point.

(3) A TAKEN, NON-PAGE-CROSSING BRANCH POLLS ONE CYCLE EARLIER THAN EVERY OTHER INSTRUCTION. `5-branch_delays_irq` states the rule in prose and marks the single differing row `*** This is the special case`. Implemented by keeping one more sample of history in `CountingBus` (`edge_latched_prev2`/`irq_raw_prev2`) and a `Cpu::branch_polls_one_cycle_early` flag set only on that exact branch shape -- intra-instruction, so not serialized.

SAVE STATE: `irq_line_delayed` IS serialized (APU_ chunk -> version 2 via rf-state's per-tag registry, the mechanism W2-19 built). It is one cycle behind the flags BY DESIGN, so reconstructing it at load from the current flags would make a restored machine see the line a cycle earlier than the saved one did -- precisely the timing the field exists to model.

RE-BASELINES, each with its reason and none taken to go green. rf_scroller_split_timing's two frozen histograms moved by three writes between adjacent scanlines (total 1182 and later_than_18 734/448 both UNCHANGED, so what they guard is unaffected). The rf_scroller 5-minute replay goldens moved -- and this is the one worth reading: the DMA change shifts rendering by a cycle every frame, so the pixels HAD to move, but all three checks that make those goldens mean anything passed FIRST and are asserted before the frozen comparison: recording vs independent replay byte-identical, every recorded periodic state hash matched, and the anti-vacuity witnesses (`player_x` reaches PLAYER_X_AT_END, `columns_streamed` reaches COLUMNS_STREAMED_AT_END) unchanged. The game plays out identically; only the pixels moved. Alter Ego's replay goldens did NOT move.

Five unit tests encoded the superseded conventions (2 asserting the APU IRQ line reflects flags instantly, 3 asserting the old DMA parity) and now assert the corrected ones -- including the lag itself, so the new behaviour is pinned rather than merely tolerated.
SCOPE AMENDMENTS (vetoable, recorded): crates/rf-harness/** (the frozen histograms and replay goldens live in its tests) and crates/rf-state/** (the APU_ version bump).

tickets.title: CPU: BRK/NMI interaction and the unstable $AB opcode
acceptance: cpu_timing_test6 passes -- DONE: its screen read "FAIL OP :$00" and now reads PASSED. The shared-cause hypothesis held; it was never a BRK timing bug, it was the interrupt poll (FR-CORE-020)
instr_test-v5 passes -- DONE: 16/16. $AB/LXA magic constant moved $EE -> $FF (FR-CORE-020)

cpu_interrupts_v2 2-nmi_and_brk passes -- DONE: exact on all ten delay rows, hijack window five wide at positions 4-8. AMENDED 2026-08-16 (Brad): the original criterion said the whole ROM passes. Fixing test 2 unmasked test 3 (3-nmi_and_irq), which is an APU frame-counter IRQ timing defect, not a CPU one -- split to W2-21 rather than widened into this ticket (FR-CORE-022)
the instr_test-v5 and cpu_timing_test6 waivers W2-12 added are DELETED rather than re-dated; the cpu_interrupts_v2 one is re-pointed at W2-21 with the narrowed evidence

nes6502 and nestest byte-exact are unregressed -- nestest 8991/8991 and 2,560,000/2,560,000 official cases hold. The unofficial vector suite carries ONE named, justified exception ($AB) for the oracle clash, with a stale-exception guard that fails if $AB ever starts passing
notes: FILED 2026-08-16 BY W2-12, from the first execution of suites that had been fetched-but-unrun since W0-03. TWO defects, and the evidence says they are probably ONE plus one: cpu_interrupts_v2 fails on 'nmi_and_brk' and cpu_timing_test6 fails on 'OP :$00' -- opcode $00 IS BRK. Two independent ROMs pointing at BRK is a strong signal; start by assuming they share a cause and try to refute that, rather than fixing them separately.

THE THIRD IS SEPARATE AND IS NOT A TIMING BUG: instr_test-v5 stops at 'AB ATX #n' (test 3 of 16, 03-immediate). $AB is LXA/ATX, one of the genuinely UNSTABLE illegal opcodes -- its result depends on an analog 'magic constant' that varies by chip and temperature. crate::cpu already models this family (`UnstableOp::Lxa`). The question is not 'what is the right answer' but 'which convention does this ROM expect', and blargg's is the one to match here. Do NOT change the magic constant without checking nes6502's 2.56M-case suite still passes: that suite covers $AB too, with SingleStepTests' own convention, and the two could disagree.

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: the CPU passes 2,560,000 SingleStepTests vectors and nestest byte-exact over all 8991 lines, and still fails these. Per-opcode vectors do not exercise an NMI arriving during BRK, and nestest's trace never takes an interrupt. That gap is precisely what W2-12 wired these suites to close.

MECHANISM: W2-12 waived all three in crates/rf-harness/waivers.toml against this ticket, with expiry 2026-11-01, so the local gate is green and any NEW CPU failure is visible immediately. The accuracy report refuses a waiver whose ticket is closed, so closing this ticket without deleting the waivers fails the gate -- which is what makes the last acceptance criterion self-enforcing.

SCOPE AMENDMENT 2026-08-16 (vetoable, recorded not taken silently): crates/rf-harness/** added to write_scope. Reason: Brad ruled $AB goes to $FF, which makes $AB fail 4422 of its 10000 nes6502 vector cases. The cargo-test exception alone was not enough -- scripts/local-gate.sh runs its OWN vector runner (rf_harness::nes6502_evidence) over all 256 opcode files, so the whole nes6502 accuracy row went red and the gate refused to emit evidence. The exclusion has to exist in both runners or the decision is not implementable.

DESIGN of that exclusion, deliberately not a skip: nes6502_evidence::EXCLUDED_OPCODES runs the excluded opcode ANYWAY and errors if it starts PASSING ("delete the exclusion rather than leaving it to mask the next regression"), and the excluded opcode still counts toward opcodes_tested (256, so the caller's partial-fetch guard and scripts/validate-evidence.mjs are untouched and still meaningful) while being left out of total_pass/total_fail. The exclusion is written into docs/evidence/local-gate.json as `vectors.excluded`, emitted even when empty -- an absent key reads as "nothing was excluded" whether or not that is true, and that file is what a reader trusts when told the vector suite is green.

FOLLOW-UP NOT TAKEN (out of scope, no ticket filed -- flagging rather than doing): scripts/validate-evidence.mjs still only asserts total_fail === 0 and knows nothing about `vectors.excluded`. It would be stronger if it required every excluded entry to carry a non-empty reason. Left alone because scripts/ is outside even the amended write_scope and the JSON is human-readable as-is.

Both #[ignore]d 5-minute replay goldens (alter_ego, rf_scroller) re-run under --release and UNMOVED, so the interrupt-poll change needed no re-baseline -- worth stating because cargo test --workspace reports them as ignored and would have passed while they were stale.

tickets.title: Tier-B accuracy gaps: PPU open-bus decay, CPU dummy cycles, OAM stress
acceptance: ppu_open_bus passes: a write to any PPU register sets the decay value, and the decay itself is modelled (FR-CORE-022)
cpu_exec_space 2/2: the write-only APU ports and the unallocated $4018-$40FF space return open bus, and code executes correctly from I/O space (FR-CORE-020)
cpu_dummy_reads and cpu_dummy_writes both 2/2 (FR-CORE-020)
oam_stress passes (FR-CORE-023)
ppu_read_buffer passes, or its frame budget is proven insufficient rather than assumed (it currently times out at 600 frames without ever leaving $80)
every waiver W2-09 added for these suites is DELETED rather than re-dated, and the Tier-B nightly is green with no waivers naming this ticket
notes: FILED 2026-08-16 BY W2-09, from the first run of the Tier-B nightly tier -- which is exactly what that tier is for. These are not speculative gaps: each is a real ROM failing today, with its own message quoted in W2-09's notes and in crates/rf-harness/waivers.toml.

PPU OPEN-BUS DECAY IS THE COMMON ROOT of at least three of these. ppu_open_bus says outright 'Write to any PPU register should set decay value'; cpu_exec_space's PPU arm fails with 'PPU open bus implementation is missing or incomplete: A write to $2003, followed by a read from $2001 should return the same value as was written'. This crate models an open-bus LATCH (`NesBus::open_bus`) but not the PPU's own decaying bus, and not writes to write-only PPU registers refreshing it. Start there: it is likely to move cpu_exec_space's PPU arm and ppu_open_bus together.

cpu_exec_space's APU arm is a separate gap in the same family: it enumerates $4000-$4016 and the unallocated $4018-$40FF and expects open bus from every one. W2-01a's APU made $4015 a real register; the write-only ports and the unallocated space still need to read as open bus rather than as whatever `read_untimed` currently returns.

ppu_read_buffer TIMES OUT rather than failing -- 600 frames elapsed with $6000 never leaving $80 (running). Do NOT simply raise the budget until it passes: establish first whether the ROM is genuinely slow or whether this engine has stalled it, because a budget raised to hide a hang is the exact shape of a gate that stops gating.

MECHANISM ALREADY IN PLACE: W2-09's `tier_b_suites` binary consults crates/rf-harness/waivers.toml, so today's failures are waived-with-justification against THIS ticket and the nightly is green. That means a NEW Tier-B failure is visible immediately -- and it also means this ticket's last acceptance criterion (delete the waivers, do not re-date them) is what proves the work actually landed.

DONE 2026-08-16. All 7 Tier-B waivers DELETED, not re-dated; `tier_b_suites` runs green with zero waivers naming this ticket (TOTAL 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 waived, 5 not fetched -- the 5 are golden_frame/audio_rms protocols with no Tier-B runner, plus unfetched ROMs, counted as skips and never as passes).

ROOT CAUSE WAS ONE BUG FOR FOUR ROMS, as the ticket predicted (it predicted three): the PPU has its OWN open-bus latch, separate from the CPU bus's. blargg's ppu_open_bus readme opens with exactly that sentence. Implementing the decay register per its table fixed ppu_open_bus, BOTH cpu_exec_space arms and cpu_dummy_writes_ppumem. Per-bit decay clocks were forced by the ROM: its tests 7 and 9 refresh PART of the register in a loop for a full second and then require the unrefreshed bits to have decayed anyway, which a single shared timer cannot do.

SECOND BUG, found by measurement not inference: `Controller::default` had `shift_index = 8`, so a never-strobed pad read back as EXHAUSTED and returned 1 on read #0 of a session. cpu_exec_space_apu catches it because it executes code from all 256 addresses in $4000-$40FF, each of which must read back $40 (the address high byte, still on the bus) = RTI; at $4016 the pad ORed in bit 0, making $41 = EOR, a two-byte opcode, and execution derailed into the ROM's own BRK trap. Isolated by patching $4016/$4017 to pure open bus (ROM then passed all 256), then confirmed by instrumenting the first read.

BUDGETS: proven insufficient, not raised until green -- the ticket forbade the latter explicitly and it would have been the easy wrong move. Bisected completion frames: ppu_read_buffer ~1300 vs a budget of 600 (and the ROM SAYS it is slow on screen: "This next test will take a while. In order to distract you with entertainment, art is provided."), oam_stress ~3620 vs 3600 -- short by TWENTY frames, which is why it reported a partial CRC rather than an obvious timeout. New budgets 2000 and 5400 (~1.5x measured need): enough headroom to not flake, little enough that a real hang still surfaces in seconds.

THIRD PROTOCOL MISTAG IN THE PROJECT: cpu_dummy_reads never writes the $6001-$6003 signature at all -- it is screen-only -- so under `six_thousand` it read as "never reached its test-status init" and W2-09 waived it as a hang. It PASSES, in under 200 frames; it was never slow and never broken. Same class as branch_timing_tests and cpu_timing_test6 (both W2-12). Rule worth keeping: an unexplained "signature never valid" is a suspected protocol mistag before it is a bug. Fixing the tag alone would have moved the ROM onto tier_b_suites' SKIP list, so that binary gained a screen_text path -- otherwise this ticket would have traded a false failure for a silent gap.

SCOPE AMENDMENTS (all vetoable, all recorded rather than taken silently). tests/rom-manifest.toml -- the protocol tag and the two frame budgets live there and criterion 5 is explicitly about a budget. crates/retroforge/** and crates/rf-state/** -- the decay register is real machine state ($2000-$2006 reads return it), so it had to enter the PPU_ chunk, and that is a wire-format change. crates/rf-harness/** for the tier_b_suites screen_text path.

SAVE-STATE DESIGN CHANGE worth knowing about: a single global CHUNK_VERSION constant in crates/retroforge was the wrong shape the moment ONE chunk changed -- bumping it would have declared CPU_/APU_/WRAM/etc. changed too and made the reader reject four chunks byte-identical to what it already understands. Replaced with a per-tag lookup of rf-state's own TagInfo::current_version, which is what that registry is for; writer and reader are now literally the same number, and PPU_ alone went to 2. Two test fixtures that hardcoded version 1 were switched to the registry as well, since a hardcoded 1 silently became a CannotMigrate fixture the moment a version moved.

FINDING, NOT FIXED, worth a ticket if save states are ever shipped: rf-state's MigrationRegistry has NO production user. The app never calls Container::decode at all yet (only tests do), and this -- the first real payload version bump -- could not use the registry anyway, because the migration (append 9 zero bytes to a v1 PPU_ payload) is NES payload knowledge and rf-state is forbidden to have any. FR-STATE-005 ("every released .rfstate fixture loads on current main") is therefore not actually exercised by anything today: rf-state's golden_v1.rfstate is built from DUMMY 16-byte payloads, so it pins the container envelope, not payload compatibility. Nothing has been released (W5-05 is the release ticket), so nothing is broken yet -- but a real PPU_ v1->v2 migration, and a decision about where migrations live given the layer rule, is owed BEFORE the first tagged release.

BOTH #[ignore]d 5-minute replay goldens re-run under --release after the controller change and are UNMOVED -- the check that actually matters for a change to input state, and one cargo test --workspace cannot make. The .rfstate golden fixtures DID move (twice: once for the PPU_ payload, once for the controller power-on state) and were regenerated deliberately through their own documented --ignored commands, never edited to go green.

tickets.title: PPU catch-up scheduler (the second half of FR-MODE-004)
acceptance: the compatibility config selects a PPU catch-up scheduler in place of lock-step per-CPU-cycle ticking (EMULATION_CORES section 5 row 1; crate::ppu's "Scheduling: lock-step, not catch-up" section owes exactly this)

W3-07's diff runs clean over the whole executed suite with the scheduler enabled -- catch-up is the one section 5 row whose "risk of compat setting" is stated as "none if catch-up correct", so unlike the open-bus switch it must produce NO divergence
ppu_vbl_nmi stays 10/10, mmc3_irq_tests stays green, and the accuracy path is bit-identical to today -- the scheduler may not be paid for out of the accuracy mode
notes: FILED 2026-08-17 BY W3-07, split on Brad's ruling. This is a SCHEDULER REDESIGN, not an optimisation, and the reason is specific: catch-up requires that nothing observe PPU state between flush points, and in this engine three things observe it at DOT granularity on every single CPU cycle.

(1) `cpu::exec::CountingBus::sample` calls `CpuBus::nmi_line` after EVERY bus op. Worse, W1-05c's fix depends on `NesBus::nmi_level_latch` being snapshotted per DOT rather than per cycle -- `tick_master`'s own doc records that a whole-cycle-wide version was tried first and measured exactly 2 PPU dots too wide against ppu_vbl_nmi 05-08. That suite is 10/10 today and this is what it rests on.
(2) `NesBus::tick_ppu_dot` drains filtered A12 rising edges into the mapper every dot; mmc3_irq_tests and mmc3_test_2 depend on that granularity (see crate::mappers' "MMC3 additions" section).

(3) Two things added in 2026-08 now key off dot counts as well: W2-19's `Ppu::age_decay_register` (per frame, driven from the dot loop) and W2-01d's `Ppu::last_2007_read_dot`, which detects a back-to-back `$2007` read as "exactly 3 dots ago".

THEREFORE the real work is PREDICTION: computing when the next NMI edge and the next A12 edge can occur, so the PPU can be safely skipped ahead to that point instead of ticked. Budget for that, not for a deferral counter. A naive "flush on register access" catch-up gains nothing here, because `nmi_line` is polled every cycle -- it would flush every cycle.
The diff W3-07 built is the tool for this ticket: run it with the scheduler on and it reports exactly where catch-up and lock-step disagree, which is the debugging loop rather than an afterthought.

tickets.title: Compatibility config path + accuracy-vs-compatibility diff (FR-MODE-004)
acceptance: CoreConfig::accuracy_mode is plumbed into rf-nes and selects a real second path. AMENDED 2026-08-17 (Brad): the second path is EMULATION_CORES section 5's "Open-bus modeling: full | simplified" switch, NOT the PPU catch-up scheduler -- that is split to W3-07b, see notes
the accuracy-vs-compatibility diff runs the whole executed test-ROM suite under both configs and reports any divergence (FR-MODE-004, EMULATION_CORES section 5's "CI diffs both")

the diff FAILS on an undeclared divergence, and equally FAILS when a DECLARED divergence stops happening -- section 5 says "divergences must be test-suite-visible, or the switch doesn't exist", so a compatibility switch that diverges nowhere is a switch that is not there, and the diff must say so
the diff is proven non-vacuous: a deliberately wrong compatibility path must make it fail, demonstrated the way W2-05's apu_mixer mutation was
nightly runs the diff (docs/TESTING.md section 4/9)
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W2-09 2026-08-16 (Brad's ruling). W2-09's criterion 5 asked for an accuracy-vs-compatibility diff over the test-ROM suite. It is NOT IMPLEMENTABLE as of that ticket, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of effort: `CoreConfig::accuracy_mode` is never plumbed into rf-nes at all, and rf-nes has exactly ONE code path -- EMULATION_CORES section 5's compatibility switches (PPU catch-up stepping, OAM decay off, simplified open bus) do not exist. A diff today would compare a path against itself and pass forever, which is precisely the class of vacuous check this project keeps removing.

SO THE SWITCH AND THE DIFF ARE ONE TICKET. A diff has no meaning without a second path, and a second path without a diff is exactly what EMULATION_CORES section 5 forbids ('CI diffs both'). Building them together is also what makes the third acceptance criterion possible: a deliberately wrong compatibility path must break the diff, or the diff is decoration.

PRE-FLIGHT already paid: crate::ppu's module doc, 'Scheduling: lock-step, not catch-up' section, records that W1-04a built lock-step only and names the catch-up path as an explicit debt, including the CI-diff requirement. Read that before starting -- it states what the second path must be equivalent to and why.

SPLIT 2026-08-17 (Brad's ruling). The original bundled the DIFF with the PPU CATCH-UP SCHEDULER. The scheduler is not an increment on this architecture, it is a scheduler redesign, and it lands on top of every accuracy gate: correct catch-up needs NMI and A12 edge PREDICTION, because three separate things observe PPU state at DOT granularity every cycle. (1) `cpu::exec::CountingBus::sample` calls `CpuBus::nmi_line` after EVERY bus op, and W1-05c's ppu_vbl_nmi 10/10 depends on `NesBus::nmi_level_latch` being snapshotted per DOT, not per cycle -- its own doc records that a whole-cycle version measured exactly 2 rows too wide. (2) `tick_ppu_dot` drains A12 rising edges into the mapper every dot, which mmc3_irq_tests depends on. (3) W2-19's decay ageing and W2-01d's `$2007` double-read latch both key off dot counts. Any deferral coarser than a dot breaks these. Filed as W3-07b with that analysis, so whoever takes it does not rediscover it.

WHY THE OPEN-BUS SWITCH IS THE RIGHT SECOND PATH, and not a consolation prize: section 5 lists six switches, and open-bus modelling is the one this crate can now actually offer BOTH sides of. W2-19 built the full model (the PPU's own decay register with per-bit ageing); "simplified" is what this crate did before it. The other candidate, "NES OAM decay: emulated | off", is not available -- this crate does not emulate OAM decay at all, so "off" is the only side that exists and a diff would compare a path against itself, the exact vacuity the original note warned about.

THE ACCEPTANCE INVERTS THE USUAL INSTINCT, deliberately. Section 5: "Compatibility never changes observable game-facing behavior for the supported library -- divergences must be test-suite-visible, or the switch doesn't exist." So the diff going green everywhere is a FAILURE condition, not a success: it means the switch does nothing. Declared divergences are enforced in both directions, the same discipline `waivers.toml` applies to known-fails and `tier_b_suites` applies to a waiver over a ROM that has started passing.

DONE 2026-08-17. `mode_diff` compares 52 ROMs under both CoreConfig modes; exactly one diverges, it is the declared one, and the divergence message is the one section 5 predicts ("Decay value should become zero by one second"). Wired into nightly.

NON-VACUITY PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS against the real suite, the way W2-05's apu_mixer mutation was. (1) Break the compatibility path somewhere undeclared (XOR bit 0 of $2002 when !accuracy_mode): a second ROM diverges, UNDECLARED DIVERGENCE is reported, exit 1. (2) Make the switch a NO-OP (age the decay register in both modes): 0 of 52 diverge, STALE DECLARATION is reported, exit 1. Baseline: 1 divergence, exit 0. Mutation 2 is the one that matters -- everything agreeing is a FAILURE here, and that is not the usual instinct.

WHY BOTH DIRECTIONS: EMULATION_CORES section 5 says "divergences must be test-suite-visible, or the switch doesn't exist". A diff that only caught undeclared divergences would go green the moment someone deleted the compatibility path -- both configs would run the same code and agree everywhere, which is exactly the vacuous state this ticket's own note warned about ("a diff today would compare a path against itself and pass forever"). The stale-declaration rule is the direct analog of tier_b_suites' rule that a waiver over a now-passing ROM is itself an error.

DESIGN NOTE on what the comparison key is: the verdict AND its message, not a bare pass/fail. Two runs that both fail but fail at DIFFERENT sub-tests have diverged, and folding them together would hide precisely the class of difference this diff exists to surface.

HONEST ABOUT WHAT THE SWITCH BUYS: simplicity, not measurable speed. Ageing eight decay bits once per frame is not a hot path. Section 5's column for this row is "full | simplified", not fast/slow. The reason to build it now is that it is the one section 5 switch this crate can offer BOTH sides of -- W2-19 built the full model, and "simplified" is what this crate did before it. The obvious alternative, "NES OAM decay: emulated | off", is unavailable: this crate does not emulate OAM decay at all, so only one side exists and the diff would compare a path against itself.

accuracy_mode is deliberately NOT serialized into the PPU_ chunk, for the same reason event_mask is not: it is caller configuration, not machine state. Restoring it from a file would let a saved state silently switch a running session's mode -- and since the mode changes observable reads, a state saved in Compatibility would drag a session out of Accuracy, which law 6 ("a fresh install boots in Accuracy Mode") exists to prevent.
SCOPE AMENDMENT (vetoable, recorded): .github/workflows/nightly.yml, required by criterion 5 ("nightly runs the diff") and not in the original write_scope.

tickets.title: Shader chain: CRT + scalers
acceptance: WGSL pass chain with param UBOs (FR-REND-003) -- the reusable chain infrastructure every later shader plugs into

the THREE ARITHMETICALLY SIMPLE first-party shaders per RENDERER.md section 4: nearest, sharp-bilinear, scanlines. The three harder ones (crt-easymode-class, lcd-grid, xbr-class) are SPLIT OUT to W3-02a, where the clean-room licensing risk is concentrated
runtime selectable, with an empty chain `[]` valid and equivalent to passthrough (RENDERER.md section 4's own example)
per-shader provenance recorded in a manifest, including the licence and a statement of how the WGSL was authored -- the format is set here and W3-02a follows it

a NONZERO tolerance threshold is calibrated for at least one filtering shader using W3-01b's harness, since filtering is what RENDERER.md section 7's non-hashability warning is actually about (W3-01b measured nearest-neighbour integer scaling as byte-exact, so the harness has not yet had to size a real allowance)
notes: PRE-FLIGHT + CLAIM 2026-08-08 (conductor, HEAD 301c3f7, baseline 699 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored). SPLIT 8 -> 5 PTS ON THE LICENSING LINE, not arbitrarily: crt-easymode-class, lcd-grid and xbr-class all have widely-circulated GPL implementations and are moved to W3-02a, where the clean-room risk gets its own focused brief and provenance review. The three that stay -- nearest, sharp-bilinear, scanlines -- are arithmetically trivial and carry no such risk, so this ticket is really about the CHAIN INFRASTRUCTURE every later shader plugs into. Scope crates/rf-renderer/** is not self-blocking; tests live under it.

THE CHAIN IS THE DELIVERABLE. RENDERER.md section 4's own examples make the shape explicit -- `[crt-easymode, vignette]`, `[xbrz4]`, or `[]` -- so an EMPTY chain must be valid and equivalent to passthrough. Get param UBOs, ordering, and the manifest format right here, because W3-02a and every later shader inherit all three. A manifest format that cannot express 'licence + basis + how the WGSL was authored' will have to be redesigned in the ticket where it matters most.

TOLERANCE FINALLY EARNS A NONZERO THRESHOLD -- this is the ticket where W3-01b's harness stops being theoretical. W3-01b measured nearest-neighbour integer scaling as BYTE-EXACT on Metal (0 of 65,632 pixels differing, max channel delta 0), so it correctly ships with channel_delta 0 rather than an invented allowance. Filtering is what RENDERER.md section 7's 'not hashable past 1x' warning is ACTUALLY about, so sharp-bilinear is the natural place to size a real threshold. Calibrate against measured noise and mutation-verify that the threshold STILL REJECTS a wrong image -- a threshold that passes a visibly wrong render is worse than no test at all.

LICENSING APPLIES EVEN TO THE SIMPLE THREE, in one specific way: `nearest` and `scanlines` are trivial arithmetic nobody can own, but the WGSL must still be authored rather than transcribed, and each manifest must say so. That habit is what makes W3-02a's harder claim credible. Note `cargo deny check licenses` only sees Cargo dependencies and will NEVER look at a .wgsl file -- this is review-enforced, the same class as the rf-cache SystemTime exemption and W2-10's vendored-C question.

WGPU 29 TRAPS, verified by compile-probe (docs/TECH_STACK.md section 2) -- two W3-01 attempts stalled to ZERO code on these: InstanceDescriptor has no Default (new_without_display_handle()); Instance::new takes the descriptor BY VALUE; enumerate_adapters returns a FUTURE; Device::poll needs a BOUNDED timeout (`None` blocks forever, the actual stall cause); ImageCopy* is TexelCopy*; bind_group_layouts is &[Option<&BindGroupLayout>] with immediate_size; RenderPassColorAttachment needs depth_slice. validate-arch.sh rule 5: exactly ONE wgpu in Cargo.lock, ever.

BUILD ON WHAT EXISTS, do not fork it: crates/rf-renderer/src/original_pipeline.rs (PalettePass), scale.rs (ScalePass, W3-01b), composite.rs (EnhancedCompositor, W4-03c) and gpu.rs (GpuContext::request_headless + from_shared, plus the shared align_up and read_buffer_sync helpers). W3-01b noted ScalePass is not yet chained to PalettePass anywhere -- if this ticket's chain work makes that wiring natural, doing it here is in scope and closes one of W3-01b's four recorded partials.

VACUITY TRAPS. (a) A pass-chain test with ONE pass cannot detect ordering bugs -- chain at least two and assert the result differs from the reverse order. (b) An empty-chain test that asserts 'no panic' proves nothing; assert it is byte-identical to the unfiltered input. (c) A param-UBO test that never CHANGES a parameter cannot tell whether the UBO is bound at all -- vary a parameter and assert the output changes. This board has caught five tests that exercised a path without discriminating it; do not add a sixth.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 at 6ad7ea5. Gate verified INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok, exactly one wgpu in Cargo.lock; workspace 712 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored (baseline 699, +13).

THE TOLERANCE HARNESS FINALLY EARNED A NONZERO THRESHOLD, which is what this ticket was predicted to deliver and did. SHARP_BILINEAR_TOLERANCE = { channel_delta: 1, max_mismatch_fraction: 0.0 }, measured across ELEVEN configs on Metal (7x13 through 256x240, sharpness 0.0-1.0): at channel_delta 0 the mismatch ran 0-17.9% and ALWAYS by no more than one unit -- ordinary GPU-vs-CPU float rounding -- and channel_delta 1 brought every config to zero. CI pins the LOWER bound mechanically by asserting channel_delta 0 fails two of those configs, so the threshold cannot be silently tightened into flakiness nor loosened without a test noticing.

THE UPPER BOUND IS HONESTLY REPORTED AS LOOSE, and that distinction is worth keeping: the mutations fail at max delta 65-69, so they would equally reject at 3 or at 10. `1` is the tightest value the MEASURED NOISE requires, not a value the mutations forced. Saying so is the difference between a calibrated threshold and a plausible-looking number -- a report claiming the mutations 'confirmed' the threshold would have been overclaiming.

MANIFEST FORMAT SET HERE FOR W3-02a TO INHERIT: { id, display_name, license, basis: Option<&str>, authorship, params }. `basis` is a STRUCTURED field rather than prose specifically because W3-02a must record 'Hyllian's xBR (MIT), not xBRZ GPL-3.0' somewhere a reviewer can find it -- and because `cargo deny check licenses` never inspects a .wgsl file, so provenance is review-enforced and needs a defined home. It is None for all three shaders here, since none has a named upstream; W3-02a is where the field becomes load-bearing.

A GAP CAUGHT ON REVIEW, worth recording as a pattern: `nearest` was constructed, selectable and manifest-documented but NEVER ACTUALLY RENDERED by any test. A pipeline stage can be fully wired and still never have produced a pixel -- that is a new costume for this board's recurring exercises-but-does-not-discriminate failure, and it is easy to miss precisely because everything around it looks complete. Now covered by a 2x2 -> 8x8 exact block-replication test.

EMPTY CHAIN IS ASSERTED BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE INPUT AND NEVER TOUCHES THE GPU -- not merely 'does not panic', which was the named vacuity trap. RENDERER.md section 4's `[]` example is thereby made VALID rather than tolerated. Ordering is covered too: [scanlines, upscale] versus the reverse, asserted to differ.

CLOSED ONE OF W3-01b's FOUR RECORDED PARTIALS: crates/rf-renderer/src/pipeline.rs::run() now chains PalettePass -> ScalePass -> ShaderChain in a single call, verified byte-identical to invoking the three passes by hand, plus an empty-chain passthrough variant. W3-01b's remaining three partials (FractionalFill dimension-tested only, no SNES-shaped input exercised, user override is a constructor parameter rather than a UI control) are untouched and still open.

SINGLE-BACKEND (Metal) MEASUREMENT, same posture as W3-01 and W3-01b: a red llvmpipe/lavapipe run in CI is a CROSS-BACKEND QUESTION TO INVESTIGATE FIRST, not automatically a regression. This now applies to a real nonzero threshold rather than to an exact-match default, so the first CI run on a software adapter is genuinely informative -- if channel_delta 1 proves too tight there, the fix is a measured wider value with the lower-bound assertion updated in lockstep, never a silent widening.

tickets.title: CRT, LCD-grid and xBR-class shaders (clean-room, MIT basis)
acceptance: crt-easymode-class, lcd-grid and xbr-class shaders as WGSL passes in the chain W3-02 built, each with param UBOs and manifest provenance

SHADER LICENSING LAW (design review G-42) satisfied and demonstrably so: the upscaler is based on Hyllian's xBR (MIT), NEVER xBRZ (Zenju, GPL-3.0) and never a libretro GPL port. Each manifest records licence, basis and how the WGSL was authored
each shader's output compared against a reference image using W3-01b's tolerance harness with a CALIBRATED nonzero threshold, and a mutation proving that threshold still rejects a wrong image
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W3-02 2026-08-08 in pre-flight, on the licensing line rather than arbitrarily. RENDERER.md section 4's shader licensing law (design review G-42) is a CLEAN-ROOM requirement, not merely an attribution one: 'the upscaler is based on Hyllian's xBR (MIT) -- never xBRZ (Zenju, GPL-3.0) or libretro GPL... whoever writes the WGSL must not have the GPL/unlicensed libretro shaders' in front of them. All three of this ticket's shaders are the ones with widely-circulated GPL implementations; W3-02's three (nearest, sharp-bilinear, scanlines) are arithmetically trivial and carry no such risk. Concentrating the risk in one ticket means it gets its own focused brief and its own provenance review instead of being a footnote on an 8-pointer.

THE GATE CANNOT CATCH A LICENCE VIOLATION HERE -- `cargo deny check licenses` only sees Cargo dependencies and will never look at a .wgsl file. This is review-enforced, exactly like the rf-cache SystemTime exemption (W4-08) and the vendored-C question (W2-10). Same class of hazard: a rule the linter structurally cannot see.

PARALLEL TO NFR-011's CORE RULE, which is the useful mental model: emulation cores are 'first-party clean-room implementations from hardware documentation -- no ported or transcribed third-party emulator source'. Shaders get the same treatment. Write from the published ALGORITHM (xBR's edge-detection rules are documented independently of any one implementation), not from a remembered GPL source file, and say in the manifest which it was.

TOLERANCE FINALLY EARNS A NONZERO THRESHOLD HERE. W3-01b measured nearest-neighbour integer scaling as BYTE-EXACT on Metal (0 of 65,632 pixels differing), so its harness ships with channel_delta 0 -- correct, because inventing an allowance with no measured noise would have made it vacuous. Filtering shaders are what RENDERER.md section 7's non-hashability warning is actually about, so this is where a real threshold must be sized. Calibrate it against measured cross-run/backend noise and mutation-verify that it STILL REJECTS a wrong image; a threshold that passes a visibly wrong render is worse than no test.
DONE 2026-08-17. All three shipped: crt (CRT-class), lcd-grid (LCD-grid-style), xbr (xBR-class), each with param UBOs, ChainStage constructors and a full ShaderManifest.

AUTHORSHIP RULING (Brad, 2026-08-17), and it is recorded in every file rather than buried: G-42's literal test is that the WGSL author 'must not have the GPL/unlicensed libretro sources open'. That test was written for a human and does not mean the same thing for an LLM author which may have been TRAINED on those sources. Flagged before writing anything rather than quietly interpreted. Brad ruled: write all three, document provenance in full. So each WGSL file opens with a PROVENANCE block that DERIVES every term from stated reasoning a reviewer can check line by line -- gaussian beam profile, aperture mask, gamma round-trip; cell-gap geometry, subpixel stripes; one diagonal-edge comparison with a luma-weighted distance -- instead of asserting an unverifiable 'sources closed'. Each manifest's authorship field carries the caveat verbatim, so a human licence review knows exactly what to audit.

THE UPSCALER, specifically, because it is the G-42-critical one: `basis` names Hyllian's xBR (MIT) as the permitted family and EXPLICITLY rules out xBRZ (Zenju, GPL-3.0) and libretro GPL ports. It is also not a transcription of Hyllian's MIT xBR -- MIT would have PERMITTED a credited port, but a port is not what this is, and claiming one would misstate the provenance in the other direction. The implementation is deliberately SIMPLER than real xBR (one 2x2 comparison versus a larger neighbourhood and a multi-level weighted rule table), so the '-class' label is accurate rather than modest, and display_name is asserted to be exactly "xBR-class".

TOLERANCE FINALLY EARNED A NONZERO THRESHOLD, and only where measurement justified it. Calibration run (Metal, 64x48 synthetic source, `calibrate_w3_02a_tolerances`, kept #[ignore]d for re-measurement): crt max channel delta 1 (0.0145% mismatched at delta 0), lcd-grid max channel delta 1 (14.68% at delta 0), xbr max channel delta 0 (0.00%). So crt and lcd-grid ship channel_delta 1 -- this crate's FIRST nonzero threshold, exactly what the brief predicted -- with max_mismatch_fraction still 0.0, because at delta 1 zero pixels mismatch and the threshold does all its work where the noise actually is (pow and smoothstep evaluating differently on GPU and CPU).

XBR KEEPS channel_delta 0 DELIBERATELY. It came back BYTE-EXACT: its arithmetic is comparisons plus one mix(_, _, 0.5), no transcendental anywhere. Giving it an allowance it has not earned is precisely the vacuity W3-01b refused when it shipped nearest-neighbour at 0 -- an unmeasured threshold tests nothing. Recorded so a future backend showing real noise is sized against THAT measurement rather than this one.

tickets.title: Renderer device-loss + shader-compile fallback
acceptance: device-loss or shader-compile failure falls back to the original pipeline within 1s with emulation uninterrupted (FR-REND-007)

a SIMULATED device-loss test drives the fallback path at runtime -- injecting a real failure, never compiling the pipeline out, since a fallback that is only reachable by deleting its alternative is not a tested fallback
every GPU wait in the test is bounded and cannot hang the suite: no unbounded device.poll, no awaiting a device-lost callback that may never fire
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W3-01 2026-08-07 (conductor, on Brad's authorization of a third attempt). W3-01 stalled TWICE at the 600s watchdog, and the evidence points at this criterion specifically rather than at the pipeline: attempt 1 reported the palette pass working 'end-to-end on real Metal hardware' and then froze immediately on 'verify the device-loss callback mechanism'. Isolating it means a hang here can no longer swallow the pipeline work, which is what happened twice.

THE HAZARD, named so it is not walked into a third time: a device-lost callback may NEVER FIRE, and awaiting one blocks forever. Likewise wgpu's readback pattern (buffer.map_async then device.poll) deadlocks trivially if poll is never called or uses the wrong mode. The conductor PROVED the environment is fine -- a headless adapter+device request succeeds here on Metal / Apple M5 Max with no hang -- so any stall in this ticket is a blocking call, not a missing GPU. Bound every wait; if a GPU call has not returned in seconds, stop and report rather than grind.

START FROM THE VERIFIED SKELETON in docs/TECH_STACK.md's 'wgpu 29 API traps' section rather than writing wgpu setup from memory: InstanceDescriptor has no Default (use new_without_display_handle), Instance::new takes the descriptor by value, and enumerate_adapters returns a Future. All three are compile errors rather than loud failures, and the conductor hit all three in sequence while probing.

DONE 2026-08-17, and it did NOT hang. Five GPU tests, whole suite green, fallback measured at ~50-120 MICROSECONDS against the 1-second budget. Every run was executed under an explicit external watchdog (background PID + bounded poll loop + kill) rather than trusting the ticket's own timeout, because that is what the two previous stalls cost.

THE KEY FACT, and the reason the previous attempts had nothing to branch on: wgpu reports validation errors OUT-OF-BAND. A shader that fails to compile does not return Err from create_shader_module -- it reaches the device's uncaptured-error handler, whose default is to PANIC the process. So FR-REND-007 is literally unimplementable until you capture those: `fallback::guarded` wraps GPU work in a wgpu::ErrorScope and turns a captured validation error into an Err. That seam is the whole ticket.

HANG AVOIDED BY VERIFICATION, NOT BY HOPE. The module awaits exactly ONE future, and it is already resolved when created -- checked against the vendored wgpu-29.0.4 source rather than assumed: backend/wgpu_core.rs's `pop_error_scope` ends `Box::pin(ready(scope.error))`, i.e. std::future::ready, Poll::Ready on first poll, needing no device.poll to progress. wgpu's own doc on ErrorScopeGuard::pop agrees in prose ("The pop takes effect immediately"). Device::set_device_lost_callback is deliberately NOT USED ANYWHERE in this crate -- it is the one API whose contract permits never firing, and it is what the acceptance criterion names.

SCOPE WIDENED BEYOND A BOOLEAN, deliberately: the first cut returned `Failed` (no pixels) on device loss, which satisfies "never abort emulation" and fails criterion 1's "falls back to the ORIGINAL PIPELINE". Device loss is recoverable on every backend this targets -- driver reset, GPU switch, suspend -- so FallbackRenderer RECREATES the device and retries once on the original pipeline, reporting RecoveredOnOriginal. "No picture, forever" would have met the letter of the requirement and none of its intent.

ALSO ADDED because a real caller needs it: a STICKY shader-disable. A chain that failed to compile will not start compiling, so retrying it every frame pays the failure cost 60 times a second. After the first failure the chain is dropped for the session and later frames report OriginalFallback without touching it.

THE TESTS INJECT REAL FAILURES, per criterion 2. Device loss: `Device::destroy()`. Shader failure: WGSL that genuinely does not compile (a naga VALIDATION error -- calling a nonexistent function -- not a parse error, since that is the likelier shape for a real third-party shader), fed through `try_enable_shader`, which is the production path a user-selected shader will arrive by when W3-02a lands. Nothing is compiled out, no GPU is stubbed, and each test FIRST asserts the enhanced path works on the same objects -- so a fallback that was always taken would fail rather than pass. The compile test also asserts a VALID shader still compiles through the same guarded path, so it cannot pass by rejecting everything.

PACED (tests/frame_bundle_perf.rs, existing harness): 60.10 fps debug and 60.06 release against NTSC's 60.0988 Hz -- 1.000x, unchanged, which is the half that had to NOT move. UNPACED headroom needed a new measurement because paced throughput is capped at 60 Hz by design and both configurations sit at the cap, so the saving is structurally invisible there; the new test drives CoreCommand::StepFrame, which produces a frame on demand with no pacer wait and is therefore the real per-frame WORK cost.

THE UNPACED NUMBERS, all four runs: debug +7.4% (19.687 -> 18.225 ms/frame, 1.462 ms saved); release across three runs -0.5%, +11.8%, +6.8%. The FIRST release run showed no saving at all, which is why it was re-run rather than reported -- on a shared machine this measurement carries real variance, and one run is not a result. The saving is genuine (three of four runs positive, median ~7%) but noisy, and that is the honest characterisation rather than 'measurably improves' full stop.

THE ASSERTION IS DELIBERATELY THE WEAK ONE -- extraction-off must not be more than 5% SLOWER -- precisely because of that variance. A strict 'must be faster' assertion would have failed on the -0.5% run and been quietly loosened later, which is how a perf gate becomes decoration. The numbers are printed for a human; the assertion only catches the failure mode that matters (a toggle whose branch costs more than the work it removes).

TWO TESTS THAT FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is what makes the gate non-vacuous: `step_frame_command_also_delivers_bg_layer_content_not_just_size` (pre-existing, now sends SetLayerExtraction(true) first) proves the toggle ON still delivers real layer content; the new `layer_extraction_is_off_until_asked_for` proves the toggle OFF sends no layer bytes at all while the main frame still arrives. An implementation that ignored the toggle in either direction fails one of them.

RELOAD HAZARD HANDLED, and there was a documented precedent for exactly it: a fresh core thread starts with extraction off, so if the Layers window was already open across a ROM reload the new core would silently never extract. app.rs re-asserts SetLayerExtraction(true) on load, right beside the sprite-overlay re-send and for the same reason `event_subscription_active` is reset there -- that reset has a paragraph of its own explaining the identical trap.

W3-03's OWN REASONING WAS REVERSED, deliberately and with its comment updated rather than deleted: it kept layer textures current every frame regardless of the checkbox, on the grounds that the upload was cheap next to the main one and that a stale image would flash when the window opened. Both true. But it left the CORE THREAD paying for the split and clones forever, and the stale-image cost is bounded at one frame (<=16.6 ms at 60 Hz) -- under a human's flicker threshold, and far cheaper than paying for it every frame of every session. The UI now keys off whether layer bytes actually arrived rather than its own copy of show_layers, so the two cannot disagree during the one frame a command is in flight.

tickets.title: Side-by-side original/enhanced compare view
acceptance: synchronized dual viewport, same frame (FR-REND-005)
screenshot captures both (FR-FE-005)
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. rf_renderer::compare (compose_split + blink_shows_original + original_rgba_from_indexed) as PURE functions, rf_renderer::png as a dependency-free encoder, and the shell wiring: a Compare menu with Off / Split (divider slider) / A-B blink, plus a screenshot action.

'SYNCED FRAME' (FR-REND-005) IS STRUCTURAL HERE, NOT MAINTAINED, and finding that pairing was the actual design work. The shell had no second same-geometry buffer: the ultrawide/enhanced camera is a different size, and scaling one into the other would have meant inventing a policy this ticket has no business guessing. The pair that DOES exist: the enhanced half is what the shell already displays (FrameBuffer::overlay_scanline paints the enhancement over the accuracy frame), and the original half is FrameBundle::video, whose own doc says 'always the accuracy-exact stream: assembled from video_scanline only, never overlay_scanline'. Same frame, same 256x240 geometry, read inside one pump_core_events call under the ordering comment that already establishes bundle-before-frame. If the geometries ever disagree the pair is DROPPED rather than composed misaligned.

THE SPLIT COMPOSES A BUFFER rather than clipping two draws, which is what a UI toolkit would do. Composing is what lets one function answer both acceptance criteria: what is on screen and what a capture contains cannot disagree. It also makes the divider testable by reading pixels rather than by driving a UI -- `moving_the_divider_moves_the_boundary` asserts the boundary actually moves, which a fixed 50/50 split labelled 'draggable' would fail.

PNG WITHOUT A DEPENDENCY, and the reasoning is the point. There is no image codec in this workspace and no TECH_STACK row for one, so adding png/image would have been a TECH_STACK decision with an NFR-011 licence review attached -- a different ticket's work. Instead: zlib permits STORED (uncompressed) deflate blocks (RFC 1951 section 3.2.4), so a conformant PNG needs only CRC-32 and Adler-32, both implemented from their specifications and checked against their published test vectors (0xCBF43926 for '123456789', 0x11E60398 for 'Wikipedia'). HONEST TRADE, stated in the module doc and in RENDERER section 6: files are roughly raw-RGBA sized (~245 KB for a 256x240 frame vs ~10-40 KB compressed) -- fine for a deliberate screenshot, WRONG for anything per-frame, so section 6's Phase-8 video capture must not be built on it.

VERIFIED WITH INDEPENDENT DECODERS, not only its own round-trip: `file` reports 'PNG image data, 64 x 40, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced'; macOS `sips` decodes it and reports the right dimensions; Python's zlib.decompress inflates the IDAT to exactly the expected byte count with every chunk CRC validating. The in-crate test additionally decodes the stored-block stream by hand at a size that SPANS MORE THAN ONE BLOCK (>65535 raw bytes), which is the boundary a single-block implementation silently gets wrong.

COST GATED, following W3-03a from the day before: the two buffers are cloned only while compare mode is on, or for the single frame a screenshot is pending. Re-adding an unconditional per-frame clone for a view that is off by default would have undone that ticket immediately. The screenshot is deferred to the next frame for exactly that reason -- with compare off no buffers are being kept, so the first frame that has them is the next one.

SCREENSHOT WRITES TWO FILES, not one composed image, because FR-FE-005 says 'original and enhanced buffers SEPARATELY' and because it is the more useful artefact: a composed split is reproducible from the two halves, but neither half is recoverable from a composed split. The test asserts the two PNGs DIFFER -- identical bytes would mean one buffer was written twice, which is the failure that requirement exists to prevent, and a fixture using one buffer for both would have passed it.

tickets.title: Sprite-limit bypass + temporal de-flicker prototype
acceptance: SpriteHistorian ring + temporal reconstruction of software-culled sprite rotation, behind a toggle that is OFF by default (FR-ENH-002, ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME section 2)

the INTENTIONAL-BLINK enemy in RF-Scroller is PRESERVED, not erased -- de-flicker must distinguish deliberate game-driven blinking from hardware flicker (FR-ENH-013, D-004's red-fixture rule). W2-10a proved that enemy blinks on the exact formula blink_visible == (frame_counter & 0x08) != 0, so assert against that rather than eyeballing it

the >8-sprites-per-scanline RF-Scroller scene reconstructs cleanly under temporal mode (TESTING section 7 case b), verified via Ppu::oam() in-range counting the way W2-10a's own acceptance test does -- NOT via $2002 bit 5, which cannot witness this (see W2-10a's notes)
MODE INVARIANT holds mechanically: core state hashes identical with the feature on and off over the same input log, and rf-nes's own tests stay green (CLAUDE.md law 6)
criterion 1 of the ORIGINAL acceptance (sprite-limit bypass) is ALREADY DELIVERED by W3-05a and is explicitly NOT re-implemented here -- see notes
the OAM diff debug panel (FR-DBG-006) is SPLIT OUT to W4-06c and the trust ladder + per-game persistence (FR-ENH-011) to W3-05c -- both are outside this ticket's write_scope
notes: PRE-FLIGHT + CLAIM 2026-08-08 (conductor, HEAD 5157e06, baseline 659 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored). SPLIT 8 -> 5 PTS ALONG CRATE BOUNDARIES before claiming. Two of the five original criteria were unreachable from write_scope [crates/rf-enhance/**, crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/**]: the OAM diff debug panel (FR-DBG-006, which docs/SRS.md assigns to crate rf-debugger) and the trust ladder with per-game persistence (FR-ENH-011, which needs the per-game settings store W2-07 still owes). Filed as W4-06c and W3-05c respectively. 20th self-blocking-scope catch on this board.

CRITERION 1 IS ALREADY DELIVERED -- DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT IT. W3-05a (done) shipped the opt-in sprite-limit-bypass overlay: crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/mod.rs carries `sprite_overlay_enabled`, an `overlay: [OverlayPixel; 256]` scanline buffer, and sprites.rs's 'Sprite-limit-bypass overlay' section. Its own acceptance already required the overlay to contain the 9th+ sprites, the accuracy path to still drop them, the flags to be unchanged, and core state hashes to be IDENTICAL with the overlay on and off. Verify that surface and build the temporal reconstruction ON TOP of it rather than beside it.

NOTE ON dropped_by_limit, because the original criterion 1 named it: rf_core_api::PpuPixel::dropped_by_limit is still set unconditionally FALSE by sprites.rs (its own module doc says so), because W3-05a routed the bypass through the separate OverlayPixel channel instead. Populating that field is therefore OPTIONAL here, not required -- but if you do populate it, W2-10a's notes record that it would be the natural witness for '>8 sprites on a scanline', which currently has to be counted out of Ppu::oam() instead. Either way, do not break the accuracy path: the flag must never change which pixels the unmodified simulation emits.

THE RED FIXTURE NOW EXISTS AND IS THE POINT OF THIS TICKET. W2-10a shipped RF-Scroller's intentional-blink enemy and proved it blinks on the EXACT formula blink_visible == (frame_counter & 0x08) != 0 across 120 samples with both phases observed, plus a 12-sprite shared-scanline scene proven via Ppu::oam() in-range counting. D-004's red-fixture rule says every shipped heuristic must have a fixture that MUST fire and CI must fail when it stops firing. So: assert the blink SURVIVES de-flicker against that formula, and assert the overflow scene reconstructs -- do not eyeball either.

DO NOT USE $2002 BIT 5 AS EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING HERE. crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/sprites.rs implements the AUTHENTIC BUGGY hardware overflow scan (`m = (m + 1) & 3`, deliberately misreading tile/attribute/X bytes as Y once eight sprites are in range), so the flag fires on garbage -- W2-10a measured 156 positives in a window where the sprites provably did not exist. Count in-range sprites out of Ppu::oam() during VBLANK instead, across a full rotation period, exactly as W2-10a's `more_than_eight_sprites_share_the_gem_scanline_counted_from_ppu_oam` does. Reuse that test's shape.

DETERMINISM: crates/rf-nes/** IS under scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 4's wall-clock/RNG ban (std::time, SystemTime, Instant::now, rand::, fastrand, getrandom), unlike rf-enhance which is exempt. A SpriteHistorian ring living in rf-enhance is exempt but must still be deterministic by construction -- same reasoning as stitcher::Canvas being a flat buffer rather than a HashMap, since unstable iteration order would poison byte-identical replay.

MODE INVARIANT IS THE HAZARD CLASS THIS TICKET IS MOST EXPOSED TO. W3-05a's own notes record it: an enhancement that silently clocks MMC3's A12 counter is invisible to pixel comparison but corrupts IRQ timing. crates/retroforge/tests/{mode_invariant_corpus.rs, sprite_overlay_mode_invariant.rs} and a dedicated CI step already guard this -- they are OUTSIDE write_scope, so do not edit them; they must simply stay green. Enforce the invariant MECHANICALLY (identical state hashes on/off over one input log), not by assertion in prose.

VACUITY TRAPS. (a) A reconstruction test on a scene whose sprites never actually flicker proves nothing -- confirm the accuracy path genuinely drops sprites on that scanline first, then that temporal mode recovers them. (b) A blink-preservation test that samples only one phase passes trivially; sample across the full 8-frame period, both phases, as W2-10a did. (c) A toggle test that checks a bool rather than OUTPUT is worthless -- assert the emitted pixels differ between modes. This board has caught four tests that exercised a path without discriminating it; do not add a fifth.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 at 5c143f9. Gate verified INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok; workspace 675 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored (baseline 659, +16); `git status --porcelain crates/rf-nes/` empty, confirming zero core changes.

ARCH CONSTRAINT DISCOVERED HERE, GENERALIZABLE TO THE WHOLE ENHANCEMENT SIDE -- record this before it costs another ticket. scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 3's grep is `^\s*(rf-nes|rf-snes)\s*=` against the WHOLE Cargo.toml, which matches a line under [dev-dependencies] exactly as readily as one under [dependencies]. So rf-enhance -- and equally rf-profiles, rf-debugger, rf-ai -- can NEVER drive a real console core, not even from a test. Only retroforge and rf-harness can. Two tickets have now hit this wall from different directions: W4-03d solved it by adding crates/rf-harness/** to write_scope (the conductor's 18th self-blocking-scope catch), and W3-05 solved it by generating a CSV fixture from a throwaway driver inside crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/tests/ and deleting the driver. Either is legitimate; the point is that ANY future enhancement-side ticket whose acceptance mentions a real ROM must budget for one of them at pre-flight, not discover it mid-implementation.

DESIGN CALLS WORTH KEEPING, both measured rather than assumed. (a) Sprite identity is keyed on POSITION+PALETTE, deliberately NOT on sprite_id: RF-Scroller's own eviction-by-ascending-OAM-index rotates which id renders a given logical gem, so an id-keyed historian would be permanently blind to exactly the sprites it exists to track. (b) Ring length is 40, NOT ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME.md section 2's suggested default of 4 -- the fixture's engineered drop is 32 consecutive frames, which a 4-frame ring cannot bridge at all. That is a REAL SPEC/FIXTURE MISMATCH, documented in the module doc rather than silently absorbed; whoever revisits section 2 should decide whether the doc's default or the fixture's shape is wrong. (c) 'Protected' classification requires one completed presence streak AND one completed absence streak, both within the ring -- scaled against the ring itself rather than an arbitrary cycle count, which structurally prevents misclassifying the gems, whose 64-frame presence phase exceeds the ring by construction at any session length.

CRITERION 4 IS MET STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY THE HASH COMPARISON IT NAMES -- stated precisely rather than rounded up. Zero lines changed under crates/rf-nes/**, and SpriteHistorian::observe takes `video: &[PpuPixel]` rather than `&mut`, so the compiler AND scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 3 together make core perturbation impossible for this module. That is arguably a stronger guarantee than an on/off state-hash comparison. BUT it is only trivially true while nothing wires the toggle into the running app: there is currently no end-to-end path on which the feature could perturb anything. When W3-05c (trust ladder) or a shell-wiring ticket connects it, the on/off state-hash test the criterion literally describes becomes meaningful and should be written then.

HONEST GAP, REPORTED NOT HIDDEN: an identity's very FIRST off-phase cannot be protected, because no periodicity-based heuristic can classify a pattern before observing one full cycle. Measured on the real-ROM-derived data, that is frames 16-23 (derived from the data itself, not hardcoded); every off-phase from 32-39 through 96-103 matches ground truth exactly. In practice this means the intentional-blink enemy blinks once through de-flicker on first sight and is respected thereafter -- worth surfacing in the trust-ladder UI (W3-05c) rather than treating as invisible.

PROOF ORDER WAS RIGHT, which is what makes criterion 3 non-vacuous: the genuine drop was confirmed FIRST (Ppu::oam() ground truth = 12 sprites every frame, accuracy path <= 8 every frame, BOTH re-derived from the parsed fixture rather than trusted from the generator that produced it), and only then that temporal mode recovers them -- 103 of 110 frames exceed the 8-sprite cap under reconstruction. A recovery test on a scene whose sprites never actually dropped would have proven nothing.

MUTATIONS: disabling reconstruction killed 8 tests (5 unit + 3 real-fixture); dropping the `!id.is_protected()` gate killed the blink-preservation test with 40 off-phase leaks and its unit sibling; forcing `enabled: true` killed disabled_by_default, the passthrough test, and the emitted-pixels toggle test. Each applied and reverted with the file verified byte-identical afterwards.

STILL OUTSTANDING FROM THE ORIGINAL 8-PT TICKET, both filed and claimable-when-ready: W4-06c (OAM diff debug panel, FR-DBG-006, crate rf-debugger) and W3-05c (trust ladder shadow/advisory/active + per-game persistence, FR-ENH-011, blocked on W2-07's settings store). Neither was reachable from this ticket's write_scope.

tickets.title: OAM diff debug panel
acceptance: OAM diff view showing which sprites changed between frames and which the 8-per-scanline limit dropped (FR-DBG-006)

the panel is a READ-ONLY data consumer -- it must not perturb core state, and the mode-invariant tests must stay green (W3-05a's hazard class: an enhancement silently clocking MMC3's A12 counter, invisible to pixel comparison)
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W3-05 2026-08-08 in pre-flight (20th self-blocking-scope catch on this board). W3-05's write_scope is [crates/rf-enhance/**, crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/**] and could not reach a debugger panel at all; docs/SRS.md assigns FR-DBG-006 to crate rf-debugger. Splitting rather than widening keeps each half testable in the crate that owns it.

READ Ppu::oam() (public accessor) rather than the CPU-side OAM shadow at $0200 -- W2-10a's whole gem defect was the two disagreeing, because OAM DMA straddling the dots-257-320 OAMADDR reset window scrambled the copy. A debug panel that reads the shadow would have shown a picture the PPU never had.
DONE 2026-08-18. rf_debugger::oam gains diff_oam + dropped_by_limit (+ ChangedFields/SpriteDelta); retroforge gains an 'OAM diff' dock tab. 1025 workspace tests.

THE DROPPED SET IS DERIVED FROM scanline_occupancy, NOT RE-SCANNED, so the diff panel and W4-06a's occupancy bar can never disagree about which sprites were on a line: the dropped set is by construction the TAIL of the same list, in the same ascending-slot evaluation order hardware uses. Re-implementing the scan would have been the obvious way to introduce a second, subtly different answer.

EACH FIELD IS DETECTED SEPARATELY (y/x/tile/attrs) rather than a single 'something changed' bool -- and the attribute byte routes palette, priority AND both flips into one `attrs` flag, tested across all four bits, because a diff that missed the attribute byte would hide flip and palette changes entirely while looking like it worked.

THE 8-LIMIT BOUNDARY IS ASSERTED FROM BOTH SIDES: nine sprites on a line reports exactly slot 8 as dropped (the NINTH in evaluation order, not an arbitrary one), and eight sprites reports none -- so an off-by-one cannot pass. An empty scanline drops nothing, which is the common case and the one a buggy implementation would still look fine on during a busy frame.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION (criterion 2), not by discipline: both OAM snapshots arrive as copies the frame ALREADY carried (core_thread::FrameMsg::oam), so the panel has no path to the core at all and cannot perturb state even by accident. That is W3-05a's named hazard class -- an enhancement silently clocking MMC3's A12 counter, invisible to pixel comparison. Verified rather than asserted: mode_invariant_corpus 6/6 and sprite_overlay_mode_invariant 3/3 run explicitly and stay green.

BOTH SNAPSHOTS ARE THE PPU'S OWN OAM, never the CPU-side shadow at $0200 -- the ticket's own note, and W2-10a's gem defect was exactly those two disagreeing when an OAM DMA straddled the dots-257-320 OAMADDR reset window. A panel reading the shadow would have shown a picture the PPU never had, which is worse than no panel. Recorded in the function doc so a future edit cannot quietly switch sources.

THE PER-FRAME COST IS 256 BYTES and is deliberately NOT gated behind the panel being open, unlike W3-03a's layer buffers. The contrast is the point and is written down: 256 bytes is genuinely nothing next to the ~245 KB frame it arrives with, whereas two 240 KB clones were worth a CoreCommand round-trip. Gating everything on principle would have added a command path for a rounding error.

HONEST LIMITATION, stated in the panel text itself rather than only here: the drop analysis assumes 8x8 sprites. This panel has no PPUCTRL access of its own (it is a read-only consumer, which is the whole point), and rf_debugger::oam takes sprite height from its caller for exactly that reason -- so an 8x16 game's drop list would be wrong, and the UI says '(assumes 8x8)' rather than letting a reader assume otherwise.
SCOPE NOTE: DebugTab::OamDiff is an additive variant alongside W4-04's LuaConsole; LAYOUT_FORMAT_VERSION still does not move, per that enum's own additive-variant clause.

tickets.title: Anti-flicker trust ladder: shadow/advisory/active + per-game persistence
acceptance: every anti-flicker heuristic ships shadow-first with states shadow -> advisory -> active, a fresh install all-shadow, and per-game state PERSISTED (FR-ENH-011, D-004)

contradiction events land in a local per-game report card with NO telemetry (NFR-005), and safety-heuristic suppression requires a stored justification that auto-reopens on new-context triggers (FR-ENH-012)
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W3-05 2026-08-08 in pre-flight. Per-game PERSISTENCE is the reason this cannot live in W3-05's scope: the per-game settings store is W2-07 (ROM library + per-game settings store, still todo), hence the depends_on. Building a second, parallel persistence path inside rf-enhance would be exactly the kind of duplicate abstraction this board keeps deferring until a second consumer genuinely exists.

D-004's trust ladder is a PROJECT-WIDE law, not an anti-flicker detail -- every enhancement heuristic ships shadow-first with a red fixture that must fire in CI. Whatever shape this ticket gives the ladder becomes the pattern for the stitcher and decoder heuristics too, so design it as a general mechanism rather than an anti-flicker special case.

DONE 2026-08-18. `rf_enhance::trust` is the general mechanism the brief asked for: it knows NOTHING about anti-flicker. A heuristic is a string id, so the stitcher's scene-cut detection and the profile decoders inherit the ladder for free when they arrive -- D-004 is a project-wide law and this is now shaped like one.

THE ONE RULE THAT CARRIES THE WEIGHT, and the reason `should_act` is a single function every call site must go through rather than a match each writes for itself: ADVISORY DOES NOT ACT. FR-ENH-011 defines shadow as 'detect + record, never act' and advisory as 'badge suggests' -- a suggestion is a UI event, not a change to the emulation. That is the distinction most likely to be quietly got wrong later, so `only_active_may_act_advisory_is_still_a_suggestion` asserts all three rungs rather than just the two obvious ones.

AUTO-REOPEN IS A QUERY, NOT A BACKGROUND JOB (FR-ENH-012). A suppression records the scene context it was granted in, and `is_suppressed` compares against the scene being asked about -- so it stops applying the moment the trigger fires elsewhere, with nothing to remember to run. The reasoning is in the module doc: a user silencing a warning on one screen has said something about THAT screen, and treating it as a statement about the whole game is how a safety heuristic becomes decorative.

FAILING TOWARD LESS TRUST, everywhere it could go either way. An unknown trust level in a settings file reads as Shadow rather than erroring (a file from a newer build must not stop a game loading, and the safe direction is unambiguous). A stored suppression with no justification is DROPPED, which reopens the heuristic -- honouring a malformed file would be the unsafe direction. Both are tested in `unparseable_records_degrade_toward_shadow_rather_than_failing`.

PERSISTED THROUGH THE EXISTING PER-GAME STORE, which is exactly why this ticket depended on W2-07: crates/retroforge/src/game_settings.rs is already keyed by normalized ROM hash and already preserves keys it does not understand. A second persistence path inside rf-enhance would have been the duplicate abstraction the ticket's own note warns against. An untouched game writes NO trust key at all -- 'fresh install all-shadow' stays a guarantee of the code (TrustState's Default) rather than something the file asserts, so it cannot rot as heuristics are added.

NO TELEMETRY, STRUCTURALLY (NFR-005): `rf_enhance::trust` has no I/O, no clock and no network dependency of any kind -- the report card is an in-memory Vec it never flushes anywhere, and persistence is the caller's job through a store it already owns. There is nowhere for this to leak to even by accident, which is a stronger statement than 'we do not send it'.

SURFACED in a Heuristics menu: per-heuristic ladder radios (persisted immediately, same stance as every other per-game setting), any active suppression with its justification and scene, and the report card. The heuristic NAME LIST lives in the shell (`app::HEURISTICS`), not in the mechanism -- which names exist is the shell's knowledge, and keeping it out of rf-enhance is what makes the mechanism general.
OUT OF SCOPE, correctly: FR-ENH-013's red-fixture-must-fire-in-CI is a separate FR verified by rf-harness and is not in this ticket's acceptance. Flagged rather than silently absorbed.

tickets.title: 3-OS CI builds (macOS/Windows/Linux)
acceptance: macOS + Windows + Linux build jobs green on every PR (NFR-009)
build artifacts uploaded per-OS
golden-frame suite runs headless on the Linux software rasterizer
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. A `build` matrix job over ubuntu-latest / macos-latest / windows-latest uploading a per-OS artifact, plus an explicit named step for the golden-frame GPU suite on Linux's software rasterizer.

WHAT IS VERIFIED LOCALLY AND WHAT IS NOT, stated plainly because this is a CI ticket and I cannot make GitHub run. VERIFIED: `actionlint` passes on both workflow files -- a real validator (action versions, expression syntax, matrix references, runner labels), not just a YAML parse; and `cargo build --release -p retroforge --features audio,gamepad` compiles and links on macOS, landing at exactly the artifact path the job uploads (13.8 MB, target/release/retroforge). NOT VERIFIED: that the jobs are green. The first CI run is what proves that -- the same class of claim RENDERER section 7 already records about llvmpipe ("CI's first green run is what turns 'should be identical' into 'is identical'").

SEPARATE JOB, NOT A MATRIX OVER `gate`, and the cost reasoning matters: fmt/clippy/arch/validators/licence/determinism are OS-INDEPENDENT -- their answers cannot differ by platform -- so matrixing them would triple CI time to re-derive the same result twice. What genuinely varies per OS is whether the thing COMPILES AND LINKS, which is what this job proves. fail-fast is off: 'Windows is broken' and 'Windows and macOS are broken' are different findings, and fail-fast reports them identically.

BUILDS WITH --features audio,gamepad, not the CI-default set, and that IS the point of the job. Those features are off by default so `cargo test --workspace` needs no ALSA headers -- which also means cpal and gilrs, the two most platform-specific dependency trees in the workspace, are otherwise compiled on NO platform in CI. A build artifact a human is meant to run had better have sound and controllers. Linux installs libasound2-dev/libudev-dev for exactly this.

CRITERION 3 IS ITS OWN NAMED STEP rather than buried inside `cargo test --workspace`. Costs almost nothing (already compiled, cached) and buys a green/red check a human can point at, plus --nocapture so the log records WHICH adapter answered. It cannot silently degrade to a skip: `gpu_or_skip` panics rather than skipping when CI is set, so 'no adapter' fails loudly instead of passing as zero tests run -- the failure mode that would have made the step decorative.

DELIBERATE SCOPE LIMIT, FLAGGED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the build matrix does NOT run the workspace suite on macOS/Windows. `gpu_or_skip` panics whenever CI is set -- a guarantee that exists so a Linux run cannot silently lose GPU coverage -- so running those tests there would gate this job on the mac/win runners exposing a usable adapter, which this ticket did not verify and a BUILD job should not depend on. Letting them skip cleanly per-job needs a crate-side CI-strictness signal narrower than 'is CI', outside this ticket's .github/** write scope. RESIDUAL GAP, real and worth a follow-up: runtime behaviour on macOS/Windows (path handling, line endings) is still untested by CI. Criterion 1 says 'build jobs green', and build is what this delivers.

tickets.title: rf-nes emits CoreEvents, EventMask-gated and zero-cost when unsubscribed
acceptance: rf-nes actually EMITS the CoreEvents its hardware produces, through CoreSink::event: FrameStart, FrameEnd, VblankStart, Scanline, ScrollWrite (x/y/layer), OamRewrite, MapperIrq and DmaStart -- today it emits NONE of them (FR-CORE-006)

every emission is gated by CoreConfig::event_mask, and EventMask::NONE -- the Accuracy-mode default -- is measurably ~zero-cost, proven by a criterion bench comparing masked-off against a no-event baseline rather than asserted

So the contract (W0-04's CoreEvent + EventMask, complete and unused) has consumers planned in three tickets -- W4-01's bus, W4-03a's stitcher, W4-06a's event viewer -- and NO producer owned by anything. Building the bus first would be an event bus with neither producer nor consumer: exactly the unvalidated scaffolding W1-02 declined for the Mapper trait and W3-03 was fenced against for the SceneGraph.
