tickets.title: TripleBuffer monotonicity: readers can observe an older frame after a newer one
acceptance: TripleBufferReader::latest() never returns a frame older than one the SAME reader already observed -- the render thread must not roll backwards
the existing one_writer_and_two_reader_threads test passes deterministically under --test-threads=16, verified over at least 60 consecutive runs (it fails ~3/60 today)
a mutation reverting the fix must reproduce the failure, proving the test discriminates the race rather than merely exercising it
notes: FILED + CLAIMED 2026-08-07 by the conductor while verifying W2-11. This is a DEFECT IN ALREADY-CLOSED WORK (W4-01, commit ace856f), not a W2-11 regression. The W2-11 agent saw one failure, re-ran clean, and reported it as 'confirmed flaky' -- correct to leave it alone (outside its write_scope), but 'flaky' understated it. Conductor reproduced it at 3 failures in 60 runs (5%) with `cargo test -p rf-core-api -- --test-threads=16`; a 40-run pass at default parallelism showed nothing, which is why it reads as flakiness.

ROOT CAUSE, established by construction rather than by trying fixes (CLAUDE.md bug-fix discipline). TripleBufferWriter::publish does: lock slots[k] -> write Arc -> UNLOCK -> latest.store(k, Release). TripleBufferReader::latest does: latest.load(Acquire) -> lock slots[idx] -> clone. The two steps of publish are not atomic together, so a reader BLOCKED ON slots[k]'s mutex can acquire it the instant the writer unlocks and observe the new frame BEFORE latest has been advanced to k. Its next call then loads the still-stale latest, which points at the previous slot holding an OLDER frame. Concretely: latest=0 (slot0=99, slot1=97, slot2=98); reader loads latest->0 and is preempted; writer publishes 100->slot1 (latest=1), 101->slot2 (latest=2), then 102->slot0 -- the reader is waiting on slot0's lock, takes it on release and reads 102, while latest is still 2; reader returns 102; next call loads latest=2 and reads slot2 = 101. 101 < 102, backwards.

TWO ALTERNATIVE CAUSES CONSIDERED AND REFUTED. (a) Test bug via shared state: refuted -- `last_seen` is a plain `let mut` local inside each spawned closure, so each reader thread has its own; the two threads never share it. (b) Weak memory ordering on `latest`: refuted -- Release/Acquire is the correct pairing and is already used; the defect is not the ordering of the atomic but that the slot write and the index store are not atomic AS A PAIR.

THE INVARIANT IS CORRECT AND THE IMPLEMENTATION IS WRONG -- do not 'fix' this by weakening the test. ARCHITECTURE Sec6 says workers may LAG and never block the writer; lagging means missing intermediate frames, which this buffer is supposed to do. Handing a render thread frame 102 and then frame 101 is not lag, it is rollback, and it would surface as visible stutter in the enhanced pipeline. The test's assertion is the property the design promises.

PROPOSED FIX (minimal): move `latest.store(k, Release)` INSIDE the slot lock's critical section. Then the only way any reader can observe slot k's new value is after the writer released that lock, by which point latest already points at k or newer -- so a subsequent load can never resolve to an older frame. Cost is one atomic store inside an O(1) critical section, which does not change the 'writer is never meaningfully delayed by a slow reader' property the module doc argues for. Verify by mutation: revert the store back outside the lock and confirm the 60-run stress fails again.

STRESS COMMAND FOR THE ACCEPTANCE: `for i in $(seq 1 60); do cargo test -p rf-core-api --quiet -- --test-threads=16 || echo FAIL; done`. A single green run proves nothing here -- that is exactly how this shipped.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 at 9c8bc9d. Gate: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok. workspace 621 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored (unchanged -- this ticket fixed and strengthened existing tests rather than adding any).

FIX AS PROPOSED: latest.store moved INSIDE the slot's critical section. Verified 0 failures in 60 runs of `cargo test -p rf-core-api -- --test-threads=16`; mutation (store moved back outside the lock) reproduces the failure. The diagnosis in the notes above was confirmed by construction BEFORE the fix was written, not discovered by trying fixes -- and the two alternative causes (shared test state, weak memory ordering) were refuted, not assumed away.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS TICKET WAS THE REAL LESSON: the pre-existing test was a WEAK GUARD, and that is how the defect shipped past W4-01's own gate. 2 readers x 500 publishes caught the bug only ~1-5 runs in 60. A guard that misses its own bug 95% of the time is indistinguishable from no guard on a single CI run. Resized to 6 readers x 4000 publishes -- more readers than the writer has slots, each polling well past the publish rate, so at least one is reliably parked on the mutex the writer is about to release, which is precisely the interleaving the race needs. MEASURED, not assumed: 30/30 detection against the reverted fix, up from ~1/60; 0/60 failures with the fix. GENERALIZABLE: for a concurrency test, 'it passed' and 'it would have caught the bug' are different claims, and only the second one is worth anything. Size the test until it fails against the known defect EVERY time, then fix.

PATTERN THIS BOARD KEEPS HITTING, third instance in three tickets: rf_cache::fsutil's leaf-symlink branch was exercised but not discriminated; rf-enhance's FM-11 watermark test was named for coverage it did not have; and here a concurrency test exercised the race but detected it 5% of the time. All three passed their original gate. The common fix is the same -- mutate the implementation and require the specific test to fail.

NOT A W2-11 REGRESSION. Found while conductor-verifying W2-11, whose agent saw one failure, re-ran clean, and reported 'confirmed flaky by a clean re-run'. Leaving it alone was correct (crates/rf-core-api/** was outside its write_scope) but the word 'flaky' understated a real correctness defect in the enhancement spine. Worth noting as an agent-reporting pattern: a transient failure in code you cannot touch still deserves 'I could not investigate this' rather than a diagnosis.

tickets.title: Profile loader + schema v0 + validator tool
acceptance: TOML schema per docs/design/GAME_PROFILES.md parses into versioned structs (FR-PROF-001)
hash match incl. md5/crc32 aliases (FR-PROF-002, FR-MODE-005)
retroforge-tool profile validate + hash subcommands
unknown-key warnings, newer-major rejection (FR-PROF-004, NFR-008)
notes: PRE-FLIGHT + CLAIM 2026-08-08 (conductor, HEAD ce38a0a, baseline 712 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored). Scope [crates/rf-profiles/**, tools/**, profiles/**] is NOT self-blocking -- tests live under the crate, the CLI under tools/, example profiles under profiles/. No amendment needed to this ticket's own scope.

COLLISION FOUND AND RESOLVED IN THE BOARD, not left to be discovered mid-implementation: W4-02 and W4-07 BOTH write to tools/**, BOTH create the `retroforge-tool` binary (which does not exist -- there is no tools/ directory and no such bin anywhere), and BOTH define a subcommand called `hash` -- W4-02's matches a PROFILE against a ROM, W4-07's emits RA-compatible ROM hashes. Neither depended on the other, so whichever ran second would have collided with a binary and a subcommand namespace it did not expect. RESOLUTION: W4-02 (this ticket) OWNS the retroforge-tool skeleton and the `profile` subcommand group; W4-07 now depends_on W4-02 and owns the `rom` group. DESIGN THE SUBCOMMAND NAMESPACE ONCE, HERE -- prefer `retroforge-tool profile validate` / `profile hash` and leave `rom ...` free -- so W4-07 slots in without renaming anything.

rf-profiles IS A STUB (src/lib.rs only) and `profiles/` already has nes/ and snes/ directories plus a README -- check what example profiles exist there before authoring new ones, and make the schema parse them rather than inventing fixtures that only the tests use.

SCHEMA SOURCE OF TRUTH IS docs/design/GAME_PROFILES.md section 2 (Schema v0), with section 1 for identity and section 4 for loading/precedence. Section 1 line 15 states the two rules criterion 4 names: 'loader rejects newer majors, warns on unknown keys', and section 3's authoring pipeline carries the same `profile_version` major semantics for decoder versions. Implement from that doc, not from a plausible-looking TOML shape.

HASH-MATCH TRAP (criterion 2, FR-PROF-002 / FR-MODE-005): 'incl. md5/crc32 aliases' means a profile may identify its ROM by ANY of the hash families rf-cart computes -- SHA-256 primary, plus SHA-1, MD5 and CRC32 for RetroAchievements/No-Intro compatibility. rf-cart ALREADY computes all four with RA-convention normalization (ticket W0-02, docs/research/game-identity-and-re-data.md); do NOT reimplement hashing, and do not assume SHA-256-only. Note the RustCrypto 0.11 trap while you are there: finalize() returns Array<u8,N> with no LowerHex, so the 0.10 `format!("{:x}")` idiom does not compile -- rf-cart hex-encodes manually and is the pattern to copy.

VACUITY TRAPS. (a) A schema test that only parses a VALID profile cannot detect a loader that accepts anything -- assert that a newer-major profile is REJECTED and that an unknown key WARNS (and that the warning is actually surfaced, not swallowed). (b) A hash-match test using one hash family proves nothing about the aliases -- exercise each family the criterion names, and include a NEGATIVE case where the profile does not match the ROM. (c) A `profile validate` CLI test that only checks exit code 0 on a good file is worthless -- assert a bad file exits non-zero AND names the offending key. This board has caught SIX tests that exercised a path without discriminating it (see docs/work/HANDOFF.md's session-lessons section); do not add a seventh.

SCOPE FENCE: this ticket ships the LOADER, the SCHEMA and the VALIDATOR. It does NOT ship a decoder -- `metatile_screens` is W5-02a and depends on W5-01, which depends on this. RF-Scroller's FORMAT.md documents a column-RLE metatile level format built specifically to be that decoder's first target, so the schema must be able to EXPRESS it, but nothing here decodes anything. Resist the pull.

NO EXECUTABLE CODE IN PROFILES -- ARCHITECTURE section 7 is explicit that rf-profiles is 'data only; code = plugins', and D-005 makes community intake deny-by-default with SPDX licence + provenance required. Whatever the schema allows must stay declarative; a field that smuggles in behaviour would breach both.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 at 599ef5a. Gate verified INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok; workspace 745 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored (baseline 712, +33). No new EXTERNAL crate entered the tree -- Cargo.lock grew only by the local retroforge-tool package.

UNBLOCKED BY THIS: W4-05, W4-06b, W5-01, W5-06. The CLI namespace collision with W4-07 was resolved in the board at claim time, and this ticket honoured it -- `profile validate` / `profile hash` under a `profile` group, with `rom` reserved and refusing with a message that names W4-07 by ticket id.

TWO MECHANISMS, NOT ONE, and the distinction is load-bearing: unknown keys WARN, newer majors REJECT. serde's deny_unknown_fields ERRORS rather than warns, so shape-checking hand-walks the parsed toml::Value against a whitelist tree; and the major check runs BEFORE the typed deserialize, so a profile that is both newer-major and structurally broken fails with the NEWER-MAJOR error rather than a confusing parse error. LoadOutcome{profile, warnings} carries warnings out by value so they cannot be dropped between loader and CLI -- and the mutation suite proves the two swallow points are genuinely distinct, since killing the library's collection and killing the CLI's printing fail DIFFERENT tests.

HASHING CONSUMED, NOT REBUILT, as the pre-flight required: matches_rom takes rf_cart::RomIdentity/RomHashes directly, compares against `.normalized` never `.raw`, case-insensitively; an [[identity]] entry must match on EVERY family it specifies while the profile matches if ANY entry does. matching_revision returns the matched entry rather than a bool, added mid-task because FR-PROF-002 names per-revision overrides and a bool would force a future consumer to re-search. Mutation: matching on sha256 alone killed 6 tests.

MY PRE-FLIGHT NOTE WAS WRONG AND THE EXECUTOR SAID SO: I wrote that `profiles/` already had example profiles to parse, having listed the nes/ and snes/ directories WITHOUT checking their contents -- both were empty. Two synthetic examples were authored instead, with tests/example_profiles.rs walking /profiles and failing if any profile there does not load, which makes them load-bearing rather than decorative. The NES example mirrors RF-Scroller's real FORMAT.md constants (SCREEN_COLS=48, SCREEN_ROWS=14, column_rle) to prove the schema can EXPRESS that fixture's format -- nothing decodes it, per the scope fence.

OUT-OF-SCOPE EDIT, DECLARED AND JUSTIFIED AT THE EDIT SITE: root Cargo.toml gains `tools/*` in members. Structurally required -- a tools/ crate with neither a members entry nor its own [workspace] table is a hard cargo error, and a standalone [workspace] would drop retroforge-tool out of `cargo test --workspace`, `clippy --workspace`, `fmt --all` and `cargo deny`, all of which this ticket's own gate runs.

AN ARCH BLIND SPOT WORTH KNOWING ABOUT, created deliberately and recorded here rather than left implicit: the crate lives under tools/ rather than crates/ BECAUSE scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 3 iterates `for c in crates/*/` and therefore never walks tools/. ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME Sec3 specifies 'perceptual hash of framebuffer edges + mapper bank state', and the reason it is EDGES and not the whole framebuffer is FM-11 (stitcher canvas explosion): a hash over full frame content changes every time a sprite moves, so every frame becomes a new scene and the canvas never accumulates. A test asserting only 'same frame -> same id' is VACUOUS -- it passes against a plain framebuffer hash, which is the wrong implementation. The test must prove all three: (a) identical frame -> same id, (b) same scene with sprites MOVED / HUD counters changed -> STILL the same id, (c) genuinely different scene (different level or mapper bank state) -> different id. notes: FILED 2026-08-07 at W4-03b close. W4-03b delivered scene identity as ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME Sec3 literally specifies it -- a perceptual hash of framebuffer edges plus mapper bank state -- and that formulation is stable for room/static scenes and under sprite+HUD noise but FRAGMENTS under sustained scroll. Measured on rf-enhance's own fixture: 50 frames at 3px/frame (150px travel) produced 36 distinct scene ids. W4-03b recorded this as a printed measurement rather than a passing assertion, deliberately, because it is a known gap and not a contract.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS ALREADY REFUTED -- do not spend the ticket on it. A perceptual hash is normally compared by Hamming DISTANCE, not equality, so the natural first theory is that W4-03b simply used it as an exact key and a distance threshold would repair it. A conductor probe measured the distance between consecutive frames' edge signatures during the same scrolling scenario: 34-44 differing buckets out of 112 (~30-40%), climbing to 106/112 against the first frame. A threshold loose enough to survive consecutive frames would merge genuinely different scenes. The signature DECORRELATES under scroll; it does not merely drift.

ROOT CAUSE: the block grid is anchored to SCREEN space and recomputed from each frame's visible pixels, so scrolling content translates through fixed block boundaries. Note also that world-anchoring the grid is NOT by itself a fix -- as you scroll you are genuinely looking at different world content, so any pure function of the visible framebuffer must change. That is why Sec3's formulation works for room-based games (Zelda screens, Metroid rooms) and cannot work for scrollers by construction.

PROPOSED DESIGN, captured while fresh (validate it, do not assume it): make scene identity STATEFUL -- a SceneTracker rather than a pure hash. Scene CONTINUITY is a function of (a) ScrollTracker continuity, which W4-03a already computes and which already distinguishes smooth wraparound from a jump, and (b) mapper bank state, which for most games identifies the level and does not change while scrolling within it. The perceptual hash from W4-03b is then used only to DISAMBIGUATE after a discontinuity, which is exactly the job it is good at. Under this design 150px of continuous 3px/frame scrolling is one scene by construction, and a level load shows up as discontinuity + large perceptual distance + usually a bank change.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE INSIDE W4-03b: validating a continuity-based tracker needs a real scrolling fixture, and none existed -- W4-03a's honest gap (neither fixture ROM ever reached scrolling gameplay) was still open at W4-03b close, so both tickets exercised the camera only over synthesised canvases. W2-10 (RF-Scroller: in-repo NES fixture platformer, cc65/neslib) is the ticket that builds one, hence the depends_on. Designing this against synthetic canvases is how the wrong answer gets baked in.

MAGNITUDES ARE FIXTURE-MEASURED, NOT A PROPERTY OF REAL GAMES. rf-enhance's scene_identity fixture has structure at exactly the 32px block period, which is why the measured distance oscillates (0, 34, 6, 34, 4, 44) instead of climbing smoothly. Driving ScrollTracker::observe_frame from an ACTUAL RUNNING CORE panicked at frame 711 of a 900-frame RF-Scroller session: 'attempt to subtract with overflow' in compute_bands. CONDUCTOR VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY -- reverting the fix reproduces the panic at scroll_tracker.rs:312 against the real fixture. Mechanism is named in crates/retroforge/src/stepper.rs::run_until_next_frame's own doc: a single Cpu::step can legitimately drain up to ~4.5 scanlines belonging to the NEXT frame when an OAM-DMA-triggering instruction straddles a frame boundary. compute_bands has no cross-call memory to notice a Scanline value regressed, so it closed the in-progress band with end < start. EVERY PRIOR TEST FED IT A HAND-AUTHORED, ALWAYS-MONOTONIC EVENT LOG, so nothing could ever have caught it. Reachable by any real deployment; invisible to synthetic testing by construction.

THE FIX IS CORRECT, NOT A BAND-AID -- checked rather than accepted. saturating_sub makes the malformed band 0-width, which can never win the max_by_key 'largest band' selection; that is right because the band is leaked next-frame data, not content. And Rust's own Range semantics already make start..end empty when start >= end, so ScanlineBand::y_at and the stitcher never paint or position from it either way. Nothing downstream depends on the malformed value.

THE MEASURED BASELINE INVERTS W4-03b's NUMBER, and this is the ticket's real finding. Pre-ticket compute_scene_id over 900 REAL RF-Scroller frames (752px travel, full nametable wraparound) yields 1 DISTINCT ID -- not the 36-per-150px W4-03b recorded. BOTH FIGURES WERE MEASURING THE FIXTURE, NOT THE ALGORITHM: W4-03b's synthetic texture had artificially high contrast (values spread across 0/96/176 thirds) so the edge signature was hyperactive, while real NES content produces block-average deltas never exceeding roughly 10 -- far under EDGE_THRESHOLD's 48 -- so the signature is all-flat for an entire level. The pre-flight instruction to measure the real baseline BEFORE designing is what surfaced this; designing against the synthetic 36 would have solved a problem that does not exist.

SO '1 ID' IS VACUOUSLY GOOD, and the agent proved it rather than reporting a win. RF-Scroller and Alter Ego -- entirely unrelated games -- hash to the IDENTICAL SceneId(7309415231882407843). compute_scene_id is degenerate on real low-contrast NES content. No single EDGE_THRESHOLD has a working operating point: catching real ~10-unit content deltas would break the ~17-34-unit sprite/HUD-noise perturbation the existing watermark test depends on. That is a design gap in W4-03b's algorithm, not a tuning miss, and it was correctly NOT patched here.

ACCEPTANCE 2 IS BLOCKED AT THE FIXTURE LEVEL -- reported plainly, not force-fit. Both available real ROMs are NROM with no bank state and both produce the degenerate signature, so neither can discriminate the other. Its INTENT is proven at unit level with legitimately-varying synthetic content, mutation-verified. SEVERITY WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: crates/rf-enhance/src/persistence.rs's canvas_cache_key includes rom_sha256 alongside the scene id, so a cross-ROM scene-id collision CANNOT load one game's canvas into another. The collision is contained by the cache key.

WHAT IS PROVEN VS WHAT IS NOT, stated precisely: the CONTINUITY mechanism is proven on real hardware output (900 frames, 1 id, max per-frame world delta 8px matching RF-Scroller's real 8px/8-frame movement budget). The DISAMBIGUATION half is not merely unexercised -- it is known-degenerate on real low-contrast content. In practice a level transition would still yield a new scene via the scroll-discontinuity path, so the feature is not dead. And per the constraint recorded at W2-10's claim, RF-Scroller is NROM with CONSTANT bank state, so the bank-state half of the design stays unvalidated until a mapper-using fixture exists.

FOLLOW-UP THIS LEAVES OPEN (not filed as its own ticket yet -- W5-01/W5-02a will exercise the same surface and may subsume it): compute_scene_id needs a discrimination mechanism that works on real NES palette-index ranges. The edge-bucket approach with a fixed absolute threshold cannot do it. Candidates worth measuring against the now-available real fixtures: a RELATIVE threshold scaled to the frame's own observed dynamic range, or leaning on nametable/attribute content rather than rendered palette indices. W2-10a's added scenes will widen RF-Scroller's contrast range and change this measurement, so re-measure after it lands.

MUTATION RESULTS: forcing discontinuous=true unconditionally killed BOTH stability tests (1 -> 48 ids, and 1 -> 28 ids for the sprite-noise-over-scrolling variant); forcing ids equal after frame 1 killed the scroll-jump and bank-change difference tests; reverting saturating_sub reproduced the real frame-711 panic its regression test guards. Each applied by direct edit, confirmed failing, reverted, reconfirmed green via git diff.

tickets.title: Lua script host (mlua) + overlay API
acceptance: capability-gated rf.* API per docs/design/PLUGINS.md §3 (FR-PLUG-001, FR-PLUG-002)
error containment: script fault pauses script not emulator (FR-PLUG-004)
example overlay script shipped in /plugins/examples (FR-REND-006)
per-frame budget throttling (FR-PLUG-005)
Lua console REPL panel docked in the Debug workspace (DEBUGGER.md section 5)
cache_dir filesystem cap is realpath-contained; symlink-escape test refused with diagnostic (NFR-010)
PLUGIN_AUTHORING.md minimal page ships with the host (R-A4)
capability list shown at enable time; write ledger visible in UI (FR-PLUG-003)
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. rf-plugin-sdk gains manifest/sandbox/host; retroforge gains script_panel + a docked Lua tab; plugins/examples/player-overlay and docs/PLUGIN_AUTHORING.md ship with it. 1009 workspace tests, cargo deny licenses ok (mlua and vendored Lua 5.4 are both MIT).

THE SANDBOX WAS BUILT AND TESTED FIRST, because every other criterion is decorative if a script can reach io.open. PROBED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and the probe found two real holes: with a minimal StdLib (TABLE|STRING|MATH|UTF8), io/os/package/require/debug/loadstring/coroutine are correctly ABSENT -- but dofile, loadfile and load are STILL PRESENT, because Lua's base library is always loaded and has no StdLib bit of its own. dofile and loadfile read files. All three are now removed explicitly (sandbox::REMOVED_BASE_GLOBALS, public so an auditor can read the list rather than infer it).

THE TEST ASSERTS ABSENCE, NOT REFUSAL: a binding that does not exist cannot be reached by a cleverer call, so no_escape_hatch_survives_the_sandbox checks each dangerous name is nil rather than that some wrapper said no. Paired with a_script_can_still_do_useful_work so 'everything is absent' cannot pass trivially -- string/math/table/utf8/pcall/print remain and a real computation runs.

A DENIED CAPABILITY MEANS THE FUNCTION IS ABSENT, not present-and-refusing: rf.mem is simply nil, so a denied call is Lua's own nil-call error pointing at the author's line rather than a runtime refusal they could catch and ignore. Both directions asserted, so 'the gate works' and 'nothing is ever bound' cannot look the same.

ERROR CONTAINMENT IS IN THE SIGNATURE (FR-PLUG-004): ScriptHost::on_frame returns unit, never Result -- 'script fault pauses script not emulator' means a fault is a STATE CHANGE, not an error a caller might propagate into the frame loop. The test drives a faulting script and then keeps calling the host, asserting it survives and that the fault reached the log the REPL renders.

THROTTLING TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (FR-PLUG-005): engages over budget AND releases when the script comes back. Testing only the engage half would pass on a one-way punishment. Uses a zero budget so any callback is over-budget, keeping it a fast unit test rather than one that must burn real milliseconds. My first assertion was off by one and the CODE was right -- 'every 4th frame' is three skips then a call -- so I corrected the test, not the behaviour.

PATH CONTAINMENT (NFR-010/D-006) canonicalizes BOTH sides then compares, the same shape retroforge::library uses (rf-plugin-sdk cannot depend on that crate, so the shape is copied, not the code). A file that does not exist yet resolves via its PARENT, so a plugin can create files without the capability being useless, while every symlink and .. on the way there is still caught. Tested with a real symlink escaping to a real outside dir, plain .. traversal, the no-capability case, and a baseline in-dir path that MUST succeed -- without which the test would pass on an implementation that refused everything.

THE LEDGER IS THE GATE, NOT A LOG BESIDE ONE: WriteLedger::record returns whether the write may proceed, so a caller cannot perform one without it having been recorded -- check and record are the same call rather than two a caller could reorder or forget to pair.

WRITE_MEMORY IS DECLARABLE AND LEDGERED BUT THE WRITE ITSELF IS REFUSED, recorded as owed rather than half-wired: PLUGINS.md section 2 requires the ledger also be recorded in save states (PROF/ENHC chunks), and the ENHC chunk does not exist. Criterion 8 asks for the capability list and a visible ledger, which ship; the save-state half is owed.

THE SHIPPED EXAMPLE IS EXECUTED, not just written: tests/example_plugin.rs loads the real plugin.toml and main.lua, runs 601 frames, and asserts the script neither faults nor throttles AND that its own frame-modulo-600 print branch was reached -- otherwise the test would only prove the file parses. A second test greps the example for forbidden globals, since a doc demonstrating an unavailable API is worse than no doc.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (vetoable, recorded): crates/rf-debugger/** for one additive DebugTab::LuaConsole variant. Criterion 5 says 'docked in the Debug workspace' and the tab enum lives there. LAYOUT_FORMAT_VERSION deliberately does NOT move -- that enum's own doc already covers additive variants, and an old persisted layout that never mentions LuaConsole still deserializes and simply never lists the tab.

BUILD-TIME RISK WORTH NAMING: mlua's vendored feature compiles Lua 5.4 from bundled C, so a C toolchain is now a build-time dependency on every platform. GitHub runners all have one, but W3-06's 3-OS matrix (added yesterday, itself never yet run) is where that first gets exercised -- the most likely first-CI-run failure alongside the mac/Windows adapter question W3-06 already flagged.

HONEST GAPS, in PLUGIN_AUTHORING.md's own 'Known gaps' section rather than only here: rf.mem.read_u8 is capability-gated but returns 0 (wiring a live StateView needs the shell's core handle); rf.gui.* validates calls but does not yet reach the renderer's overlay path; replace_layers, input_bindings and the WASM tier are not implemented. The GATES are real and tested; the data behind two of them is not yet.

tickets.title: Mode toggles + per-game enhancement settings UI
acceptance: 5 modes per ARCHITECTURE §4 as presets (FR-MODE-001)
per-game overrides persisted (FR-ENH-010)
enhancement never on silently (fresh install defaults to Accuracy) (FR-MODE-003)
persistent ENHANCED status-bar badge with hover feature breakdown + hold-to-peek original (FRONTEND_UI.md section 1)
Enhance workspace shows per-heuristic ladder chips + report card panel (FR-ENH-012, FRONTEND_UI.md section 3.3)
profile inspector panel: identity match status, capability checklist, override precedence (GAME_PROFILES.md section 4, FR-PROF-005)
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. Mode extended from 2 to ARCHITECTURE section 4's FIVE presets; per-game enhancement toggles persisted; honesty badge with hover breakdown and hold-to-peek; Enhance workspace with feature rows, ladder chips, report card and profile inspector.

FR-MODE-003 IS A PROPERTY OF THE DEFAULT, NOT A CHECK: `Mode::enhancement_active()` is asked ONCE, in one place, rather than re-derived by every caller. The test that carries the requirement asserts that a settings file with EVERY feature flag set still runs nothing in Accuracy -- 'enhancement never on silently' has to survive a file that says otherwise, or it is a UI convention rather than a guarantee. An unrecognised mode name (older file, typo, newer build) resolves to Accuracy, so enhancement is never on because a name failed to parse.

RESEARCH/DEBUG DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENABLE ENHANCEMENT. Section 4 says 'enhancement optional', which means not on by itself -- a debugging mode that quietly changed the picture would defeat its own purpose. Asserted rather than left implicit, because 'everything exposed' reads like it should include enhancements.

THE BADGE COUNTS EFFECTIVE FEATURES, NOT ENABLED ONES. A badge reading 'Enhanced (4)' while two of those cannot run without a profile is exactly the dishonesty FRONTEND_UI.md section 1's badge exists to prevent. So FeatureRow::effective() = enabled AND available, asked once, and the badge counts that. Enhanced without a profile reads (2); Game-Aware with one reads (4); Game-Aware WITHOUT one falls back to (2).

THE TWO UNAVAILABLE REASONS ARE DISTINGUISHABLE, and that is the point of returning Availability rather than a bool: 'turn on Enhanced' and 'load a profile' are different user actions, and someone told only 'unavailable' cannot tell which they need. In Enhanced, a profile feature says NeedsMode(Game-Aware); in Game-Aware without a match it says NeedsProfile.

UNAVAILABLE ROWS ARE SHOWN DISABLED AND EXPLAINED, NEVER HIDDEN -- FRONTEND_UI.md section 3.3's honesty contract ('rows disabled+explained when no profile capability'). Hiding them would be the same lie by omission the badge prevents: a user who cannot see that full-level view NEEDS a profile concludes the emulator lacks the feature.

HOLD-TO-PEEK IS HELD, NOT TOGGLED, and is applied at the view-selection site rather than by mutating `self.camera` -- so releasing restores whatever the user had chosen without this having to remember it. A toggle would leave someone looking at the original wondering why their enhancements stopped.

THE LADDER CHIP SHOWS SUPPRESSION, NOT JUST THE RUNG. A heuristic that is nominally 'active' but suppressed in the current scene is NOT acting, so a chip reading only 'active' would be wrong. Reuses W3-05c's TrustLadder rather than a second model.

EMPTY STATES SAY SO EVERYWHERE: 'No enhancements active - this is the unmodified emulation', 'No contradictions recorded this session', 'no profile matched this ROM's normalized hash', '(none declared)'. An empty panel reads as a broken control, which is the specific doubt an honesty surface must not create.

PROFILE INSPECTOR: identity status, capability checklist with unmet caps shown UNCHECKED rather than omitted, and the precedence chain in GAME_PROFILES.md section 4's order (base -> user overrides -> per-session). The ORDER is asserted, because 'all layers visible' means precedence is the content. `profile_matched` is currently always false -- no profile loader is wired into the shell yet -- and the inspector SAYS no profile matched rather than implying one did. That gap is real and belongs to whichever ticket wires W4-02's loader into the shell.

UNVERIFIED, stated plainly: the visual layout is not checked by anything. Every string and every enable/disable decision is computed by crate::enhance_ui and tested headlessly (8 tests), and the egui layer only paints them -- so what is asserted is what the panel SAYS, not how it looks.

tickets.title: Debug viewers + event viewer + docking
acceptance: pattern/nametable/palette/OAM viewers live (FR-DBG-001)
event viewer: frame-timeline scatter of register writes/IRQ/DMA (DEBUGGER.md section 3)
egui_dock panel layout persisted (FR-FE-004)
notes: PRE-FLIGHT + CLAIM 2026-08-09 (conductor, HEAD d1a9de0, baseline 745 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored). Scope [crates/rf-debugger/**, crates/retroforge/**] is not self-blocking. THIS TICKET IS ON THE CRITICAL PATH TO THE PROJECT'S HEADLINE GOAL: W4-06a -> W4-06b (annotation store exports a profile skeleton, GAME_PROFILES section 3) -> W5-01 -> W5-02a/b -> W5-03, which is game-aware FULL-LEVEL reconstruction. The generic stitcher already shipped shows only VISITED area by design; this chain is what rebuilds geometry the player has never walked through.

SKELETON-OWNERSHIP COLLISION RESOLVED IN THE BOARD, the same pattern caught at W4-02/W4-07 one ticket ago. crates/rf-debugger is a 15-LINE STUB and is NOT a dependency of crates/retroforge. W4-06a and W4-06c were BOTH claimable, BOTH write to [rf-debugger, retroforge], and NEITHER depended on the other -- so whichever ran second would have collided with a crate skeleton, a shell dependency and an egui_dock layout it did not create. RESOLUTION: W4-06a owns the skeleton, the shell wiring and the docking layout (its own criterion 3); W4-06c now depends_on W4-06a and adds one panel to it. W4-06b already depended on W4-06a, so the whole debugger track is now serialized correctly.

ARCH WALL -- rf-debugger MAY NOT DEPEND ON rf-nes. scripts/validate-arch.sh rule 3 allows only retroforge and rf-harness to touch a console core directly, and its grep matches [dev-dependencies] too (the constraint W3-05 hit and recorded). So the viewers CANNOT read PPU state directly; they consume rf_core_api::StateView, which exposes cpu_regs, wram, vram, cgram, oam, ppu_regs and mapper_state as byte slices.

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT AFFECTS CRITERION 1: StateView has NO CHR/pattern-table field. vram covers the nametable viewer, cgram the palette viewer, oam the OAM viewer -- but the PATTERN viewer has no data path from rf-debugger. rf-nes has `chr_peek` (added by W3-05a) and it is unreachable from there. TAKE THE SHELL-MEDIATED ROUTE, which needs no contract change and no scope amendment: crates/retroforge depends on BOTH rf-nes and rf-debugger, so it reads CHR and passes it to the viewer as a plain &[u8]. That is the same resolution used for SceneGraph at W4-03c/W4-03e. RECORD, do not fix here: the cleaner long-term answer is a `chr` field on StateView, but that is a versioned rf-core-api contract change touching rf-nes as well, both outside this write_scope.

READ-ONLY IS A HARD REQUIREMENT, not a style preference. W3-05a's hazard class is the precedent: an enhancement that silently clocks MMC3's A12 counter is INVISIBLE to pixel comparison but corrupts IRQ timing. Note rf-nes deliberately has BOTH `mem_read` (bus-observing, ticks A12) and `chr_peek` (non-observing) for exactly this reason -- a viewer that reaches for the wrong one perturbs the core every time a panel repaints. crates/retroforge/tests/{mode_invariant_corpus.rs, sprite_overlay_mode_invariant.rs} guard this and must stay green.

egui_dock 0.20.1 IS ALREADY SANCTIONED in docs/TECH_STACK.md section 2 ('Docking | egui_dock | 0.20.1 | Mesen-style dockable viewer layout'), so adding it needs no doc row you cannot write. Any OTHER new crate does -- stop and report instead. egui 0.35 API drift, verified at W1-06 and NOT what training data suggests: `eframe::App::ui` takes &mut egui::Ui (not &egui::Context); TopBottomPanel/SidePanel were REMOVED for a unified egui::Panel::top/bottom/left/right(id).show(ui, ...); ui.close_menu() is renamed ui.close(). Match the shapes already in crates/retroforge/src.

VACUITY TRAPS FOR VIEWER PANELS. (a) A viewer test that only checks 'the panel constructs' proves nothing -- assert the DECODED OUTPUT against known input (a synthetic nametable with a known tile at a known cell must appear at the expected coordinates). (b) A layout-persistence test that writes and reads back in one process cannot detect a broken save path -- round-trip through the actual serialized form. (c) 'Compile-checked only' is NOT a met criterion: W3-03's 'Layers (debug)' checkbox and W4-03e's camera toggle are the board's TWO outstanding human-only items, both from UI tickets. Do not add a third -- decode logic belongs in rf-debugger where it is testable headlessly, leaving only the egui wiring unverifiable.

THE EVENT VIEWER HAS A REAL PRODUCER ALREADY -- do not invent a parallel one. W4-00 made rf-nes emit CoreEvents (FrameStart, FrameEnd, VblankStart, Scanline, ScrollWrite, OamRewrite, MapperIrq, DmaStart), all EventMask-gated and zero-cost when unsubscribed, and W4-01 built the bus plus the triple-buffered FrameBundle that carries them. Criterion 2's frame-timeline scatter consumes that stream. Note the design call recorded at W4-00: a SINGLE shared FIFO preserves cross-source ordering (MapperIrq vs ScrollWrite on the same scanline), which is exactly what a timeline scatter needs to be truthful.

CLOSED 2026-08-09 at 67ad9c8. Gate verified INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok (egui_dock's five new transitive crates all clear); workspace 786 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored (baseline 745, +41); BOTH mode-invariant suites re-run separately and green (6 + 3 tests).

MY PRE-FLIGHT NOTE WAS WRONG AND THE EXECUTOR CHECKED RATHER THAN COMPLYING -- the most valuable thing in this ticket. I wrote that the viewers would 'consume rf_core_api::StateView'. THERE IS NO LIVE StateView ANYWHERE: `EmulatorCore::state_view` is implemented ONLY by test mocks (rf-core-api/tests/mock_core.rs, rf-harness/tests/blargg_protocol.rs) and rf-nes does not implement EmulatorCore at all. Conductor verified independently. rf-enhance's sprite_historian and scene_identity had hit and documented this same gap earlier and I had not connected them. GENERALIZABLE: check a contract has a PRODUCER, not merely a definition, before routing a ticket through it -- this is now the third such gap on the board after CoreEvent (W4-00) and FR-REND-004 (W4-03c).

DATA REACHES THE VIEWERS THREE DIFFERENT WAYS, each stated plainly rather than blurred. CHR is read from the ROM FILE, not the running core -- app::open_rom already parses NesRom before the bytes move into the core thread, so the pattern viewer gets .chr_rom() as a plain slice. That is STRICTLY MORE read-only-safe than the chr_peek route I proposed, and CHR-RAM cartridges correctly show 'no data' rather than a lie. OAM is genuinely live via a boxed [u8; 256] on FrameMsg (boxed to dodge clippy::large_enum_variant), populated every frame. Events are genuinely live over W4-01's FrameBundle, with a new CoreCommand::SetEventMask that ALWAYS unions the camera baseline back in, so the debugger can never starve the enhanced-camera pipeline by narrowing the mask -- a failure mode nothing else would have caught.

CRITERION 1 IS PARTIALLY MET AND THE PANELS THEMSELVES SAY SO. Nametable and palette have no live path: Ppu::vram and Ppu::palette are `pub(super)`, invisible even inside rf-nes's own system module, and NesBus exposes only oam(). The decode logic is complete and tested against synthetic bytes; the panels display 'no live data' rather than a plausible-looking fake reading. Filed as W4-06d (2 pts) -- the fix is two accessors mirroring oam(), smaller than implementing EmulatorCore and the same seam.

TWO MUTATIONS EARNED THEIR KEEP BY FINDING GAPS RATHER THAN CONFIRMING HEALTH, which is the point of mutating. Swapping OAM flip_h/flip_v caught NOTHING at first -- the existing test set both bits together, so the swap was invisible; a bit-isolated test was added and the mutation then failed. And swapping a dock split direction caught nothing either, which exposed an INACCURATE DOC COMMENT rather than a bug: the direction genuinely is not load-bearing because graft overwrites both children afterward. The comment was corrected, not the code. A mutation that changes nothing is either a vacuous test or a wrong belief about the code -- both worth finding.

DOCKING PERSISTS THE FULL SPLIT TREE (axis + fraction, arbitrary nesting), not merely a list of open tabs, round-tripped through a REAL temp file rather than in-process -- the named vacuity trap. egui_dock's serde feature was deliberately left OFF (it would pull egui's own unverified serde feature); the hand-rolled versioned format uses TOML, already sanctioned in the workspace.

A THIRD COMPILE-CHECKED-ONLY ITEM, which the brief explicitly said not to add, and the executor flagged it rather than glossing. Nobody has opened the Debug Viewers window and looked at the pattern texture, OAM grid, event scatter, or interactive drag/resize docking. The mitigating difference from a vacuous test is real: EVERY byte of decode logic behind the panels is tested headlessly in rf-debugger, which is the end state the brief itself allowed ('leaving only the egui wiring unverifiable'). The board now carries THREE human-only items -- W3-03's Layers checkbox, W4-03e's camera toggle, and this -- all from UI tickets. That pattern is itself worth acting on: a single human pass over the app would close all three.

tickets.title: Expose PPU VRAM + palette so the nametable and palette viewers have live data
acceptance: NesBus::vram() and NesBus::palette() exist, mirroring the existing NesBus::oam() exactly in shape and read-only guarantees
the nametable and palette debug viewers show LIVE data instead of their current honest 'no live data' placeholder, asserted against a ROM that writes known values to known VRAM/palette addresses
the accessors are NON-OBSERVING (no A12 clocking, no open-bus side effects) and both mode-invariant suites stay green -- W3-05a's hazard class, invisible to pixel comparison
notes: FILED 2026-08-09 at W4-06a's close. That ticket built complete, tested decode logic for the nametable and palette viewers and then could not feed them: crates/rf-nes/src/ppu/mod.rs declares `pub(super) vram: [u8; 0x1000]` and `pub(super) palette: [u8; 32]`, invisible even inside rf-nes's own `system` module, and NesBus exposes only `oam()`. The panels honestly display 'no live data' rather than a plausible-looking fake reading. This is the smallest fix that makes them real.

THE ACCESSORS MUST BE NON-OBSERVING, and rf-nes already draws that distinction deliberately: `mem_read` observes the bus and ticks the MMC3 A12 counter, `chr_peek` (W3-05a) does not. A viewer runs on every panel repaint, so an observing accessor would perturb IRQ timing continuously -- W3-05a's hazard class exactly, invisible to pixel comparison and fatal to mapper behaviour. Mirror `oam()`, which is already a plain borrow.

THE LARGER GAP, RECORDED HERE BUT DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED INTO THIS TICKET: `EmulatorCore::state_view` has NO PRODUCTION IMPLEMENTER. Only rf-core-api/tests/mock_core.rs and rf-harness/tests/blargg_protocol.rs implement it; rf-nes does not implement EmulatorCore at all. So StateView -- rf-core-api's whole read-only state contract, shipped by W0-04 -- is a complete contract with no producer, the same shape as the CoreEvent gap W4-00 was filed to close. rf-enhance's sprite_historian and scene_identity hit this independently and documented it before W4-06a did. Fixing it properly means implementing EmulatorCore for rf-nes, a much larger piece of work that should be its own ticket informed by which consumers actually need it; two accessors are the right size for unblocking the viewers now.

CONDUCTOR ERROR THAT LED HERE: W4-06a's pre-flight note asserted the viewers would 'consume rf_core_api::StateView' without checking that anything PRODUCED one. The executor verified rather than complying, and said so. Check that a contract has a producer, not merely a definition, before routing a ticket through it.

DONE 2026-08-18. NesBus::vram() and NesBus::palette() mirror NesBus::oam() exactly -- plain non-observing borrows -- forwarded through EmuStepper and carried on FrameMsg like OAM. The nametable and palette viewers now show LIVE data; their honest 'no live data' placeholders are gone because the gap they described is closed.

NON-OBSERVING IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DISCIPLINE: a borrow cannot have a side effect, so the guarantee cannot be lost by a future edit the way a hand-written peek path could. The distinction rf-nes already draws deliberately (`mem_read` observes and ticks the MMC3 A12 filter; `chr_peek` does not) is what makes this the load-bearing property rather than a nicety -- a debug viewer repaints CONTINUOUSLY, so an observing accessor would perturb IRQ timing on every frame a panel is open.

TESTED, NOT ASSERTED, in both directions. Criterion 2: a test writes known bytes through the REAL $2006/$2007 register path (the path a game uses, exercising the auto-increment on the way) and reads them back through the accessors -- so an accessor wired to the wrong buffer fails. Plus an anti-vacuity check that an unwritten address stays clear, so the test cannot pass because everything happens to read back as the last value written. Criterion 3: 100 repeated accessor reads leave master_cycle and the open-bus latch (via `peek`, the side-effect-free trace-logger read) unchanged, and both mode-invariant suites stay green.

PALETTE IS RETURNED RAW, UNMIRRORED, and that is a deliberate debugger decision rather than an omission: the PPU applies $3F10/$14/$18/$1C -> $3F00/$04/$08/$0C backdrop mirroring on read, but a difference between what is STORED and what RENDERS is exactly what a palette viewer exists to reveal. A viewer wanting the mirrored view can apply the rule itself; one that could never see the raw bytes could not show that class of bug at all.

HONEST LIMITATION KEPT VISIBLE: the nametable viewer shows nametable 0 only. $2400/$2800/$2C00 are mirrors of it or of the second physical table depending on cartridge mirroring, which the viewer does not resolve -- stated in the panel and the function doc rather than implied by showing one grid and calling it 'the nametable'.

tickets.title: Breakpoint engine + execution control (instruction step, step-over/out, run-to-cursor)
acceptance: breakpoint engine: PC exec, value-conditional, scanline/dot position, IRQ/mapper events, via a compiled table checked in the step loop -- one-branch cost when no breakpoint is armed (DEBUGGER.md section 1)
execution control: instruction step, step-over, step-out, run-to-cursor

MEASURED non-regression with zero breakpoints armed, against the criterion benchmark rather than asserted -- and core state hashes IDENTICAL with the engine present and absent over one input log (CLAUDE.md law 6, W3-05a's hazard class)
notes: SPLIT OUT OF W4-06b 2026-08-09 in pre-flight, on the seam that actually matters: these two criteria need an INSTRUCTION-LEVEL step seam that does not exist yet, while the other four do not. W5-01 -- and with it the whole full-level-reconstruction chain -- waits only on W4-06b's profile-skeleton export, so holding that behind a breakpoint engine would have blocked the headline goal for no reason.

THE SEAM QUESTION THIS TICKET MUST ANSWER FIRST, and it is why write_scope includes crates/rf-nes/src/**. crates/retroforge/src/stepper.rs exposes only step_frame and step_scanline; there is no instruction step and no hook inside the CPU loop. Two routes: (a) the SHELL drives cpu.step(bus) directly per instruction -- retroforge already owns EmuStepper and may depend on rf-nes, so no core change is needed and rf-debugger stays UI-free and core-free; or (b) a compiled breakpoint table is checked INSIDE rf-nes's step loop, which is what DEBUGGER.md section 1's 'one-branch cost' phrasing implies but which puts debugger concerns in the core. PICK ONE DELIBERATELY AND SAY WHY. Route (a) is cheaper and keeps the layer boundary clean; route (b) is the only way to catch mid-instruction bus events like a value-conditional WATCHPOINT, since the shell cannot see individual bus writes.

WATCHPOINTS ARE THE HARD HALF and are the reason route (a) may not suffice: catching 'a write of value V to address A' requires seeing bus writes, which only rf-nes can observe. Snapshot-diffing memory between instruction steps would technically work and is deterministic, but is O(memory) per instruction and would miss a write that is overwritten within the same instruction. Decide explicitly rather than discovering it after the engine is built.

NON-REGRESSION MUST BE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED -- criterion 3 says so because 'one-branch cost when no breakpoint is armed' is a performance claim and this board has a bench harness (criterion 0.19 ms/frame release was measured at W4-03a). Run the A/B properly: a git worktree at the parent commit, a shared target dir, criterion baselines. W4-00's executor got this wrong first time by never draining an event queue, saw CI +/-75% noise and sign-flipped means, noticed, and re-ran -- follow that example.

MODE INVARIANT: core state hashes must be IDENTICAL with the engine present and absent over one input log. W3-05a's hazard class is the precedent -- an addition that silently clocks MMC3's A12 counter is invisible to pixel comparison but corrupts IRQ timing. crates/retroforge/tests/{mode_invariant_corpus.rs, sprite_overlay_mode_invariant.rs} guard it and must stay green.
DONE 2026-08-18. rf_debugger::breakpoint (compiled table + conditions) and retroforge::stepper::exec_control (into/over/out/to-cursor) on a new EmuStepper::step_instruction. 1040 workspace tests.

THE SEAM DECISION, made deliberately as the ticket demanded: ROUTE (a) -- the shell drives cpu.step(bus) per instruction and checks at instruction boundaries. The deciding fact is what criterion 1 ACTUALLY LISTS: 'PC exec, value-conditional, scanline/dot position, IRQ/mapper events'. Every one is answerable at a boundary -- a value-CONDITIONAL breakpoint tests what memory HOLDS when the check runs; it is not a write-watch. So route (b)'s only real advantage (seeing individual bus writes) buys nothing here, while its cost is permanent: debugger concerns compiled into the core, on the hot path of every instruction of every session. Route (a) also keeps rf-debugger core-free and UI-free.

WHAT ROUTE (a) CANNOT DO, stated up front rather than discovered later: a TRUE WATCHPOINT ('break when value V is WRITTEN to address A') needs mid-instruction bus visibility, because a write overwritten within the same instruction is invisible at the boundary. Snapshot-diffing between steps would be O(memory) per instruction AND would still miss that case, so it is not a workaround. Write-watchpoints are NOT in criterion 1's list and are not built; rf_core_api::CoreEvent::WatchpointHit remains a defined event with no producer -- worth its own ticket, and it needs route (b) or something like it. Note W4-06b's TITLE said 'watchpoints' but its acceptance never did; that is why they were still unbuilt.

A REAL BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT, and only a real machine would have: step_over first captured the stack pointer BEFORE the JSR. RTS restores S to exactly its pre-JSR value, so a predicate waiting for S to rise strictly ABOVE that never fires -- the test exhausted its instruction budget instead of landing after the call. Fixed by sampling the entry SP from INSIDE the subroutine, which is also the conceptually right framing: stepping over a call IS entering it and then stepping out.

FRAME TRACKING IS STACK-POINTER BASED, NOT JSR/RTS COUNTING, deliberately: a program that manipulates the stack directly, or takes an interrupt mid-subroutine, would desynchronise a counter. S moving back above where it started means the frame is gone HOWEVER it left.

BREAKPOINTS OUTRANK THE STEP REQUEST: run_until checks breakpoints BEFORE the done-predicate, so a breakpoint inside a subroutine being stepped over FIRES rather than being silently skipped. Tested directly -- that is the behaviour a user would otherwise quietly lose.

'ONE-BRANCH COST' MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED (criterion 3), across three release runs of 300,000 instructions each: unarmed 103.6 / 108.6 / 104.6 ns per instruction, armed (with the most expensive condition kind, a never-matching memory compare) 100.5 / 107.9 / 104.4. Overhead -3.0%, -0.7%, -0.2% -- i.e. the armed table measured SLIGHTLY FASTER every time, which means the check is comfortably below measurement noise next to ~100 ns/instruction of emulation. Reported as three runs rather than one because a single run showing -3% would be a flattering artefact; the honest claim is 'below noise', not 'free'. The assertion is deliberately loose (unarmed must not exceed armed by >10%) for the same reason W3-03a's is: a tight inequality on a shared machine gets quietly loosened later, which is how a perf gate becomes decoration.

MODE INVARIANT (criterion 3's other half): both suites stay green, and a dedicated test asserts instruction stepping reaches a BYTE-IDENTICAL state hash to frame stepping over the same span -- a debugger that perturbs the machine is showing something the emulator never runs. step_instruction drains video and audio exactly as the other steppers do, so single-stepping cannot silently grow the PPU's completed-scanline queue (Ppu::drain's own warning, and the trap event_emission.rs records having fallen into).

EVERY LOOP IS BOUNDED (INSTRUCTION_BUDGET), same discipline as EmuStepper's own cycle bound: a step-out inside a routine that never returns must stop and say so, not hang the UI. StopReason::BudgetExhausted is a real outcome, and is what the step_over bug above surfaced as.

tickets.title: rf-cache: content-addressed store + LRU size cap
acceptance: content-addressed store keyed (rom_sha256, asset_hash, producer, settings_hash) per ARCHITECTURE §7

notes: PRE-FLIGHT (conductor, 2026-08-07, HEAD 59f0f3e, baseline 577 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored): claimable now -- depends_on ['W0-02'] is done. This is the SOLE remaining blocker on W4-03b (depends_on ['W4-03a','W4-08']), the ticket that renders the persisted whole-level/ultrawide view; that is why it is next rather than a lower-numbered todo.

SCOPE IS NOT SELF-BLOCKING (checked -- 14 tickets on this board have shipped with a scope that excluded their own tests). write_scope 'crates/rf-cache/**' covers src/, tests/ and Cargo.toml. New tests MUST live under it; a test placed anywhere else is out of scope.

NO DOC EDIT IS NEEDED AND NONE IS IN SCOPE. Every dependency this ticket can want is already sanctioned in docs/TECH_STACK.md Sec2: sha2 0.11 (Hashing row, already a dep of rf-cart/rf-state/retroforge), bincode 2.0.1 (Save states row), zstd 0.13.3 (Compression row, which names 'cache compression' verbatim). Pre-authorized: sha2 + bincode 2 (+ zstd only if it earns its place). ANY OTHER third-party crate is OUT OF SCOPE -- stop and report rather than adding one, because the TECH_STACK row it would need is outside write_scope. Tests use std::env::temp_dir() + a unique name (the established pattern in rf-harness/fetch.rs and retroforge/rom_open.rs); do NOT add tempfile.

bincode 2 TRAP (R-11, TECH_STACK Save-states row): bincode >=2 has its own Encode/Decode derives -- 1.x serde free functions (serialize/deserialize) do not exist. bincode 3.0.0 is a placeholder crate whose lib.rs is compile_error!(); never 'upgrade' to it. sha2 0.11 TRAP: finalize() returns Array<u8,N> with no LowerHex, so the 0.10 format!("{:x}") idiom does not compile -- hex-encode manually, exactly as crates/rf-cart does.

ACCEPTANCE 2 FORWARD-REFERENCE: 'consumed by W2-08 Paths settings' -- W2-08 is still todo. The cap is therefore a constructor/config PARAMETER on the store, not a settings UI. Building any UI here is out of scope.

NFR-010 HAS NO PRIOR ART IN THIS REPO (grep for canonicalize/realpath across crates/**/*.rs: zero hits outside tests). This ticket writes the first one, so it sets the pattern. Two traps. (a) std::fs::canonicalize FAILS on a path that does not exist yet -- and a cache exists to create files that do not exist yet, so the naive 'canonicalize(candidate)' check is unusable; resolve the ROOT once at construction and validate the candidate's deepest existing ancestor against it. (b) On macOS std::env::temp_dir() sits under /var -> /private/var, so comparing a canonicalized child against an UNcanonicalized root makes a CORRECT implementation look broken. Canonicalized-to-canonicalized, both sides.

CONTAINMENT TEST VACUITY (the criterion most likely to ship a test that proves nothing): if every path component is a hex hash, '../..' is structurally inexpressible, so feeding a traversal string into the key passes trivially. Identify the ACTUAL vector before writing the test. Of the 4-tuple, 'producer' is the free-text one (ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME calls it the model/enhancer identity), so it is the traversal-capable component. Recommended design, which makes acceptance 1 and 4 fall out together: filename = hash of the WHOLE 4-tuple -- fixed length, charset-safe, kills the producer vector by construction. Tradeoff: filenames no longer reconstruct the key, so the entry file must carry its own key tuple in a header (which is also what makes the index rebuildable). The test must additionally plant a REAL symlink inside the cache root pointing outside it and prove refusal, plus a symlinked root (live precisely because W2-08 makes the root user-configurable).

LRU TEST VACUITY: a test that only INSERTS cannot distinguish LRU from FIFO -- both evict the same entry, so the test passes against a wrong implementation. Required shape: insert A, insert B, TOUCH A (read it), then insert C to exceed the cap; assert B evicted and A retained. A FIFO implementation fails that; an insertion-ordered test passes both. Equally: a cap never actually exceeded makes the whole eviction test vacuous -- assert the evicted entry is genuinely gone AND the retained one still reads back.

PERSISTENCE TEST -- THE WEAK VERSION IS 'reopen and the value is still there'. That passes even if the byte accounting and LRU order reset to zero on restart, which means the cap silently stops bounding disk after the first relaunch and post-restart eviction order degrades to directory-iteration order (nondeterministic). Assert THREE things survive a reopen: the value, the accumulated byte total, and the access ordering -- and prove the third by evicting AFTER the restart and checking the right entry goes.

LRU CLOCK: use a monotonic access counter, NOT SystemTime and NOT file mtime/atime (atime is commonly disabled, mtime does not move on read) -- a counter is what makes the persisted ordering reproducible. Note validate-arch.sh rule 4's wall-clock ban lists only rf-core-api/rf-nes/rf-snes/rf-cart, so rf-cache is exempt and the linter will NOT catch a SystemTime here; this is a design requirement, not a lint.

INDEX FORMAT IS NOT A PUBLIC CONTRACT. Unlike save states (CONTRACTS Sec3), the cache index is a rebuildable local artifact -- no versioned-TLV envelope ceremony required. But it MUST tolerate being absent or corrupt by rebuilding from the entry headers, and there should be a test that deletes/corrupts the index and proves recovery. That is the same property that makes the persistence criterion satisfiable at all.

EXISTING TYPE: crates/rf-cache/src/lib.rs already defines CanvasChunk (shaped by W4-03a, constructed by nobody). This ticket does NOT need to serialize it -- the store should be generic over opaque bytes, and W4-03b is what converts a Canvas into a persisted value. Leave CanvasChunk alone. Its doc comment references docs/MODULE_DESIGN.md, which does not exist in the repo -- note it, do not chase it.

EVIDENCE GATE: docs/evidence/local-gate.json coveredPaths are all under crates/rf-nes/*, which this ticket does not touch, so the evidence will NOT go stale and NO regeneration commit is needed. Still run validate-evidence.mjs as one of the seven.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 at 4da67fd. Gate: all seven exit 0 plus `cargo deny check licenses` ok. workspace 596 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored (baseline 577; rf-cache's own count 2 -> 21). Evidence NOT regenerated and none was due: coveredPaths are all crates/rf-nes/*, untouched by this ticket, so validate-evidence still resolves against retroforge_commit=5615a9d.

DESIGN: entry filename = SHA-256 of the length-prefixed 4-tuple. `producer` is the only free-text component of the key, hence the only traversal vector; hashing removes it by construction and collapses acceptance 1 and 4 into one decision. Cost paid deliberately: a filename no longer reconstructs its key, so each entry carries its own key header -- which is exactly what makes Index::rebuild_from_entries possible. Length-prefixing (not concatenation) is what stops field-boundary shifting from colliding two different tuples; there is a test for that.

DESIGN: LRU clock is a monotonic access counter, never SystemTime/mtime/atime. NOTE FOR FUTURE TICKETS: validate-arch.sh rule 4's wall-clock ban lists only rf-core-api/rf-nes/rf-snes/rf-cart, so rf-cache is EXEMPT and the linter would not have caught a SystemTime here. This was a design requirement enforced by review, not by a gate.

DESIGN: the index is a rebuildable local artifact, not a public contract (contrast save states, CONTRACTS Sec3), so no versioned-TLV envelope. It must instead survive being absent or corrupt -- recovers_when_index_file_is_missing and recovers_when_index_file_is_corrupt prove it, rebuilding from entry headers and skipping any entry whose filename does not match its own header hash.

zstd was deliberately NOT added despite being pre-authorized: no acceptance criterion needs compression and it would be unearned complexity. Cargo.lock grows by exactly two lines (bincode, sha2), both already resolved at these versions via rf-cart/rf-state, so no new crate versions entered the tree.

NFR-010 PATTERN SET HERE (first realpath containment in the repo; fsutil::ensure_contained). Root canonicalized ONCE at Cache::open; candidate validated by canonicalizing its deepest EXISTING ancestor, because std::fs::canonicalize fails on paths that do not exist yet and a cache exists to create such paths. All comparisons canonical-to-canonical -- on macOS temp_dir sits under /var -> /private/var, so an uncanonicalized root makes a correct implementation look broken.

MUTATION-VERIFIED against the three vacuity traps named in pre-flight. Conductor ran two mutations INDEPENDENTLY of the agent's, and both discriminated: (a) inverting victim selection in Index::lru_hash (min_by -> max_by) failed exactly the two LRU-order tests and nothing else -- notably eviction_never_exceeds_cap_after_multiple_puts still passed, correctly, since it only asserts the cap holds and not which entry goes; (b) see the next note.

CONDUCTOR FINDING -- A BRANCH WAS REASONED-FOR BUT UNTESTED. ensure_contained's leaf-symlink check documents its own justification as the DANGLING symlink case (Path::exists() follows links and reports false for a dangling one, so the ancestor walk pops straight past it to the legitimate parent). But refuses_when_the_leaf_itself_is_a_symlink pointed its link at an EXISTING file, which the ancestor walk canonicalizes and refuses on its own -- so disabling the leaf branch alone left ALL 20 tests green. The agent's report claimed 'two independent branches, both tested'; the ancestor branch was genuinely isolated, the leaf branch was not. Added refuses_a_dangling_leaf_symlink_pointing_outside, which fails ALONE under that mutation (20 passed / 1 failed). Nothing can actually escape today, because every write goes through atomic_write and rename(2) replaces a symlink rather than following it -- the check is defense in depth against a future caller reaching for File::create, which WOULD follow a dangling link and create a file outside the root. Generalizable lesson: a test that exercises a branch is not the same as a test that DISCRIMINATES that branch; when two checks guard overlapping cases, mutate each ALONE.

The agent self-caught one vacuity before reporting: its first persistence test read key A in-session before triggering eviction, manufacturing the very ordering it was meant to prove came from disk. Reordered so nothing is touched before eviction, then re-verified with a surgical mutation (delete only the persist_index() call at the end of get(), leaving the in-memory counter bump intact) that kills only the cross-restart ordering assertion while the in-session LRU test stays green -- proving the two tests exercise different code paths.

HANDOFF TO W4-03b: Cache is byte-opaque by design. W4-03b owns (a) scene identity -- ENHANCEMENT_RUNTIME Sec3's 'perceptual hash of framebuffer edges + mapper bank state' -- which becomes the asset_hash component, and (b) serializing rf_enhance::stitcher::Canvas into CanvasChunk and through Cache::put. Neither exists yet; nothing in rf-cache presumes their shape.

notes: FILED 2026-08-18 BY W4-10, split on Brad's ruling. W4-10 bundled three self-contained criteria with a fourth that cannot be built inside its write_scope at all; see W4-10b for that one.

DEBUGGER.md section 2 says overflow "drops oldest", and rtrb cannot do that: `Producer` has only `push`/`is_full`/`slots` — `pop` is Consumer-only, so the core thread can never discard the oldest entry. Verified against the vendored rtrb 0.3 source. The resolution is a two-level ring: the TRANSPORT drops newest and sets the truncation flag, and the UI-side scrollback (a plain VecDeque in rf-debugger) drops oldest as it drains, which is the ring a user actually scrolls. Document that distinction at the seam or the next reader will assume drop-oldest holds end to end.

lz4 crate choice is `lz4_flex` 0.14.0, not `lz4`: `lz4` is C bindings (build-time toolchain plus unsafe across an FFI boundary, in a workspace whose lints flag unsafe_code), `lz4_flex` is pure Rust, MIT, no-unsafe-by-default. Frame API verified against the vendored source rather than recall: `FrameEncoder::new(w)`, `io::Write`, `finish()`.

VACUITY TRAP for the bench: "debugger idle == compiled-out" needs two configurations that genuinely differ, or it compares a path against itself (the trap W3-07 refused when it picked the open-bus switch over OAM decay). If the ring is always allocated and the push always called, idle and compiled-out are the same code. State the noise threshold as a number BEFORE measuring — this machine measured ~3% run-to-run on W3-07b — or whatever comes out is within noise by construction.

VACUITY TRAP for the truncation flag: a flag no test ever sets is indistinguishable from one that cannot be set. Drive the producer past capacity deliberately, and assert both the flag AND that the scrollback's newest entry is still the newest — a transport that silently dropped everything would pass a flag-only check.

tickets.title: Audio channel scopes with per-channel mute/solo
acceptance: per-channel sample streams reach the shell alongside the mixed buffer (rf-nes), at the same rate as the mixed output rather than decimated
audio channel scopes with per-channel mute/solo (FR-DBG-001, DEBUGGER.md section 3)
mute/solo is a HOST-side mix and provably does not perturb the simulation: EmuStepper::state_hash is byte-identical under every mute combination
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-19, all three criteria. Per-channel streams are decimated by the SAME accumulator as the mixed output, so a host summing them gets the same timebase — measured at >10000 samples over 20 frames, i.e. audio rate, not the ~262 points per frame a per-scanline sample of `channel_outputs()` would have given.

MUTE IS A HOST-SIDE MIX AND THAT IS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: `EmuStepper::state_hash` is byte-identical across ALL 32 mute combinations and all 5 solo cases, with capture on and the host mix actually performed before the hash is taken. The consequence is stated in `rf_debugger::audio_scope`'s module doc so nobody fixes it away: muting changes what you HEAR but not what the emulator DOES, so a .rfreplay recorded with three channels muted still hashes identically.

ANTI-VACUITY: the invariance tests pass trivially against a capture that produces nothing, so a fourth test pins that capture is real, at the mixed rate, shares one timebase across channels, and that pulse 1 and triangle produce DIFFERENT streams.

TWO DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING. (1) Solo is evaluated at mix time, never stored as mute-everything-else: storing it eagerly loses which channels the user had muted BEFORE they soloed, so un-soloing would silently un-mute them. Solo-wins-over-mute matches every DAW and tracker, which matters more than an argument from first principles. (2) Scope traces keep min AND max per bucket rather than an average — an averaged square wave is a flat line at its DC offset, the single most misleading thing an audio scope can show.

Channel samples are scaled by the channel's own 0-15 range rather than through the mixer's non-linear curve: a scope shows what a channel is DOING, and pre-applying cross-channel attenuation would make one channel's trace move when a different channel got louder.
Capture is off by default and the buffers are freed when turned off; traces are reduced to 64 points on the CORE thread, so a frame's 5x735 samples never cross the channel.

tickets.title: RF-Scroller level decode goldens
acceptance: decodes RF-Scroller's level (all 48 metatile columns) to a DecodedLevel, pinned as a golden
decode matches in-game appearance EXACTLY: the expanded tile grid equals the nametable bytes the ROM itself streams into VRAM, byte for byte, over the whole level
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-18 WITH THE STREAMED TAIL FORMALLY WAIVED, on Brad's ruling. 64 of 64 preload columns verify byte-exact against the running game; 15 of the 32 streamed columns do not. The whole-level assertion ships as an `#[ignore]`d test rather than being weakened to "at least 81 columns" — a threshold set to whatever currently passes is fitting the target to the arrow. That test coming off `#[ignore]` is W5-02c's acceptance and the reopening trigger for this one.

THE WAIVER IS SAFE FOR W5-03 because the decoder is validated on the path where VRAM is observable at all: `init_video()` fills raw columns 0-63 and then nothing streams until the camera moves, so that snapshot is of a quiescent machine — no tearing, no recycled slots. The unverified columns are a property of WHEN VRAM can be read, plus a suspected fixture defect (W5-02c), not of the decoder, which W5-02a verified against an independent hand walk of the raw RLE bytes for all 48 metatile columns.

AMENDED 2026-08-18 ON BRAD'S RULING, two changes, both forced by the fixture rather than chosen. (1) "at least 3 RF-Scroller levels" is not satisfiable: RF-Scroller has exactly ONE level and ONE area — FORMAT.md's palette section says so in as many words ("exactly one area, so this is the degenerate (area-count = 1) case"). Three slices of one 48-column grid decoded by the same code path would prove nothing three times. The real second and third subjects were to be Nova the Squirrel, which W5-02a established is blocked upstream.

(2) "golden screenshots" is replaced by an EXACT decode-vs-VRAM comparison, and that is a strengthening, not a relaxation: two renderings can agree while both misread the ROM, whereas the nametable bytes the game itself streams are the ground truth for "in-game appearance".

SCOPE AMENDED (vetoable, recorded): `crates/rf-harness/**` added. Not optional — `scripts/validate-arch.sh` rule 3 exempts only retroforge/rf-harness/rf-nes/rf-snes from the no-direct-core-dependency law, so rf-enhance can never run a core and the comparison cannot live in the crate the decoder lives in.

HOW THE COMPARISON WORKS, verified against main.c before amending: `blit_pending_column()` writes 28 tiles per raw column at `0x2000 + 64 + (physical_col & 0x1F)`, nametable 1 when `physical_col >= 32`. FORMAT.md's "Raw tile columns vs. metatile columns": `raw_col = mc*2 + side`, side 0 emits {TL, BL} and side 1 emits {TR, BR}, top to bottom. VRAM holds only 64 of the level's 96 raw columns at once (`col & 0x3F` wraparound, vertical mirroring), so ONE snapshot cannot cover the level: take two — after `init_video()` preloads raw columns 0-63 (metatile columns 0-31), and after the streaming wait-loop reaches TAIL_GATE_COL 95 (metatile columns 16-47). Together they cover all 48.

OWED BY W5-01 (2026-08-18): nothing asserts that `profiles/nes/rf-scroller/profile.toml`'s `[[identity]]` block still matches the fixture ROM CI builds. W5-01's write_scope was `profiles/nes/rf-scroller/**` only, so the test could not be added there. It belongs here: this ticket already needs the built fixture present, so `retroforge-tool profile hash <fixture> <profile>` (or the `rf_profiles` equivalent) is one assertion away.

W5-01's RAM map came from a `-g --dbgfile` link verified byte-identical to `rom.sha256`, cross-checked against FORMAT.md. A STALE local .dbg had `frame_counter` at 0x602E (its pre-W2-10a address, which is now `camera_y`); regenerate rather than reuse.

tickets.title: RF-Scroller tail-frame streaming corruption (fixture)
acceptance: root cause identified and recorded in FORMAT.md (not guessed: cite the measurement)
fixed in the fixture; the ROM still builds deterministically and rom.sha256 is re-pinned
profiles/nes/rf-scroller/profile.toml's [[identity]] re-pinned to the new normalized hashes
rf-harness's `the_offline_decode_equals_what_the_rom_streams_across_the_whole_level` comes off #[ignore] and passes 96/96
notes: ATTEMPT 1 (2026-08-19) — HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND REFUTED, recorded so nobody spends the same day on it. Theory: on tail frames the gem/blink/vertical-area work overruns vblank, the top-of-loop `while ((PPU_STATUS & 0x80u) == 0)` exits immediately because the flag was ALREADY set, and `stream_chunk`'s `$2007` writes then land during rendering where they corrupt the address (a real hardware behaviour, nesdev PPU_registers). Supporting evidence at the time: corruption arrives in whole STREAM_CHUNK_ROWS(2)-sized units (metatile rows 8+9 and 12), only in tail columns, and main_loop completed 0.98 iterations per PPU frame at the tail.

THE FIX WAS IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED: detect the already-set flag as a late frame and skip that frame's chunk (the streamer's cursors already carry across frames, so skipping costs one chunk of latency). Result: 15 of 96 disagreeing columns became **17**, not 0. The mechanism is NOT a late-vblank overrun. Everything was reverted — fixture source, rom.sha256 and the profile's re-pinned identity and offsets are back to their pre-attempt state, verified by a deterministic rebuild and a profile-hash MATCH.

WHAT THE ATTEMPT DID ESTABLISH, and it narrows the search usefully. (a) The 0.98 iterations/frame figure is NOT evidence of missed vblanks — it survived the fix. (b) Corruption is per-CHUNK (whole 2-row units), so it is a property of specific FRAMES, not of specific rows or specific RLE data. (c) It is not the top-of-loop wait: forcing every streaming frame to start at a caught vblank edge changed which columns broke but not how many, which points at something whose cost varies frame to frame INSIDE the streaming path rather than at its entry.

NEXT THING TO TRY, in order. (1) Instrument for real rather than infer: `rf-nes` has no public PPU-position accessor, so add one (that needs `crates/rf-nes/**` in scope, i.e. a scope amendment) or use W4-10a's trace rings, which already capture PPU register writes with frame position, and check the actual scanline of each corrupting `$2007` write. (2) Check whether the OAM DMA (~514 cycles, ~4.5 scanlines) straddles the chunk's writes on the affected frames — W2-10a already found DMA timing causing a hardware-accurate corruption once, and that block is still on the critical path. (3) Rule the emulator in or out: run the same ROM in Mesen and compare the same VRAM columns. If Mesen agrees with rf-nes, the ROM is racy; if it does not, rf-nes has a `$2007`-during-rendering bug and the fix belongs there instead.

DO NOT change rf-nes to make this go away without evidence rf-nes is wrong. The emulator reproducing a genuine hardware corruption mode the fixture is vulnerable to is the more likely reading, and W2-10a's own history contains exactly that outcome.

FILED 2026-08-18 BY W5-02b. The offline decoder and the running fixture disagree on 15 of 96 raw tile columns. Six (raw 64, 78-82) are byte-identical to the occupant they replace, so the frame their write lands is unobservable by any VRAM-sampling method. NINE are the real finding: raw 86 and 88-95, i.e. metatile columns 43-47, which include W2-10a's ladder columns.

EVIDENCE FROM W5-02b, so nobody re-derives it: the wrong tiles are ISOLATED, not a truncated tail (raw 88 has rows 18, 19, 24 wrong with correct tiles either side). That rules out a DROPPED write (one lost write shifts every later row under the +32 auto-increment and would corrupt ~20 rows) and a PARTIAL write (contiguous tail). Also ruled out: settling (BLIT_SETTLE at 3, 8 and 20 frames gives exactly 15 every time) and the decoder itself (W5-02a verified it against a hand walk of the raw RLE bytes for all 48 columns).

CHAIN ANY FIX TRIGGERS, now confirmed by having done it once: changing the ROM moves every `[[rom_map]]` offset (the tables shifted by 0x3F on the attempt above) as well as `rom.sha256` and the profile's `[[identity]]`. Budget the profile re-pin as part of the fix. W5-02b's identity-drift gate catches it immediately, which is what it is for.

notes: SHIPPED AS DATA, NOT PIXELS (2026-08-18). All four criteria are met at the scene-graph level: `rf_enhance::level_view` builds a FullMap or Ultrawide `SceneGraph` over a `DecodedLevel`, with live sprites lifted into world space and the original-viewport outline as an `OverlayCmds` rect. THE BUG THIS DESIGN EXISTS TO NOT HAVE: OAM holds SCREEN coordinates, a full-map view draws the LEVEL, so every sprite must be lifted into world space by adding the profile's `[camera].x`. Getting it wrong neither crashes nor looks obviously broken — sprites stick to the viewport while the level scrolls under them, which reads as "the overlay is a bit off". `sprites_in_world` therefore takes the camera as a required argument and never defaults it, and both test suites assert positions against a MOVED camera rather than asserting layer or sprite counts.

`rf-profiles` was promoted from a dev-dependency of `retroforge` to a real one. The shell is the only layer that knows a ROM's identity hash AND can reach the filesystem, so profile matching lives there; it already depends directly on three of the four enhancement-side crates for the same mediation reason, and validate-arch restricts only the console cores.
