tickets.title: Profile authoring loop: hot-reload + live decode preview
acceptance: profile TOML file-watch hot-reloads on save (E6-S2)
decode errors shown inline with ROM offsets
level preview panel re-renders immediately per FRONTEND_UI.md section 3.5
authoring walkthrough doc written end-to-end against RF-Scroller (annotate -> export -> decode -> validate -> golden), recording time-to-first-decoded-level (R-A2)
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-19, all four criteria. Criterion 4's walkthrough is `docs/AUTHORING.md`, and it is EXECUTED rather than described: `crates/retroforge/tests/authoring_walkthrough.rs` runs annotate -> export -> decode -> validate -> golden against the real fixture and prints the timings the doc quotes, so the doc cannot drift from the tool without a test failing.

R-A2 TIME TO FIRST DECODED LEVEL: 0.40 ms of machine time (annotate 0.001, export 0.058, decode 0.222, validate 0.109, golden 0.016). The doc states plainly what that EXCLUDES — finding the addresses in the debugger, and writing the `[decode]` section, which the exporter cannot infer from a list of addresses — because quoting a machine number as though it covered the whole loop would overstate the tool by orders of magnitude. What the number does say is that the loop is not the bottleneck: at sub-millisecond re-decode an author sees the result before their hand leaves the keyboard, which is the property hot-reload was built for.

SCOPE AMENDED 2026-08-19 ON BRAD'S RULING: `docs/**` added. Criterion 4 is a walkthrough DOC and there was nowhere in the original scope to put one; MASTER_PROMPT's always-writable set covers a STATUS.md line and a TECH_STACK row, not a new document. Recorded as vetoable.
HANDOFF 2026-08-19: criteria 1-3 are BUILT, GATED AND PUSHED; criterion 4 is blocked on write_scope and needs a ruling. Left `in_progress` deliberately rather than closed — three of four is not done.

WHAT IS DONE. (1) Hot-reload: `retroforge::authoring::Watch` polls (mtime, len) and re-decodes on change. (2) Decode errors inline with ROM offsets: `AuthoringError` carries the offset the author typed, rendered in hex like every other ROM address in this project, and a mistyped table address is tested end to end against the shipped profile. (3) Live preview: an Author window (FRONTEND_UI section 3.5's minimal Phase-4 form) showing errors first, then warnings, then a metatile-id grid; the test asserts the preview's CONTENT changes when the column table moves, not merely that a reload happened.

WHAT IS BLOCKED. Criterion 4 is a walkthrough DOC ('annotate -> export -> decode -> validate -> golden, recording time-to-first-decoded-level, R-A2'). It belongs under `docs/`, and this ticket's write_scope is `crates/retroforge/**`, `crates/rf-profiles/**`, `crates/rf-enhance/**`. MASTER_PROMPT's always-writable set covers plan.json status/notes, a one-line STATUS.md append, Cargo.lock and a TECH_STACK row — not a new doc. Amending scope to add `docs/**` is a one-line ruling; it was not taken unattended.

DESIGN DECISION WORTH KEEPING: mtime polling rather than the `notify` crate, and not merely to dodge a dependency. The shell already repaints continuously so one `stat` per repaint is below the noise floor of a frame that uploads a 240 KB texture; a watcher's callback arrives on its own thread at the OS's convenience, so testing one means sleeping (flaky) or mocking the watcher (testing the mock), whereas `Watch` is a pure function of two `fs::metadata` calls and its tests assert BOTH that it fires on a save and that it stays quiet otherwise — the half a watcher's tests usually skip. `notify` would also add per-OS backends, a TECH_STACK row and a `cargo deny` pass. The honest limit is recorded in the module doc: polling cannot see a change made and reverted between two polls, and compares (mtime, len) rather than content.

The Author control only appears when a profile actually claims the open ROM — a workspace with nothing to author against would be a control that does nothing. Polling is gated on the panel being open, so a session that never opens it does not stat a file at 60 Hz (DEBUGGER.md section 6's pay-for-use rule, applied one layer over).
